strategies.name: Box-vs-Treasury convenience-yield trade

legs.strike_rule: matched-maturity T-bill or SOFR future (notional = K2 - K1), or short bill repo

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat: (K2 - K1) from the box minus the bill repayment; P&L = (K2 - K1) * (e^{-r_bill T} - e^{-r_box T}) ~ (r_box - r_bill) * T * notional.
strategies.max_profit: The rate spread times maturity times notional, locked if both legs held to T.
strategies.max_loss: Mark-to-market if the spread widens before T (spread widened ~4x in 2008 per vBDG); negative if r_box < r_bill at entry.

greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho ~0 (rates hedged), exposed to box-bill basis

strategies.when_to_use: When the SPX box rate is above bills by more than its historical median (~40 bp per vBDG) and you can finance the bill short cheaply (institutions); for retail the practical version is simply holding boxes instead of bills (long-box entry).
strategies.risks: Basis risk between SPX box maturity and bill/SOFR future maturity; margin on two venues (CBOE/OCC and CME); the spread is a convenience yield that widens in stress exactly when margin is scarce; four-leg spread cost eats most of a 40 bp edge for maturities < 6 months.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin on the box (~0) plus CME SPAN on the rate future; requires cross-venue collateral.
strategies.crypto_notes: Crypto analogue: Deribit inverse box rate minus bill rate is the crypto dollar premium (hundreds of bp); the hedge leg would be a bill short or a USDC lending position; not the same convenience-yield phenomenon.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a (no European metals option boxes).
variants: Box vs SOFR futures strip
Box vs bills only at maturities > 6 months to amortise spread cost
Short box / long bill when r_box < r_bill (rare)
strategies.claim: The SPX box rate minus matched Treasury bill yield averages +25 to +60 bp and widens when VIX > 30 (positive correlation between daily spread changes and VIX changes), so the trade earns a stable carry with a stress-correlated drawdown.

trial.statistic: Mean of r_box - r_bill series; correlation of its daily change with VIX change.
trial.null: Mean spread <= 0 and correlation with VIX = 0.
trial.procedure: Build a daily SPX box-rate series from captured chains; join FRED bills and CBOE VIX; studentized block bootstrap of the mean and the correlation.
trial.data: Daily SPX chain capture (not available before 2026-10-14), FRED bills, VIX history.
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI for mean spread excludes 0 and lies within [15,80] bp; correlation with VIX changes > 0.2.
trial.controls: Use mid prices for the series, executable for the P&L; exclude expiries inside 30 DTE; check robustness to strike pair choice.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture, ~180 days, to form a box-rate series (alternative: ingest van Binsbergen-Diamond-Grotteria published box-rate data)
strategies.harness_suggestion: box.py daily series -> mandel/experiments/box_bill_spread.py joining FRED + VIX; bootstrap via existing block bootstrap.

strategies.name: Cash-and-carry with options (spot vs synthetic short / dated future)

legs.strike_rule: spot (BTC spot, IBIT, GLD, or stock)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat at K: you sold the forward at F_impl = K + (C - P) x (1 + rT) and own spot, earning basis = F_impl - S0 (the conversion viewed as a carry trade). Future version: replace the two options with a short dated future at F.
strategies.max_profit: Basis locked = F_impl - S0 - financing/storage/fees, certain if held to expiry and no funding leg.
strategies.max_loss: Negative basis at entry; mark-to-market if basis widens before T (margin call on the short leg while spot is unencumbered on another venue); custody/venue risk.
strategies.breakevens: F_impl = S0 x (1 + r T) (basis equals the risk-free rate).
strategies.when_to_use: Crypto: when annualised dated-futures or option-synthetic basis exceeds the T-bill rate by more than venue fees plus a risk premium (it was ~5.4%/yr on BTC-24SEP27 vs index on 2026-10-14). Metals: when GC contango exceeds financing plus storage (rare for retail). Equity: a conversion.
strategies.risks: Cross-venue (spot on one exchange, future on Deribit) means the hedge margin is on the futures venue and spot cannot be posted directly unless spot is held on Deribit; exchange failure; basis inversion forcing margin top-ups; for inverse futures the hedge quantity drifts with price (USD-notional contracts).
strategies.margin_note: Deribit: spot BTC held on the venue serves as collateral for the short future (fully hedged, low margin). IBIT + CME BTC futures: Reg-T for IBIT, SPAN for CME, no cross-margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: long spot BTC on Deribit + short dated inverse future; payoff in BTC, hedge ratio 1/F USD contracts; no funding on dated futures; the perp version pays/receives 8-hourly funding (see next entry). 24/7 settlement at 08:00 UTC.
strategies.metals_notes: GC cash-and-carry requires physical delivery/warehousing (COMEX-registered bars), so the retail route is GLD long vs OG synthetic short, whose basis is the USD rate minus the GLD expense ratio minus any gold lease rate; Section 1256 applies to OG/GC legs only.
variants: Reverse cash-and-carry (short spot/perp, long future) when basis is negative
Spot + synthetic short via options instead of future (adds strike choice)
Basis term-structure trade (long near basis, short far basis)
IBIT + CME BTC options version (US-regulated, 1256 on the options)
strategies.claim: The Deribit BTC dated-futures basis, annualised, exceeds the FRED 3-month bill rate at every listed quarterly maturity on the capture day, by at least 100 bp, so cash-and-carry has positive carry over Treasuries; the claim is falsified on any day a quarterly future trades at or below spot x (1 + r_bill T).

trial.statistic: Annualised basis per expiry minus r_bill (bp); minimum across expiries.
trial.procedure: Daily (and hourly) snapshot of get_book_summary_by_currency kind=future; compute (mark/index)^(365/DTE) - 1 per expiry; join FRED; record; after 60 days bootstrap the proportion of days with all-positive spread.
trial.data: Deribit public API (live), FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: All quarterlies exceed r_bill + 100 bp on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Use bid for the short future (executable); fee drag 0.05%; compare with CME BTC futures basis if a free quote source is added.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/deribit_basis.py (futures curve snapshot) feeding both this and the box entry; payoff template [underlying+, put+, call-].

strategies.name: Conversion
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat: K at every S_T (stock delivered against the call above K, put exercised below K).
strategies.max_profit: Locked = (C - P) - (S0 - K) + D_received - interest on (S0 - (C - P)) over T. Positive when the synthetic (call rich / put cheap) exceeds fair carry.
strategies.max_loss: Same number if negative; otherwise only the pin/assignment and dividend-change risk below.
strategies.breakevens: None (payoff is flat); the trade is a lending position at implied rate r_impl = ln(K/(S0 - C + P - PV(D)))/T.

greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 (small positive: carry on the locked amount)
greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho negative (higher rates make the synthetic short lose)

strategies.when_to_use: When C - P > S - PV(K) - PV(D) by more than spreads, or to lend cash in a hard-to-borrow name where the put is rich (the conversion collects the borrow). Also a clean way to park a long stock position flat over an event.
strategies.risks: Pin risk at K on expiry (American): if S_T ~ K you may be assigned on the call or not, leaving an unhedged stock position Monday; dividend cut or special dividend; early assignment of the short call before ex-div (loses the dividend); rate rise during the trade.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T treats long stock + long put + short call as a conversion: margin ~ 10% of strike plus any ITM amount of the put; portfolio margin near zero. Carry cost of the stock dominates.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the 'stock' leg is spot BTC or the dated future; with the dated future the conversion collapses to a parity check (no funding). Using the perpetual as the underlying leg turns it into a funding-capture trade (see perp-funding entry). Payoffs in BTC, so the locked USD amount is paid in a variable BTC quantity.
strategies.metals_notes: GC version: long GC future + long OG put + short OG call (same month) locks the future; margin is SPAN on the futures plus option margin; American early assignment on the short call possible when deep ITM. GLD version identical to the equity case with no dividends.
variants: Conversion with ITM put (adds downside cash lock)
Conversion in HTB names to earn implied borrow
Futures conversion (GC/ES)
strategies.claim: Across US single names with CBOE chains, the conversion-implied lending rate exceeds the 3-month bill by more than 100 bp (net of half-spreads) in at least 5% of names on any day, concentrated in names with high short interest, i.e. conversions earn an economically positive borrow premium that ETF conversions (SPY/QQQ/IWM, < 25 bp) do not.

trial.statistic: Cross-sectional distribution of r_impl - r_bill from near-ATM conversions, net of half-spread; share of names with gap > 100 bp.
trial.null: Gap distribution centred at 0 with 95% of names inside +/- 50 bp (no borrow premium anywhere).
trial.procedure: Daily: for the 200 most liquid optionable names plus SPY/QQQ/IWM, compute r_impl per name from 30-60 DTE ATM pairs after paying half-spread on both legs; report the 95th percentile and the ETF values.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains, FRED DGS3MO, dividend schedule.
trial.pass: >= 5% of names with net gap > 100 bp; ETFs < 25 bp; result holds on >= 10 of 15 captured days.
trial.controls: Drop names with ex-div inside T; require put bid > 0.05; compare against a placebo rate computed from mismatched expiries.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse parity.py implied rate per name; add payoff template [underlying+, put+, call-] and assert flat payoff in payoff engine test.

strategies.name: Covered call / cash-secured put equivalence (synthetic identity trade)

legs.strike_rule: same K (the comparison leg: buy back the equivalent short put to prove the identity; in practice you hold either the covered call OR the short put, not both)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Covered call (S_T capped at K + C) equals a cash-secured short put (K - max(K - S_T,0) + P) plus cash PV(K): their difference is the conversion, flat at K. Holding all three legs above gives the flat conversion payoff; the trade decision is which equivalent form to hold.
strategies.max_profit: Covered call: (K - S0) + C; short put: P; difference locked = conversion value (C - P) - (S0 - K) + D - interest.
strategies.max_loss: Covered call: S0 - C (to zero); short put: K - P; the identity itself has no loss except parity frictions.
strategies.breakevens: Covered call: S0 - C; short put: K - P; they coincide when parity holds.

greeks_at_inception.delta: +0.5 to +0.7 for either form (equal by parity)

strategies.when_to_use: Choose the cheaper execution of the same payoff: short puts need one trade and less capital under portfolio margin and avoid dividend/assignment handling; covered calls receive dividends and qualify for 'qualified covered call' tax rules; SPX/XSP versions (1256) exist only as put-write since the index cannot be held (use SPY + XSP calls or pure XSP puts).
strategies.risks: Both carry full downside; early assignment differs (call assignment pre-dividend vs put assignment deep ITM); margin treatment differs by broker.
strategies.margin_note: Covered call: stock margin, call is covered (no extra); cash-secured put: full K in cash or ~20% under Reg-T naked margin; portfolio margin ~15% stress for either.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: covered call = long BTC on venue + short inverse call (premium in BTC); short put requires BTC collateral and pays out in BTC; equivalence holds with interest_rate 0 and no dividends, but inverse convexity makes the BTC-denominated P&L differ.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: long future + short OG call equals short OG put plus a long future at K (all 1256); GLD covered call vs GLD short put as in equities; GLD shares taxed as collectibles if assigned and held.
variants: Put-write index (CBOE PUT) vs buy-write index (CBOE BXM) comparison
Wheel strategy (alternate short put / covered call)
XSP put-write as 1256 substitute for SPY covered calls
strategies.claim: Over 1990-2026 the CBOE S&P 500 PutWrite Index (PUT) and BuyWrite Index (BXM), which hold parity-equivalent positions, differ in annualised return by less than 1 percentage point and their monthly return correlation exceeds 0.95, with PUT ahead by 0.3-1.0 pp/yr because of the Treasury-bill collateral yield and intraday put-sale timing; a larger or sign-reversed gap would falsify the parity-equivalence claim.

trial.statistic: Annualised return difference PUT - BXM; monthly correlation; bootstrap CI of the difference.
trial.procedure: Ingest CBOE PUT and BXM daily index histories (free CSV on cboe.com); compute monthly returns; studentized block bootstrap of the difference and correlation; walk-forward by decade.
trial.data: CBOE PUT/BXM index histories (free download, not yet ingested); FRED bills for the collateral explanation.
trial.pass: Difference inside (0, 1) pp/yr with 95% CI, correlation > 0.95.
trial.controls: Compare BXM with BXMD (OTM calls) to show strike dependence; check the 2008 and 2020 drawdowns coincide.

strategies.blocked_on: CBOE PUT and BXM index daily history (free CSV at cboe.com, not yet ingested)
strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/ingest cboe_index_history(PUT, BXM); experiments/putwrite_vs_buywrite.py with block bootstrap.

strategies.name: Crypto put-call parity vs dated future (Deribit inverse options)

legs.strike_rule: K near ATM (USD strike, premium in BTC)
matching dated future (e.g. BTC-26MAR27), same notional

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Inverse payoff in BTC: call pays max(S_T - K, 0)/S_T, put pays max(K - S_T, 0)/S_T, future pays (S_T - F)/S_T per 1 USD notional unit; sum = (F - K)/S_T BTC = (F - K) USD -> locked. Parity (Deribit prices with interest_rate = 0 and underlying = the future): (C_btc - P_btc) x index = F - K.
strategies.max_profit: Locked = [(C_btc - P_btc) x index] - (F - K) when positive (sell the rich synthetic, buy the future).
strategies.max_loss: Same if negative; plus liquidation risk from BTC-denominated margin during a crash (collateral falls as USD value of the short-put obligation rises).

greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; exposure to BTC/USD on the locked amount (fixed USD, variable BTC)

strategies.when_to_use: Continuously on Deribit BTC/ETH books: parity deviations beyond fees (taker 0.03% of underlying per option, capped at 12.5% of premium; futures 0.05%) appear in illiquid strikes/expiries and around 08:00 UTC settlement. Also the base for every other crypto synthetic (boxes, rolls, cash-and-carry).
strategies.risks: Collateral convexity (inverse); 24/7 liquidation engine; delivery price = 30-min TWAP of the index, not the last trade; different expiry sets between options and futures (use same expiry); exchange counterparty risk; USDC-linear options on Deribit have different parity (no inverse term).
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin recognises the flat combination; standard margin charges the short put (max(0.15 - OTM%, 0.10) x index + mark) in BTC.
strategies.crypto_notes: Live check 2026-10-14: BTC-15OCT26-73000-C mark 0.1257 BTC, index 83,475, underlying_price (BTC-15OCT26 future) 83,494.5, interest_rate 0; the futures curve shows BTC-24SEP27 at ~87,750 vs index 83,475 (~5.1% to Sep-2027, ~5.4%/yr), which is the carry every synthetic inherits. No dividends; funding only matters if the perpetual is used as the hedge.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a (crypto-specific).
variants: Inverse vs USDC-linear option parity (same strike/expiry, different settlement)
Perp-hedged synthetic (adds funding exposure)
ETH parity with ETH/BTC cross-check
Cross-venue: Deribit synthetic vs CME BTC futures (CME 1256, USD cash)
strategies.claim: For Deribit BTC options with open interest > 100 BTC at strikes within 10% of the future and DTE between 7 and 180, the option-implied forward K + (C_mid - P_mid) x index deviates from the matching future's mark by less than 10 bp in at least 99% of (K,T) pairs, and no pair's deviation exceeds the round-trip fee (about 0.11% of notional), i.e. inverse parity holds to within fees at all times sampled.

trial.statistic: |F_impl - F_mark| / F_mark in bp per pair; 99th percentile and max vs fee threshold.
trial.null: 99th percentile < 10 bp and max < fee threshold (no exploitable violations).
trial.procedure: Poll Deribit public API (get_book_summary_by_currency kind=option and kind=future, ticker for underlying_price) hourly; compute per-pair deviation; accumulate 7 days (24/7) for intraday coverage; bootstrap the exceedance rate.
trial.data: Deribit public API (live, reachable now).
trial.pass: Exceedance (> fee threshold) rate < 1% and no persistent (> 1 hour) violations; otherwise the claim is falsified and a parity-capture bot is warranted.
trial.controls: Use mids and executable bid/ask; filter min_trade_amount and zero-bid quotes; verify underlying_price equals the future's mark; include the 08:00 UTC settlement window separately.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/deribit_parity.py polling public endpoints (get_instruments, ticker, get_book_summary_by_currency); payoff engine with inverse payoff mode (divide USD payoff by S_T).

strategies.name: Deribit inverse box spread (USD lending/borrowing in BTC collateral)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: (K2 - K1)/S_T BTC = exactly (K2 - K1) USD worth of BTC at the delivery price, for any S_T. The net debit is paid in BTC today: debit_usd = debit_btc x index. Implied USD rate r_box = ln((K2 - K1)/debit_usd)/T.
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - debit_usd in USD terms, certain (long box); you receive it as BTC quantity (K2 - K1)/S_T.
strategies.max_loss: Zero in USD terms at expiry (European); in BTC terms the position loses BTC when BTC rises (fixed USD paid in fewer coins); margin liquidation risk on the short legs if BTC collateral collapses before expiry.

greeks_at_inception.delta: 0 in USD terms; -1 x (K2-K1)/S in BTC terms (fixed USD claim)

strategies.when_to_use: Lend USD into the crypto funding premium while holding BTC collateral (long box earns r_box typically well above T-bills); borrow USD against BTC via the short box when r_box is below CEX margin-borrow rates; both sides are stablecoin-free USD rate exposure.
strategies.risks: Rate is paid in BTC at delivery: the USD lock is exact but you hold a BTC-denominated receivable; exchange insolvency; liquidation of the short legs under standard margin in a crash (portfolio margin mitigates); wide quotes on far strikes; fees capped at 12.5% of premium can be large relative to interest for short maturities.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin nets the box to near-zero risk; standard margin charges each short option in BTC. Position must be held in a BTC sub-account.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit option premiums and settlement are in BTC (ETH for ETH options); expiry 08:00 UTC; delivery price is a 30-minute TWAP of the index; the futures curve (BTC-24SEP27 at ~5.4%/yr over index on 2026-10-14) sets the expected r_box. Compare with CME BTC options (USD cash, 1256) for a true cross-venue USD rate spread.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a.
variants: Short inverse box (borrow USD against BTC)
ETH box
Box vs futures basis consistency check (r_box should equal the futures carry)
Box vs USDC-linear box (collateral denomination arbitrage)
strategies.claim: The Deribit BTC inverse box-implied USD rate for the two most liquid quarterly expiries (executable prices, after fees) exceeds the FRED 3-month bill by at least 100 bp annualised and matches the same-expiry futures basis within 50 bp, i.e. boxes and futures price the same crypto dollar premium and lending via boxes earns a positive spread over Treasuries.

trial.statistic: r_box - r_bill (bp) and r_box - r_basis (bp) per expiry per poll.
trial.null: r_box - r_bill <= 0 or |r_box - r_basis| > 50 bp (boxes either offer no premium or are inconsistent with futures).
trial.procedure: Hourly polls of Deribit books; build boxes at strikes +/- 20% around the future for the two front quarterlies; compute executable r_box after fees; join FRED and the futures basis; bootstrap over 14 days.
trial.data: Deribit public API, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Median r_box - r_bill >= 100 bp and median |r_box - r_basis| <= 50 bp with 95% CI.
trial.controls: Mid vs executable; strike-pair invariance; exclude the 08:00 UTC settlement hour; ETH as replication.

strategies.harness_suggestion: deribit_parity.py box_rate(); inverse payoff mode in payoff engine; join with FRED via existing ingest.

strategies.name: Dividend arbitrage (long stock + ITM put over ex-div)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T, K) + D - S0 - P: stock is put at K if below, kept if above; the dividend D is collected.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded above K (stock rallies); minimum outcome is the locked amount below.
strategies.max_loss: P - (K - S0) - D = put time value minus dividend; the trade is an 'arbitrage' only when the dividend exceeds the put's time value (rare in liquid names).
strategies.breakevens: D = P - (K - S0), i.e. dividend equals put time value.

greeks_at_inception.theta: - (put time value) offset by dividend accrual

strategies.when_to_use: Day before ex-dividend in names whose deep ITM puts trade at or near intrinsic (time value < dividend), typically illiquid or high-yield names; otherwise an education in market efficiency.
strategies.risks: Put time value usually already embeds the dividend (market makers price it); early exercise by the counterparty is irrelevant (you are long the put) but assignment on any short leg of variants is; execution across two instruments; dividend cancellation risk between purchase and record date; tax: dividend may not qualify as 'qualified' because the put eliminates risk (holding-period rules).
strategies.margin_note: Long stock + long put is a protective put: Reg-T 50% initial on stock, the put reduces maintenance; portfolio margin ~ max loss.
strategies.crypto_notes: No dividends; the closest analogue is airdrop/fork capture with a protective put on Deribit, which Deribit handles via contract adjustments rather than dividend-style payments.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV pay no dividends; GC/SI have no dividend; strategy not applicable.
variants: Deep ITM call sale instead of put purchase (covered call over ex-div; assignment risk means you often lose the dividend)
ETF dividend capture with SPY ITM puts around the quarterly ex-div
strategies.claim: For liquid US names and SPY, on the day before ex-dividend the time value of deep ITM puts (delta < -0.9) expiring after ex-div exceeds the declared dividend in more than 95% of cases, so the dividend-arbitrage has negative expectancy after spreads; positive-expectancy pockets (time value < dividend) are confined to names with option volume below 1,000 contracts/day.

trial.statistic: Share of ex-div-eve observations with (P_ask - (K - S)) < D.
trial.null: Share >= 5% in liquid names (an exploitable pocket exists).
trial.procedure: Capture chains on ex-div eves for names in an ex-div calendar; compute put time value at the executable ask for puts with delta < -0.9 and 7-30 DTE; compare to declared D; stratify by option volume.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains captured on ex-div eves; ex-dividend calendar (not yet ingested); SPY Dec 2026 ex-div as first ETF observation.
trial.pass: Liquid-name share < 5%; illiquid-name share significantly higher (bootstrap CI excludes equality).
trial.controls: Use ask prices (you buy the put); drop special dividends; placebo on non-ex-div days should show time value > 0 always.

strategies.blocked_on: ex-dividend calendar feed plus daily chain capture on ex-div eves (~60 days to accumulate 100 observations)
strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/dividend_play.py keyed off an ex-div calendar; payoff template [underlying+, put+ ITM].

strategies.name: Early exercise of deep ITM American puts for interest

legs.expiry_rule: any American expiry with K(1 - e^{-rT}) > C(K,T)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Decision rule: exercise the put now (receive K, deliver stock) iff interest on K until T, K(1 - e^{-rT}), exceeds the call value C(K,T) you forfeit plus any dividend PV(D) you would have received by holding the stock. Trading version: buy deep ITM puts quoted below intrinsic (K - S) and exercise immediately for a riskless K - S - P_ask.
strategies.max_profit: K - S - P_ask when the put trades below intrinsic (instant); otherwise the interest saved minus forfeited call value.
strategies.max_loss: Forfeited call value if exercised when C(K,T) > interest; execution slippage on the stock leg.
strategies.when_to_use: High-rate regimes (r > 3%) with long-dated deep ITM puts; whenever a market maker quotes a deep ITM American put below intrinsic (happens on wide, stale quotes). Also tells you when to expect assignment on short deep ITM puts (synthetic longs, reversals).
strategies.risks: Need to own or short the stock at exercise (deliverable); stale CBOE delayed quotes can show false sub-intrinsic prices; exercising a hedge put early removes protection.
strategies.margin_note: Exercise delivers stock short if not held: short-sale margin applies until covered.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European: no early exercise; deep ITM puts can trade below intrinsic in BTC terms only as a liquidity artefact, captured by trading not exercising.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO are American on futures: exercising a deep ITM put delivers a short GC future with no interest on K (futures are margined), so the interest motive is absent and early exercise of futures puts is rarely optimal; GLD/SLV follow the equity rule.
variants: Sub-intrinsic put sweep (buy below intrinsic, exercise)
Assignment forecast for short deep ITM puts in synthetic longs
strategies.claim: At the current ~4% bill rate, at least 30% of SPY puts with delta < -0.95 and DTE > 60 quote a mid at or below intrinsic value plus 0.5% of the early-exercise interest K(1 - e^{-rT}), i.e. the market prices immediate exercise as optimal, whereas puts with DTE < 14 almost never do (< 5%).

trial.statistic: Share of deep ITM puts with mid <= (K - S) + 0.005*K(1 - e^{-rT}), by DTE bucket.
trial.null: Share is identical across DTE buckets (no interest-driven exercise premium).
trial.procedure: Daily SPY/QQQ/IWM chain: filter delta < -0.95; compute intrinsic and interest; bucket by DTE; compare shares; bootstrap over captured days.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains, FRED DGS3MO.
trial.pass: Long-dated share >= 30% and short-dated share < 5% on day one; stable over 20 days.
trial.controls: Exclude zero-bid quotes; use bid-ask midpoint and also ask; repeat on SPX (European) where the share should be ~0 for the sub-intrinsic test after discounting.

strategies.harness_suggestion: early_exercise.py put_exercise_criterion; scan function over chains; SPX control built in.

strategies.name: Early exercise of deep ITM calls before ex-dividend (and dividend spread)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after ex-div; exercise at close of the day before ex-div

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Decision rule, not a payoff: exercise iff D > P(K,T) + K(1 - e^{-rT}) (dividend exceeds the put you give up plus interest on the strike). After exercise you hold stock and collect D. Dividend-spread variant: long call K1 / short call K2 (both deep ITM) in huge size, exercise all longs, and profit on whatever fraction of the shorts is not assigned (the pro-rata unexercised OI).
strategies.max_profit: D - [P(K,T) + K(1 - e^{-rT})] per share exercised (vs holding); dividend spread: D x (unassigned fraction) minus spread cost.
strategies.max_loss: If exercised wrongly: forgone put value P(K,T) plus interest; dividend spread: commissions/fees on enormous size with zero capture if all shorts are assigned.
strategies.when_to_use: Any long American call that is deep ITM into an ex-dividend date; essential hygiene for covered-call writers (expect assignment) and for conversion/reversal holders (expect the short call to be called away).

strategies.margin_note: Exercise requires cash or margin for K per share overnight; dividend spread needs enormous notional but offsets as a spread (Reg-T spread margin = K2 - K1).
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European; no early exercise and no dividends, so the rule is void. IBIT options are American but IBIT pays no dividend.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO options are American but futures pay no dividend, so early exercise is driven only by interest/convenience (rarely optimal for calls); GLD/SLV pay nothing.

strategies.max_profit: The initial parity mispricing between the two synthetic forwards plus favourable tracking; small.

strategies.name: Event-contract vs vertical-spread replication (Kalshi/Polymarket digitals vs SPXW verticals)

legs.expiry_rule: SPXW 0 DTE matching the event date (PM, 4:00 pm ET close)

legs.strike_rule: Kalshi/Polymarket YES contract on 'close above K1' (each pays $1; 5 contracts per $5-wide spread per index point; scale by $100 multiplier)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: The vertical pays (K2 - K1) x 100 if S_T >= K2, ~linear between, 0 below K1: a digital call smoothed over [K1, K2]. Divided by its width it approximates P(S_T > K1) under the risk-neutral measure; the YES contract pays $1 if the event occurs. Long vertical + short matched YES has payoff ~0 (hedging error confined to S_T in [K1, K2]).
strategies.max_profit: (YES price - vertical price/width) x contracts when YES is rich relative to the SPXW-implied digital (sell YES, buy vertical), or the reverse.
strategies.max_loss: The hedging error on [K1, K2] plus fees (Kalshi fee ~ 7% x P x (1-P) per contract; SPXW commissions) plus settlement mismatch if the event's reference price differs from SPX's 4:00 pm close.
strategies.breakevens: YES price = (C(K1) - C(K2)) / (K2 - K1), the risk-neutral digital probability (both quoted at the same time).

greeks_at_inception.delta: ~0 after matching; vertical alone delta = density x width
greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0; the YES contract has no explicit vega but its fair value moves with SPX IV

strategies.when_to_use: Whenever an event venue lists a threshold contract on an asset with a liquid 0 DTE option chain (SPX, NDX, BTC via Deribit dailies, gold via GLD weeklies) and the YES price differs from the options-implied digital by more than fees; also to price binary contracts fairly before quoting them.
strategies.risks: Settlement source mismatch (Kalshi uses the official index close; Polymarket may use a different oracle/time); CBOE delayed quotes (15 min) make live arbitrage impossible from the free feed, so this is a paper/signal test unless a real-time feed is added; venue counterparty and withdrawal risk; position limits on event venues; the vertical's width creates basis in the [K1, K2] band.
strategies.margin_note: Vertical: debit paid; YES/NO contracts are fully collateralised ($1 per contract minus price); no cross-margin between venues.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC threshold contracts on Polymarket/Kalshi vs Deribit daily options: Deribit digitals come from inverse call spreads divided by width, settled at the 08:00 UTC TWAP, while event venues settle on their own oracle/time, so align the settlement time or carry the gap as basis; 24/7 markets mean the options venue can hedge continuously.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold threshold contracts vs GLD weekly verticals (GLD closes vs the event's gold fix/reference: different reference prices, so the basis is larger).
variants: YES + NO complement parity (YES + NO < 1 - fees on the same venue; buy both)
Cross-venue same event (Kalshi vs Polymarket YES price divergence)

trial.null: Share > $0.05 is below 10% and the signed mean is 0 (event prices are consistent with options).

trial.data: Polymarket/Kalshi contract data (available), CBOE delayed SPXW chain (available, 15-min delay), SPX official closes.
trial.pass: Exceedance share >= 10% with 95% CI excluding 10%, and the options-implied digital has a lower Brier score than the event price (confirms the options venue is the better pricer).

strategies.name: Expiration pin risk management and pinning trade

legs.strike_rule: K_pin = strike with highest combined OI within 0.5% of spot on expiry day

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Short straddle at the pin: credit - |S_T - K_pin|; the defensive version is the opposite action: close or roll any short option within 1% of spot before the close to avoid uncertain assignment.
strategies.max_profit: Net credit (S_T = K_pin).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded (short straddle) until the close; after the close, pin risk: unknown assignment leaves an unhedged stock position over the weekend.
strategies.when_to_use: Pinning trade: last 1-2 hours of monthly/weekly expiration when spot sits within 0.5% of a heavy-OI strike (delta-hedging flows by long-gamma market makers push price toward the strike). Risk management: every conversion/reversal/covered-call holder must decide before the close whether a short leg at the money will be assigned (OCC exercise-by-exception auto-exercises at $0.01 ITM).
strategies.risks: Late news; after-hours moves after the 4:00 pm ET close can change ITM status for SPY (holders can exercise until ~5:30 pm) -> assignment surprises; SPX AM-settled options settle on the opening print (SET), not the prior close; pinning weakens when market makers are net short gamma.
strategies.margin_note: Short 0 DTE straddle requires naked-straddle margin (~20% of underlying); assignment on an ETF leg converts to a stock position needing Reg-T 50%.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit expiry is 08:00 UTC with delivery = 30-minute TWAP of the index, cash-settled in BTC: there is no assignment surprise, only TWAP settlement risk; max-pain pinning is widely discussed for the quarterly 08:00 UTC expiries and is testable from Deribit OI.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO exercise into GC/SI futures (American): a pinned short option can leave you with a futures position at the open; GLD/SLV follow equity rules.
variants: Defensive: close/roll short legs within 1% of spot by 3:30 pm ET
Max-pain fade: short straddle at the max-pain strike on expiry morning

trial.statistic: Mean |close - nearest integer| on expiration days vs non-expiration days; bootstrap difference.
trial.null: No difference (distance ~ uniform on [0, 0.5], mean 0.25 both groups).
trial.procedure: SPY daily closes since 2005 (when $1 strikes and weeklies became available), flag third Fridays (and Mon/Wed/Fri weeklies from 2016); compute distance to nearest integer; studentized block bootstrap of the difference; walk-forward by year.
trial.data: SPY daily closes (available), expiration calendar (deterministic).
trial.pass: Expiration-day mean distance at least 10% below non-expiration mean with bootstrap p < 0.05, and the effect present in the majority of years.
trial.controls: Placebo days (Thursdays); scale test with $0.50 strikes post-2020; repeat for QQQ and single names with $5 strikes where the effect should be larger.

strategies.name: Hard-to-borrow synthetic (implied borrow extraction and lending via conversion)

legs.strike_rule: spot S0 (shares you can lend or already own)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat at K; the locked profit equals the implied borrow fee: in HTB names puts are rich / calls cheap, so C - P < S - PV(K) and the conversion earns (S - PV(K)) - (C - P) ~ borrow x T x S on top of the risk-free rate. Reverse conversion (short stock, long call, short put) is the borrower's side and pays the fee.
strategies.max_profit: Implied borrow fee x S x T + r x S x T, locked, when the stock is not recalled.
strategies.max_loss: If you lend the shares and they are recalled or the fee collapses, you lose the fee; early assignment of the short call pre-dividend loses the dividend; pin risk at K.
strategies.breakevens: None in S_T; profitable while implied borrow > 0 after spreads.
strategies.when_to_use: When you hold or can buy a hard-to-borrow stock (meme names, recent IPOs, biotech) and the chain shows implied borrow > 5%/yr: the conversion monetises your long's lending value with options instead of a stock-loan desk. For short-sellers: use the synthetic short only if its implicit borrow is below your broker's fee.
strategies.risks: HTB stocks have huge spreads; the fee is a compensation for crash/squeeze risk you actually hold if assignment goes wrong; corporate actions; dividend changes.
strategies.margin_note: Conversion margin (Reg-T ~10% of strike + ITM put amount); lenders of shares at the broker may be earning only part of the fee, so compare with the options-implied rate.
strategies.crypto_notes: No stock-borrow market on Deribit; the analogue is the perpetual funding rate (longs pay shorts when crowded long), captured with short perp + long dated future or long option synthetic (see perp-funding entry). CEX margin borrow rates for altcoins are the HTB analogue.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/SLV occasionally become HTB during physical squeezes (2021 silver); SLV implied borrow from the chain spikes then. GC/SI futures have no borrow.
variants: Reverse conversion for market makers receiving full borrow

strategies.name: Long box spread (SPX box lending)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Exactly K2 - K1 at every S_T (bull call spread + bear put spread).
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) - net_debit, certain if European; implied lending rate r_box = ln((K2 - K1)/net_debit)/T.
strategies.max_loss: Zero at expiry for European options (fixed payoff); mark-to-market loss if rates rise before T and you unwind; for American options, early assignment can unwind one spread and leave open risk.
strategies.breakevens: None; it is a zero-coupon bond paying K2 - K1 at T.

greeks_at_inception.vega: 0; rho negative (rate rise lowers the box's present value)

strategies.when_to_use: Lend cash at the SPX box rate, which historically exceeds T-bills by a convenience yield of roughly 30-40 bp (van Binsbergen, Diamond, Grotteria); earn interest as 60/40 Section 1256 capital gains; park collateral in a margin account with no bank or money-market intermediary.
strategies.risks: Liquidity/spread: four legs, wide strikes; must use European cash-settled options (SPX, XSP, SPXW, NDX, RUT); American boxes (SPY) can be blown up by early assignment (the 2019 Robinhood case lost ~$57k on $5k after one leg was exercised); counterparty risk is OCC (AAA-like); mark-to-market if unwound early.
strategies.margin_note: Long box is fully paid (net debit); portfolio margin recognises a flat payoff and requires ~0 beyond the debit. Spread width should be wide (e.g. 1000-2000 SPX points) to minimise relative spread cost; use deep ITM/OTM legs with tight quotes via complex order book.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse box pays (K2 - K1) USD worth of BTC at the delivery price (each inverse option pays max(S-K,0)/S BTC), so a BTC box is a USD lending trade settled in BTC; implied USD rate typically far above T-bills, mirroring the futures basis; European, cash-settled, 08:00 UTC expiry; see deribit-inverse-box entry.
strategies.metals_notes: OG/SO boxes are American (exercise into GC/SI futures) so early-assignment risk exists; GLD/SLV boxes also American. Not a clean lending vehicle in metals; prefer SPX.
variants: Box calendar / forward-rate lock: long near box, short far box (locks the forward rate between T1 and T2)
Box ladder across expiries (term structure of box rates)
XSP box (1/10 size) for small accounts
Box vs SOFR/T-bill futures spread trade (see box-treasury-convenience-yield)

trial.procedure: Each day: build boxes at every SPX expiry with 90 <= DTE <= 365 using strikes +/- 15% around spot; r_box = ln((K2-K1)/debit_exec)/T; interpolate FRED bill to the same maturity; record spread; block-bootstrap the daily median as capture accumulates.

strategies.name: Perpetual funding vs dated-future/option-synthetic carry
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Delta-flat: long dated forward (via options) vs short perp; P&L = cumulative funding received - (F_impl - S0) basis paid + perp-vs-index tracking.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded in principle (funding can stay high), realistically funding - basis over T.
strategies.max_loss: If funding turns negative for long stretches you pay funding while also having paid the basis; plus liquidation risk on the perp during squeezes.
strategies.breakevens: Cumulative funding over T = basis paid at entry.
strategies.when_to_use: When annualised perp funding exceeds the dated basis (crowded longs); common in bull phases; the options version lets you pick a strike and avoids a second futures position.
strategies.risks: Funding is variable and mean-reverting; perp mark deviations from index; 24/7 liquidation; collateral convexity (inverse).
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin offsets the perp against the option synthetic; standard margin charges both.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit funding on BTC-PERPETUAL is paid continuously (8h reference), history via public get_funding_rate_history; dated futures pay no funding. ETH analogue identical.
strategies.metals_notes: n/a.

Long perp / short synthetic when funding is negative
Cross-exchange funding arbitrage (Deribit vs other perps)

strategies.name: Put-call parity scan / synthetic forward
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - K per unit (a forward struck at K). Parity: C - P = S - PV(K) - PV(D), i.e. implied forward F_impl = K + (C - P)*e^{rT}. Every other entry in this family is a rearrangement of this identity.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded above (S_T - K - net_debit, net_debit = C - P).
strategies.max_loss: K + net_debit per unit if S_T -> 0 (same as owning the forward).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: 0 (call gamma cancels put gamma at same K/T)
greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 net; carry accrues as interest on PV(K) minus dividends

strategies.when_to_use: Baseline monitor: compute F_impl for each (K,T) and compare with S*e^{rT} - FV(D). A violation larger than half the combined bid-ask is a conversion/reversal candidate; otherwise the scan yields the market-implied financing rate and dividend, which feed every other arbitrage template.
strategies.risks: American early exercise breaks exact equality for equity/ETF options (only bounds hold: S - K <= C - P <= S - PV(K) - PV(D)); dividend forecast error; stale quotes on CBOE 15-min delayed feed can fake violations; execution legging risk.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T: short put margin (20% of underlying) plus long call premium; portfolio margin treats the pair as a synthetic stock. Index (SPX/XSP) legs are 1256 contracts.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse options: premium and payoff in BTC/ETH, underlying_price on the ticker is the matching dated future and interest_rate = 0, so parity reads (C_btc - P_btc)*index = F - K with no discounting. No dividends; 24/7; funding appears via the futures basis, not the option legs.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI options are American and settle into the future, so parity is C - P = e^{-rT}(F - K) only as a bound; GLD/SLV options follow the equity-option version with D = 0 but a 0.40%/0.50% expense drag embedded in the forward; GC/SI options are Section 1256, GLD/SLV options are not.
variants: Fiduciary call = married put (long call + PV(K) cash vs long stock + long put)
Cash-secured put = covered call equivalence
American parity bounds check (S - K <= C - P <= S - PV(K) - PV(D))
Implied dividend extraction D_impl = S - PV(K) - (C - P)
strategies.claim: On CBOE delayed SPY/SPX chains, option-implied forwards from ATM +/-5 strikes deviate from S*e^{rT} - FV(D) by more than half the combined call+put bid-ask spread in fewer than 2% of (K,T) pairs, so there is no exploitable parity edge in liquid ETF/index options and the implied financing rate sits within 50 bp of the FRED 3-month bill.

trial.statistic: Fraction of (K,T) pairs with |F_impl - F_theo| > 0.5*(spread_call + spread_put); and median (r_impl - r_bill).
trial.null: Deviations are inside the half-spread noise band (exploitable fraction = 0, median rate gap = 0 +/- 50 bp).
trial.procedure: Each day: pull SPY and SPX chains, FRED 3m bill, SPY dividend schedule; for each expiry take ATM +/-5 strikes; compute F_impl from mids and r_impl per expiry; count violations; block-bootstrap the daily violation rate as capture accumulates.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains (SPY, SPX), FRED DGS3MO, SPY ex-div calendar (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec third Friday).
trial.pass: Violation fraction < 2% and |median r_impl - r_bill| < 50 bp on day one; stable over 20 captured days.
trial.controls: Exclude strikes with zero bid; use mids not lasts; re-run with quotes aged < 15 min; placebo: shuffle puts across adjacent strikes to confirm the statistic detects artificial violations.

strategies.harness_suggestion: mandel/options/parity.py: implied_forward(chain, r, divs) -> per-(K,T) table; wire into payoff engine as a 2-leg template; daily job appends to data/options/parity/.

strategies.name: Reversal (reverse conversion)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Flat: -K at every S_T (you buy stock at K via the call above K or via put assignment below K and cover the short).
strategies.max_profit: Locked = (S0 - K) - (C - P) + interest on short proceeds - D_paid - borrow fee.
strategies.max_loss: Same number if negative; plus unbounded tail if the short stock is bought in or the borrow fee spikes before T.
strategies.breakevens: None; it is a borrowing-and-lending position: you lend the short proceeds at r and effectively borrow via the synthetic at r_impl.
strategies.when_to_use: When the put is cheap relative to the call (C - P > fair) or when you can earn full interest on short-sale proceeds and the stock is easy to borrow; market makers use reversals to flatten inventory.
strategies.risks: Hard-to-borrow: fee rises or forced buy-in destroys the lock; must pay dividends on the short stock (dividend increase hurts); pin risk at K on the short put; early assignment of the short put (American) if deep ITM with rates high.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T reversal margin ~10% of strike plus ITM amount of the call; short-sale proceeds typically earn little or nothing at retail brokers, which kills the trade for retail; portfolio margin near zero.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: short the dated future instead of borrowing coin, so no borrow fee and no buy-in risk; the lock is then a pure parity check. Shorting spot BTC on CEX margin incurs hourly borrow interest that replaces the equity borrow fee.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: short GC future + long OG call + short OG put; no borrow fee (futures), SPAN margin. GLD/SLV: ETF borrow is usually general collateral but can tighten when physical premiums spike.
variants: Reversal with ITM call
Futures reversal (no borrow)
Reversal on IBIT vs long BTC on Deribit (cross-venue)
strategies.claim: Options-implied borrow rates (r_bill - r_impl from reversal pricing) in US single names are widely dispersed on any day: the 90th percentile exceeds 200 bp/yr while SPY/QQQ/IWM sit below 50 bp, so reversals in ETFs have zero edge and reversals in high-implied-borrow names have negative expectancy unless the trader actually receives the borrow.

trial.statistic: 90th percentile of implied borrow across names vs ETF implied borrow; both net of half-spread.
trial.null: Implied borrow is not dispersed: 90th percentile < 50 bp, indistinguishable from ETFs.
trial.procedure: Daily cross-section over the 200 most liquid optionable names at 30-90 DTE; compute implied borrow = r_bill - r_impl; report quantiles; bootstrap the quantile over captured days.
trial.data: CBOE delayed chains, FRED DGS3MO, dividend schedule.
trial.pass: 90th percentile > 200 bp and ETFs < 50 bp on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Exclude ex-div inside T; exclude names with stale (non-updating) quotes; placebo with randomised strikes.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Same parity.py output, reported as implied_borrow column; payoff template [underlying-, call+, put-].

strategies.name: Short box spread (SPX box borrowing)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Exactly -(K2 - K1) at every S_T; you received net_credit today.
strategies.max_profit: None as a trade; it is a loan: borrow net_credit, repay K2 - K1 at T; implied borrowing rate r_box = ln((K2 - K1)/net_credit)/T.
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - net_credit (the interest), certain for European options; with American options early exercise against you can create open directional risk.
strategies.when_to_use: Borrow at near-Treasury rates against portfolio margin instead of paying the broker's margin loan rate; fund stock or other positions; interest cost is a 1256 capital loss rather than non-deductible margin interest for many retail traders.
strategies.risks: Broker margin requirement on the short box may not be zero (Reg-T can require the spread width as margin, defeating the purpose; portfolio margin usually recognises it); forced liquidation if other positions lose; must not be done with American options; unwind cost if rates fall.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin: requirement ~0 beyond the (K2-K1) liability, which is recognised as a debit; Reg-T brokers may hold full spread width. Only SPX/XSP/NDX/RUT.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit short inverse box borrows USD (received as BTC premium) and repays a fixed USD amount in BTC; implied rate equals the crypto dollar funding premium, usually several hundred bp above bills, so crypto short boxes are an expensive way to borrow.
strategies.metals_notes: Not advisable in American futures options (OG/SO) or GLD/SLV because of early assignment.
variants: XSP short box for small loans
Rolling short boxes (refinance at each expiry)
Short box financing a long box at a later date (forward rate lock)
strategies.claim: The executable SPX short-box borrowing rate for 6-24 month maturities is at least 100 bp below a benchmark retail margin rate of (3-month bill + 150 bp) on at least 80% of trading days, so portfolio-margin accounts can refinance margin loans via boxes.

trial.statistic: r_box_borrow (hit bids / lift offers on four legs) minus (r_bill + 150 bp).
trial.null: r_box_borrow >= r_bill + 50 bp (no advantage over margin loans).
trial.procedure: Daily over SPX expiries with 180 <= DTE <= 730: build wide boxes, compute executable borrowing rate, compare to bill + 150 bp; also record the mid-based rate.
trial.data: CBOE delayed SPX chain; FRED DGS6MO/DGS1/DGS2.
trial.pass: Median advantage > 100 bp on day one and on >= 80% of captured days.
trial.controls: Check strike-invariance; drop expiries with zero-bid legs; compare SPX vs XSP implied rates (should match).

strategies.harness_suggestion: box.py with side='short' using executable prices; report borrow curve.

strategies.name: Synthetic long stock (combo)

legs.strike_rule: K ATM (or K_call >= K_put for split-strike)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - K - net_debit (same-strike); split-strike: flat between K_put and K_call, long above, short-put exposure below.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded.
strategies.max_loss: K + net_debit (S_T -> 0), i.e. stock-like.

greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 (same strike); carry = -(K*(1-e^{-rT})) + PV(D) embedded in the debit

strategies.when_to_use: Stock replacement with less cash tied up than margin buying, when the options-implied financing rate is below the broker margin rate; expressing long exposure in an account that cannot buy the underlying (e.g. BTC exposure via IBIT or Deribit options).
strategies.risks: Full downside; early assignment of the short put (American) when deep ITM with high rates; you do not receive dividends (they are priced in); implied financing can exceed margin rates in HTB or high-rate regimes; margin call on the short put.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T: short put margin (~20% of underlying minus OTM amount) plus long call cost; portfolio margin ~ 15% stress; SPX/XSP versions are cash-settled 1256 contracts.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit a synthetic long via inverse options behaves like a long inverse future: USD-linear payoff paid in BTC; margin is taken in BTC so a crash shrinks collateral as the position loses (convexity of inverse contracts). Equivalent to a dated future with interest_rate = 0.
strategies.metals_notes: OG synthetic long = long GC future with option margin instead of SPAN; GLD synthetic avoids the 28% collectibles tax rate on physical/GLD shares held > 1 year only if the options themselves qualify as equity options (short-term rates), so the tax angle is mixed.
variants: Split-strike synthetic / risk reversal (K_put < K_call), zero-cost collar inverse

strategies.name: Synthetic short stock (combo)

legs.strike_rule: K ATM (or K_put <= K_call for split strike)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: K - S_T + net_credit (same strike).
strategies.max_profit: K + net_credit (S_T -> 0).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded above.
strategies.when_to_use: Short exposure without a locate, without buy-in risk and without paying dividends explicitly (they are in the price); hedging a long position in a name that is hard to borrow; shorting an index via SPX/XSP with 1256 treatment.
strategies.risks: Unbounded loss; early assignment on the short call before ex-div (American); in HTB names the put is rich, so the implicit borrow is paid up front; margin on the short call rises as the stock rallies.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T: short call margin (20% of underlying) plus long put cost; portfolio margin ~15% stress. Pin risk at K on the short call at expiry.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit synthetic short via inverse options = short inverse future: profits in BTC grow in BTC terms as price falls (convex in favour of the short); no borrow or funding, unlike shorting the perp.
strategies.metals_notes: OG synthetic short = short GC future with option margin; SLV/GLD synthetic shorts avoid ETF borrow, which can become expensive in physical squeezes.
variants: Split-strike synthetic short (bearish risk reversal)
Deep ITM put stock-replacement short

trial.null: ETF implicit borrow >= 50 bp (synthetic shorts systematically expensive).

strategies.name: Calendarised (time) butterfly
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Wings bought in the far expiry, body sold in the near, K1 < K2 < K3 equidistant. At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = V_far(S; K1) + V_far(S; K3) - 2*max(S - K2, 0) - D. Because the intrinsic values cancel for equidistant strikes ((S-K1) + (S-K3) - 2(S-K2) = 0), the far-wing extrinsic is what remains on a big move, so the structure is a butterfly whose edges are lifted by the wings' remaining time value.
strategies.max_profit: Near S = K2 at T1: V_far(K2; K1) + V_far(K2; K3) - D, roughly (K2 - K1) + 2*extrinsic_far - D (higher than the plain fly's (K2 - K1) - D, Fidelity).
strategies.max_loss: Approximately D - residual far-wing extrinsic when S is far outside the wings at T1; bounded by D at T1. If the far wings are held after T1 they become a long strangle with its own bleed (cannot lose more than their value).
strategies.breakevens: Two roots near K1 + D - extrinsic_far and K3 - D + extrinsic_far (the plain fly's K1 + D and K3 - D, Fidelity, pushed outward by the wings' remaining time value).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative near K2 (two short near calls)
greeks_at_inception.vega: near zero to positive (two far-wing vegas vs two near-body vegas), unlike the plain butterfly's negative vega (Fidelity)

strategies.when_to_use: Pin-the-strike view for the front cycle with protection against an IV rise (the plain fly loses when IV rises); low absolute IV; flat or inverted term structure (front body rich). Serves as a calendar with a cheaper, wider body.
strategies.risks: A move through a wing before T1 loses toward D; the two short body calls carry assignment and pin risk at T1; four legs of costs; after T1 the far wings must be re-sold against or closed; brokers may margin the two near shorts against the far longs only if the long expiries are later (they are).
strategies.margin_note: Debit structure; margined as two diagonal spreads (long far / short near on each side), defined risk, IRA-eligible at most brokers.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit strike grids are coarse at long expiries (wider steps at quarterlies), so equidistant wings across expiries may not exist for the same K1/K3; European cash settlement removes body-assignment risk; standard margin does not net the body against the wings (Portfolio Margin does); weekend theta on the body is a plus.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: wings and body reference different futures months; SPAN spread credit; 1256. GLD/SLV: fine strike grids ($1 on GLD) make equidistant time butterflies easy to construct; SLV's call skew tilts the pricing. CME pages unreachable this session (503).
variants: Broken-wing calendarised fly (skip a strike on one wing to finance)
Put time butterfly
Iron time butterfly: short near ATM straddle, long far OTM strangle (Fidelity's inside-straddle double diagonal reversed)
Reverse time butterfly: body in the far, wings in the near (short vega)
Weekly body (7 DTE) vs monthly wings

strategies.name: Double calendar spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1 with K1 (puts) < S0 < K2 (calls): P&L(S) = V_far_put(S; K1) + V_far_call(S; K2) - max(K1-S, 0) - max(S-K2, 0) - D. Two humps centred on K1 and K2 with a shallow saddle between them; floor -D far outside both strikes.
strategies.max_profit: At S = K1 or S = K2 on the front expiry: V_far_put(K_i) + V_far_call(K_i) - D (the far leg at that strike holds maximum time value); depends on IV at T1.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), when S finishes far outside both strikes at T1; if the humps merge (strikes close) the saddle can still be a small profit.
strategies.breakevens: Up to four roots of V_far_put(S)+V_far_call(S) - max(K1-S,0) - max(S-K2,0) = D: one outside each hump and, if the saddle dips below zero, two inside; typically two (outside) when the saddle is positive.

greeks_at_inception.theta: positive between the strikes (sum of two calendars), negative far outside

strategies.when_to_use: Range-bound expectation over the front cycle with low IV expected to rise or stay; a wider profit zone than a single calendar at the cost of a lower peak and twice the commissions. Prefer when the term structure is flat or inverted (selling the front rich).
strategies.risks: A trending move through either strike loses toward D; IV drop hurts; four legs of bid-ask; early assignment on the short near legs (puts on ex-div for ITM puts, calls before ex-div); pin risk at T1 on either short strike.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full; two defined-risk spreads, IRA-eligible; no margin beyond the debit while the longs outlive the shorts.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: four legs each pay taker fees capped at a fraction of premium; standard margin does not offset the shorts against the longs (Portfolio Margin does), so collateral is higher than the debit. European cash settlement at 08:00 UTC removes assignment risk; BTC's positive call skew makes the call calendar half pricier than on SPY. Weekend theta accrues 7 days a week.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: both shorts and both longs reference different futures months (near vs far), so the structure also carries the futures calendar spread; SPAN margins it as two calendar spreads; 1256 60/40. GLD/SLV: equity-option route with weeklies; SLV's call skew tilts the pricing. CME spec pages unreachable this session (503); futures-month and exercise details from training knowledge.

Triple calendar (adds an ATM calendar to fill the saddle)
Weekly double calendar: 7/35 DTE

strategies.name: Double diagonal spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Wings-outside form (K1 < K2 < S0 < K3 < K4, an iron condor whose wings are in the later expiry). At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = V_far_put(S; K1) + V_far_call(S; K4) - max(K2-S, 0) - max(S-K3, 0) - D (or + C if entered for a credit). Plateau between K2 and K3, sloping down to a floor outside the wings. Fidelity's version puts a long 56-day ATM straddle inside a short 28-day strangle (long legs at the middle strike).
strategies.max_profit: Between K2 and K3 at T1: V_far_put(K; K1) + V_far_call(K; K4) - D (both shorts expire worthless, longs keep time value); highest near a short strike; depends on IV at T1 (Fidelity).
strategies.max_loss: Wings-outside: approximately (K2 - K1) + D - residual far-wing value (or (K2 - K1) - C for a credit entry), when S is far beyond a wing at T1. Fidelity's inside-straddle form: D, if S sits at the straddle strike at the straddle's expiry.
strategies.breakevens: Two: one below K2 and one above K3, where the far wing's remaining value minus the short's intrinsic equals D; exact levels depend on volatility (Fidelity).

greeks_at_inception.theta: positive between the short strikes; approaches zero beyond a breakeven (Fidelity)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive and large ('highly sensitive to volatility', Fidelity); approaches zero if S moves sharply beyond a short strike

strategies.when_to_use: Iron-condor alternative when IV is low and expected to rise, or when the term structure is flat/inverted so the near strangle is rich relative to the far wings; neutral forecast with S between K2 and K3 through T1.
strategies.risks: Profit potential is small in dollar terms relative to legs traded (Fidelity); a trending move past a short strike approaches max loss; falling IV hurts; early assignment on the shorts around ex-dividend; after T1 the two far wings are a long strangle that bleeds unless re-sold against.
strategies.margin_note: Wings-outside form is margined as two diagonal spreads (max loss = width + debit) and is IRA-eligible at most brokers; the inside-straddle form is a debit structure. Requires the long expiry >= short expiry on each side.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: wings and body expire on different Fridays at 08:00 UTC; European cash settlement means the body settles to cash and leaves the far strangle; standard margin does not net longs against shorts, so Portfolio Margin is needed for the structure to be capital-efficient; BTC skew is roughly symmetric to call-skewed, so the call side is not the cheap side as it is on SPY.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: four options across two futures months; SPAN gives inter-month spread credit; 1256. GLD/SLV: the natural retail route; SLV call skew makes the call wing relatively costly. CME pages unreachable through the proxy this session (503); spec details from training knowledge.

trial.null: Zero difference; paired monthly P&L permuted between structures

trial.pass: Difference > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 in both halves; result holds with and without the SKEW tilt
trial.controls: Eight fills of costs vs four; max-loss normalisation uses the realised far-wing value at T1 (not the theoretical bound) so capital efficiency is compared fairly

strategies.name: Event (earnings / macro) calendar

legs.expiry_rule: near: first expiry after the event (<= 7 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry just after the event: P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1_post) - max(S - K, 0) - D. Same tent as a long calendar, but the edge is in the entry: the event-week option carries an implied event move that inflates the front IV far above the back (a local inversion of the term structure), and after the event the front IV collapses while the back's IV falls much less.
strategies.max_profit: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_post) - D at S = K after the event; sigma_post is typically the back IV minus the event's share of variance.
strategies.max_loss: D, when the realised event move carries S far from K; D is small because the front sells rich (often 30-60% of the far leg's premium).
strategies.breakevens: Two roots of V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_post) - max(S - K, 0) = D; the distance from K is roughly the implied event move minus the IV-crush gain on the back leg.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative and large (the event move is the risk)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive and large (the front's event premium decays in days)
greeks_at_inception.vega: short front/event vega, long back vega - net long vega to the back month, net short 'event variance'

strategies.when_to_use: When the implied event move (front ATM straddle / spot) exceeds the name's historical realised event move by a margin, and the front/back IV ratio is well above 1; works on earnings (TSLA, NVDA, AAPL), FOMC/CPI weeks on SPY/TLT, and ETF-flow or macro dates on IBIT.
strategies.risks: A realised move beyond the implied move loses the debit (and the debit is the only cushion); post-event IV crush also hits the back leg (partial); pin risk on the event-week expiry; early assignment if the stock gaps through K before expiry; liquidity in the event-week expiry on smaller names.
strategies.margin_note: Debit calendar, defined risk, IRA-eligible; the short leg must expire no later than the long.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit's daily and weekly expiries (08:00 UTC) let the front leg be placed exactly after a scheduled macro print or ETF decision; BTC has no earnings, so events are CPI/FOMC, ETF-flow announcements and protocol dates; the event premium shows up as a kink in the chain's mark_iv by expiry (DVOL is 30-day only and will not show it); European cash settlement means no assignment risk; inverse premium in BTC.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: FOMC/NFP/CPI weeks inflate the front weekly options on the active futures month; weekly GC options (Fri/Mon/Wed) give precise post-event expiries; the far leg references the same futures month if both are within the month, otherwise the futures spread enters; 1256. GLD/SLV: weeklies on the ETF for the same trade. CME pages unreachable this session (503).

strategies.name: Jelly roll (synthetic time spread / financing trade)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long jelly roll = long far synthetic (long call / short put at K, T2) and short near synthetic (short call / long put at K, T1). At T1 the near synthetic settles to -(S - K) and the far synthetic is worth S - K*exp(-r*tau) - PV(dividends in (T1, T2)), so P&L = K*(1 - exp(-r*tau)) - PV(div) - D: independent of S. Fair value at entry D* = K*(exp(-r*T1) - exp(-r*T2)) - PV(dividends between T1 and T2).
strategies.max_profit: D* - D (fair carry minus price paid), locked at entry absent early exercise or dividend surprises; no spot dependence.
strategies.max_loss: D - D*, plus early-assignment and dividend-change risk on the short legs (a short ITM put may be assigned early for interest; a short ITM call before ex-div); pin risk at T1 if S ~ K.
strategies.breakevens: None in spot; the trade breaks even when realised carry (rates and dividends over (T1, T2)) equals the price paid.

greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 apart from the accrual of carry; the sensitivities that matter are rho (rates) and dividends

strategies.when_to_use: To lend or borrow at the option-implied rate, to move a synthetic position between expiries (roll a long synthetic forward), or as a no-arbitrage check on a chain: a jelly roll priced away from K*(exp(-rT1) - exp(-rT2)) - PV(div) by more than the bid-ask is either a dividend-forecast disagreement or a mispricing.
strategies.risks: Early assignment on the short legs converts the structure into stock plus options with margin consequences; dividend changes between T1 and T2 move the fair value one-for-one; pin risk at T1; four-leg execution slippage usually exceeds the theoretical edge; under Reg T the short synthetic may be margined as a naked short option.
strategies.margin_note: Portfolio margin (and SPX/XSP in particular) recognises the near-zero risk; Reg T retail accounts may require naked-short margin on the short put/call legs, which kills the economics; SPX/XSP jelly rolls are 1256 contracts and European (no early exercise).
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the jelly roll trades the futures basis/funding between two Fridays rather than r - q: fair value is K times the difference in the two expiries' discount factors implied by the futures, with no dividends; European settlement removes early exercise, so deviations are purer; inverse premium denominates the carry in BTC. Deribit lists option_combo instruments, and public/get_delivery_prices gives the settlement series needed to verify realised carry.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: a jelly roll across futures months is a synthetic futures calendar spread; its fair value is the futures spread (gold carry = rate - lease rate), so deviations measure option-vs-futures mispricing; 1256 60/40. GLD/SLV: no dividends, so fair value is K*(exp(-rT1) - exp(-rT2)) exactly; American exercise adds a small early-exercise premium on deep-ITM puts. CME pages unreachable this session (503).

strategies.name: LEAPS collar (long-dated put, serial short calls)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At each short-call expiry T1: P&L(S) = (S - S0) + V_put(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S - Kc, 0) + sum of call credits - P_put. At the put's expiry with all shorts expired OTM: standard collar payoff, floor at Kp and cap at the last Kc.
strategies.max_profit: Per cycle: Kc - S0 + C_t (plus the put's residual value); over the put's life: (Kc - S0) + sum of credits - P_put if the stock finishes at or above the final Kc (Fidelity collar: call strike + net credit - stock price).
strategies.max_loss: S0 - Kp + P_put - sum of credits, if S <= Kp at the put's expiry (Fidelity: stock price - net credit - put strike).
strategies.breakevens: S0 + P_put - sum of call credits (Fidelity: stock price + put price - call price); falls each month as credits accumulate.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: slightly negative near Kc, slightly positive near Kp
greeks_at_inception.theta: near zero to positive: fast decay of the monthly call versus slow decay of the 12-month put
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long-dated put vega far exceeds the near call's); a standard same-expiry collar has near-zero vega (Fidelity)

strategies.when_to_use: Protect a concentrated or low-basis position with a cheap-per-day long-dated floor financed by serial monthly calls; exploits the term structure of theta (the put bought at 365 DTE loses time value far more slowly than the 30-DTE calls sold against it). Also the standard way to hedge SPY/QQQ holdings through a year of known events.
strategies.risks: A strong rally caps gains at each Kc while the put's value evaporates; after a sell-off the put is ITM but the stock is lower (hedge pays, but rolling the put resets it at a higher cost); IV collapse hurts the long put; early assignment on the short call before ex-dividend; the monthly call credits may not cover the put's annual cost in low-IV regimes.
strategies.margin_note: Long stock plus long put plus covered call: no margin beyond the stock; IRA-eligible; the short call is covered by the shares. Synthetic version (LEAPS call instead of stock) is a debit structure, also IRA-eligible.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: spot BTC cannot be posted as the covering asset on the options venue, so the collar is built with inverse options against BTC held as margin collateral (the long put pays out in BTC, whose USD value falls in the scenario it hedges - buy more notional or use USDC linear puts); longest puts are ~12-month quarterlies; monthly/weekly calls expire 08:00 UTC Fridays; no dividends and European settlement remove assignment risk. IBIT holders can run the exact US equity version.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: collar the futures with a deferred-month put and front-month calls (American exercise; SPAN margin nets the hedged position); 1256. GLD/SLV: equity-style collar on the shares; no dividends; GLD/SLV share gains are taxed as collectibles if held over a year, which a protective put may 'reset' under straddle rules - a tax question outside this scope. strategies.name: Long calendar (horizontal) spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Evaluated at the front expiry T1 (the far leg is still alive): P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S-K, 0) - D, where V_far is the Black-Scholes value of the far call with T2-T1 remaining at the IV then prevailing and D is the net debit. Tent-shaped: peak at S = K, floor at -D far from K. Put version identical with max(K-S,0).
strategies.max_profit: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - D, reached at S = K on the front expiry; depends on the IV at T1 so it is not known in advance (Fidelity, Options Playbook).
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), when S is far from K at T1 so both calls trade near parity/zero and the spread collapses; holding the far leg past T1 cannot lose more than D in total but adds a naked long-option bleed.
strategies.breakevens: Two roots S* of V_far(S*, T2-T1) - max(S*-K, 0) = D, one above and one below K; approximate (depend on IV at T1), roughly K +/- (V_far(K) - D) scaled by the far leg's delta.

greeks_at_inception.delta: ~0 at the forward ATM strike (slightly positive for a spot-ATM call calendar because the far call's delta exceeds the near's)
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative near K (near-leg gamma > far-leg gamma)
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive while S is near K; turns negative once S moves far from K
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (far-leg vega > near-leg vega; Fidelity: 'slightly positive, close to zero' at 28/56 DTE, larger with wider expiry gap)

strategies.when_to_use: Neutral forecast around K with low absolute IV expected to rise (tastylive), or when the front IV is rich relative to the back (flat/inverted term structure sells the front at a premium). Johnson (JFQA 2017) shows the slope of the VIX term structure prices variance risk rather than predicting VIX, so a steep contango argues against the long calendar (you are buying the rich back month) and for its reverse.
strategies.risks: Large move either way loses the debit; a fall in IV hurts (long vega); early assignment on the short near leg before an ex-dividend date leaves short stock (Fidelity); pin risk at the front expiry; after T1 the position is a naked long option with its own theta bleed unless re-sold (campaign) or closed.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full; no additional margin while the long leg's expiry is later than or equal to the short's (Options Playbook). IRA-eligible. Brokers treat it as a defined-risk spread until the front expires.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit options are European and cash-settled at a 30-minute TWAP delivery price (public/get_delivery_prices), all expiring 08:00 UTC Fridays with daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly settlement_period values from public/get_instruments; the debit and P&L of an inverse calendar are in BTC/ETH, so the premium itself carries coin exposure. No dividends, so no ex-div assignment problem; 24/7 trading means weekend theta is real and the front leg decays through weekends. Standard margin margins each short option on its own (calendar offsets are recognised only under Portfolio Margin), so the trade ties up more collateral than on a US equity broker. DVOL is 30-day only; the term-structure slope must be built from chain mark_iv (get_book_summary_by_currency kind=option).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: American-style options on futures where each expiry's underlying is a different futures month, so a 'calendar' also contains the futures spread (gold contango ~ rate - lease rate); premium paid up front with SPAN margin on the short and spread recognition; Section 1256 contracts (26 USC 1256(b)) with 60/40 and year-end mark-to-market. GLD/SLV: the equity-option route, weeklies available, physical delivery of ETF shares, no dividends (no ex-div assignment risk); GLD/SLV options are equity options (not 1256). strategies.name: Long diagonal spread (bullish call / bearish put)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1 with K1 < K2: P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S-K2, 0) - D. Rises with S up to K2, then flattens at roughly (K2-K1) + remaining far extrinsic - D; floor approaches -D as S collapses.
strategies.max_profit: Approximately (K2 - K1) + extrinsic_far(K2, T2-T1) - D, at S = K2 on the front expiry (tastylive: can exceed the strike width because the long leg keeps time value).
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), if the far call expires worthless with S <= K1; tastylive's guard: keep D <= 75% of (K2 - K1) so the trade cannot lose on an upside move.
strategies.breakevens: Lower: S* where V_far(S*, T2-T1) = D (roughly K1 + D - remaining extrinsic). No upper breakeven when D <= K2 - K1; if D > K2 - K1 the upside loses D - (K2 - K1) - extrinsic.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: slightly negative near K2, roughly neutral elsewhere
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive when the short's premium >= the long's extrinsic (tastylive setup rule); near zero otherwise

strategies.when_to_use: Moderately bullish (calls) or bearish (puts) with elevated near-term IV (event week) or a flat/inverted term structure, when the trader wants a vertical with positive theta and long vega; a two-step forecast (first neutral-to-K2, then higher) suits it better than a plain vertical.
strategies.risks: IV collapse hurts the far leg; a sharp rally through K2 early caps gains while the far leg's extrinsic shrinks; early assignment on the short when ITM before ex-div; rolling the short up/out for a debit can push the total debit past the strike width (tastylive warns against this); tastylive never trades diagonals on volatility products (VIX) because each expiry is its own underlying.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread: pay D in full; brokers require the long expiry >= short expiry and usually the long strike no further OTM than the short for defined-risk treatment; otherwise the short is margined naked.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: strikes are listed in fixed USD steps and both legs settle 08:00 UTC Fridays; inverse premium means the ITM long's cost in BTC rises as BTC falls (negative convexity on the premium itself). No dividends so no assignment risk; 24/7 so the short near leg decays through weekends. Standard margin does not net the long against the short; Portfolio Margin does. BTC skew is often positive on calls, so call diagonals can be relatively expensive (reverse of SPY).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: the far long and near short reference different futures months; American exercise on the short into a futures position; SPAN recognises the diagonal as a spread with reduced margin; 1256 60/40. GLD/SLV: equity options with weeklies, ideal for 7-DTE short vs 60-DTE long diagonals; SLV's upside call skew makes put diagonals cheaper than call diagonals.
