strategies.name: Poor man's covered call (PMCC / LEAPS diagonal)

legs.expiry_rule: far: 365 DTE (LEAPS, 1-2 years; replace at ~90 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At each short expiry T1 with K1 < K2: P&L(S) = V_leaps(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - max(S-K2, 0) + sum of credits collected - P_leaps. Shape of a covered call whose 'stock' is the LEAPS: rises with S to K2, flat beyond, falls toward -(P_leaps - credits) as S drops below K1.
strategies.max_profit: Per cycle at S = K2 on the short expiry: (K2 - K1) + extrinsic_leaps(K2, T2-T1) - D, where D = P_leaps - C_short; over the LEAPS life, bounded by (K2 - K1) + total credits - P_leaps if every short expires at K2.
strategies.max_loss: D = P_leaps - C_short (net debit) if S <= K1 at the LEAPS expiry with all shorts expired OTM; the LEAPS cost is ~20-35% of the stock price for a 0.80-delta strike (Options Playbook: 20%+ ITM, delta >= 0.80).
strategies.breakevens: On a short expiry: S* where V_leaps(S*, T2-T1) = D (roughly K1 + D - remaining LEAPS extrinsic); at LEAPS expiry: K1 + P_leaps - total credits. Entry guards: short premium >= LEAPS extrinsic (tastylive diagonal rule) and (K2 - K1) + C_short > D so an upside blow-through still closes at a profit.

greeks_at_inception.theta: near zero to positive: the short's theta usually exceeds the slow LEAPS decay, but the LEAPS still erodes several dollars a year if the stock is flat
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (LEAPS vega far exceeds the short's) - a long-vega covered call, the opposite of the stock-based covered call

strategies.when_to_use: Capital-efficient covered call on a bullish-to-neutral view; best when long-dated IV is low (cheap LEAPS) and front IV is relatively rich; a term-structure trade in theta per day (sell fast-decaying front extrinsic against slow-decaying LEAPS extrinsic).
strategies.risks: IV collapse deflates the LEAPS even if the stock is flat (Options Playbook); the short caps the upside so it lags stock in a strong rally; assignment on the short leaves short stock, and exercising the LEAPS to cover forfeits its extrinsic (goal is for the short to expire OTM); no dividends; Options Playbook: roll the short before it is ~2-4% ITM; rolling for a debit can push the total debit past the strike width (tastylive).
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full; treated as a diagonal spread (defined risk) and IRA-eligible when the long expiry is later than the short's; no stock-level margin needed.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists quarterly options out to roughly 12 months, so the 'LEAPS' is the furthest quarterly; inverse premium means the deep-ITM long's BTC cost rises as BTC falls; no dividends so no ex-div assignment; European settlement at 08:00 UTC removes early assignment entirely; standard margin does not net the short against the long, so Portfolio Margin is needed for PMCC to be capital-efficient; weekend theta on the front short is a plus for the seller. IBIT options (US-listed, American) give the dividend-free equity-style route with the same mechanics as SPY.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: long-dated options on deferred futures months (liquidity thins beyond ~6-9 months), American exercise, SPAN spread margin, 1256 60/40 - note the long and short reference different futures contracts so the structure carries the gold forward curve. GLD/SLV: LEAPS exist out to ~2 years, no dividends, so the PMCC transfers cleanly; GLD/SLV options are equity options (not 1256). strategies.name: Ratio (vega-weighted) calendar spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1 with n near shorts per far long (n ~ sqrt(T2/T1) ~ 1.7 for vega neutrality; 2:1 in practice): P&L(S) = V_far(S, T2-T1) - n*max(S-K, 0) - D (D may be a credit). Tent peaked at K, falls off faster on the upside because n-1 short calls are uncovered.
strategies.max_profit: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - D at S = K on the front expiry (plus the credit if the structure was entered for a credit).
strategies.max_loss: Downside: D (or zero if entered for a credit). Upside: grows without bound before T1 as (n-1)*(S-K) exceeds the far call's gain; if the structure survives to T1 and the far call is kept, the uncovered shorts have expired, so the loss realised at T1 is roughly (n-1)*(S-K) - extrinsic_far(S) + D for S well above K.
strategies.breakevens: Lower: root of V_far(S, T2-T1) = D (none if credit). Upper: root of n*(S-K) - V_far(S, T2-T1) = -D (or +C).

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative for the call version (n*0.5 short vs 0.5 long); positive for the put version
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive and large (n near-legs of theta)
greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 by construction when n = vega_far/vega_near ~ sqrt(T2/T1); otherwise negative for n above that

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest front-month theta while staying flat to parallel IV shifts, i.e. express 'front realised < front implied' without a bet on the IV level; attractive when the term structure is flat or inverted (front rich). The theta-weighted version (n < 1, long 2 far / short 1 near) is a positive-vega, positive-gamma-at-the-back long-vol structure.
strategies.risks: Uncovered shorts: a gap through K before T1 loses many multiples of the credit; vega neutrality holds only for parallel shifts (a vol spike steepens the front, hurting more than the model says); pin and assignment risk on n short options; brokers margin the excess shorts as naked.
strategies.margin_note: The n-1 excess short options are margined as naked (Reg T ~20% of underlying each; portfolio margin much less on SPX); not permitted in most IRAs; the 1:1 portion is a calendar spread.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit standard margin charges the shorts individually (no calendar offset), so the ratio structure is collateral-heavy outside Portfolio Margin; min_trade_amount lets BTC options trade in 0.1-contract steps, so the sqrt(T2/T1) ratio can be set precisely (1.7:1) rather than rounded to 2:1; 24/7 gaps make the uncovered front shorts riskier than on SPY.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: SPAN margins the uncovered short options against the futures scan range; the near and far legs reference different futures months; 1256. GLD/SLV: equity-option naked margin on the excess shorts. CME spec pages unreachable this session (503).

strategies.name: Rolling a short option (out / up / down)

legs.expiry_rule: near: 21 DTE (buy to close the existing short)
far: next monthly, ~45-50 DTE (sell to open)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: The roll itself is a calendar/diagonal trade whose cash flow is delta-premium = Prem(K2, T2) - Prem(K1, T1) (a credit when positive). The rolled position's payoff at T2 is that of the new short: for a call, cumulative net credits - max(S - K2, 0); for a put, cumulative net credits - max(K2 - S, 0). Roll out: K2 = K1 (time only); roll up/down: K2 above/below K1 in the same expiry (a vertical); roll out-and-up/down: both (a diagonal). Rolling in: moving the strike closer to spot (tastylive).
strategies.max_profit: Sum of all net credits collected across rolls (if the final short expires OTM).
strategies.max_loss: Call: unbounded (naked) or capped by the shares in a covered call; put: K2 - cumulative net credits. Rolling adjusts risk without removing it.
strategies.breakevens: Call: K2 + cumulative net credits; put: K2 - cumulative net credits; each credit roll moves the breakeven further from spot, each debit roll closer.

greeks_at_inception.delta: reduced in magnitude after the roll (strike moved away from spot) - the point of rolling a tested short
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative, smaller after moving out in time
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive, restored by the new extrinsic
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative, larger after moving to the longer expiry

strategies.when_to_use: Defend a tested short option (roll out, or out-and-away, for a credit) to re-centre the breakeven and buy time; roll an untested strangle side in toward spot to collect premium; roll a covered call up and out when the stock rallies through the strike (Options Playbook: before it is 2-4% ITM); roll winners at 21 DTE to the next cycle to avoid gamma risk (tastylive's 21-DTE study).
strategies.risks: Rolling for a debit adds risk without new premium; repeated rolls of a losing short can accumulate a large undefined loss and tie up margin for months; rolling a defined-risk spread can push the debit past the width (tastylive); early assignment can pre-empt the roll; a roll is two fills of slippage.
strategies.margin_note: Naked shorts remain margined as naked; covered calls remain covered; rolling out in time usually raises margin (more extrinsic, longer expiry) under Reg T; portfolio margin is more forgiving.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: all expiries are Fridays 08:00 UTC, so rolls are from one Friday to a later Friday; European settlement means no early assignment to pre-empt a roll; inverse premium credits are in BTC; 24/7 trading lets a tested short be rolled on a weekend gap (liquidity thinner); the roll's two legs are margined separately under standard margin, so a credit roll can still raise collateral.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: rolling out in time usually means rolling to an option on a different futures month (the futures spread moves the effective strike); American exercise can assign a deep-ITM short early; SPAN margin; 1256. GLD/SLV: equity-style rolls with weeklies for fine-grained timing. CME pages unreachable this session (503).

strategies.name: Short (reverse) calendar spread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = C + max(S-K, 0) - V_far(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1), where C is the net credit. Inverted tent: trough at S = K, approaches +C when S is far from K.
strategies.max_profit: C (net credit), when S finishes far above or below K at T1 so both calls are near parity/zero and the spread's value approaches zero (Fidelity).
strategies.max_loss: V_far(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - C at S = K on the front expiry (depends on IV then); becomes unlimited if the long near call expires and the short far call is left open naked.
strategies.breakevens: Two roots of V_far(S*, T2-T1) - max(S*-K, 0) = C, one above and one below K; rising IV widens them (Fidelity).

greeks_at_inception.delta: ~0 (slightly negative for a spot-ATM call version)
greeks_at_inception.theta: negative near K (the near long decays fastest); slightly positive once S is far from K

strategies.when_to_use: Expect a large move in either direction before T1, or a flattening/inversion of the term structure (front IV rising relative to back); steep contango where the far variance carries a large premium (Johnson: slope reflects variance risk premia) makes the short far leg the richer sale. Cheaper than a long straddle for the same big-move view (Fidelity).
strategies.risks: The stock sits at K and IV falls: loss approaches the far call's full time value; once the near leg expires the short far call is naked with unlimited risk; early assignment on the short far call near ex-dividend; broker margin on the far short jumps when the near leg expires.
strategies.margin_note: Fidelity: needs less capital than long straddles/strangles but risk is 100% of committed capital; most brokers margin the far short as a naked option (or require the spread to be closed) once the near long expires, and several do not permit it in IRAs.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the short far option is margined individually under standard margin (no offset from the near long except in Portfolio Margin), so the credit received in BTC is small relative to collateral; the credit is coin-denominated. Big-move thesis fits BTC's fat tails and 24/7 gaps; expiries 08:00 UTC Fridays, cash-settled at TWAP, so the near long settles to cash and leaves the far short naked automatically at 08:00 UTC unless closed. Build the BTC term structure from chain mark IVs (DVOL is 30-day only).
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI options on futures: the far short settles into a different futures month than the near long, so after T1 you are short an American-style option on a different contract with futures-style SPAN margin; metals term structure is usually mildly upward sloping (contango), so selling the back carries both the vol premium and the futures carry. 1256 treatment on GC/SI; GLD/SLV equity options are not 1256. strategies.name: Straddle calendar (time spread of straddles / forward-vol trade)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the front expiry T1: P&L(S) = V_far_straddle(S, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - |S - K| - D. A tent peaked at K whose height is the far straddle's time value; the economic exposure is forward volatility between T1 and T2, FV^2 = (T2*sigma_T2^2 - T1*sigma_T1^2)/(T2-T1).
strategies.max_profit: V_far_straddle(K, T2-T1; sigma_T1) - D at S = K on the front expiry; grows with the IV then prevailing.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit): a large move makes the near straddle's intrinsic cancel the far straddle's value gain, leaving only the lost time value.
strategies.breakevens: K +/- x where x solves V_far_straddle(K +/- x, T2-T1) - x = D; approximately the far straddle's remaining time value at the breakeven minus the debit.

greeks_at_inception.vega: positive to parallel IV shifts (far vega ~ sqrt(93/30) of near vega); vega-neutral only if sized by the vega ratio (see ratio calendar); long forward volatility

strategies.when_to_use: Long version: when forward implied volatility between 30 and 93 days is low relative to expected realised volatility over that window, or when a vol shock is expected after T1. Reverse version (short far / long near, delta-hedged): to harvest a forward variance risk premium when forward implied exceeds subsequently realised variance.
strategies.risks: Realised move before T1 larger than the near straddle's premium; IV collapse hurts the long version; pin risk at K; early assignment on the short near legs (puts on ex-div, calls before ex-div); the reverse version is short far vega and loses in a vol spike that outlasts the near long.
strategies.margin_note: Long version: debit paid, defined risk, IRA-eligible. Reverse version: the far short straddle is margined as a naked straddle once the near expires; SPX in portfolio margin is far cheaper than SPY under Reg T.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists weekly, monthly and quarterly expiries so a 30/90-day straddle calendar maps onto the monthly vs quarterly 08:00 UTC Fridays; inverse premium means the straddle debit is in BTC and the P&L of a USD-notional view is distorted by BTC's own move (hedge with a small perpetual position or use USDC linear options). DVOL gives only the 30-day point, so forward vol must be computed from the chain's monthly and quarterly ATM mark_iv; realised vol via public/get_historical_volatility.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: the two straddles reference different futures months, so the 'forward vol' trade also carries the futures spread and the two months' different realised vol; SPAN spread credit; 1256. GLD/SLV: cleanest route for a pure forward-vol expression on gold; GVZ (CBOE gold vol index) provides a 30-day point but no 3-month analog. strategies.name: Theta ladder (staggered-expiry short premium)

legs.expiry_rule: 24 DTE (rung 4; next to exit at 21 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Sum of the rungs' payoffs: P&L = sum_i [c_i - max(K_i - S_i, 0)] where each rung i has its own strike K_i (set at entry) and expiry; one new rung is sold each week at 45 DTE and each rung is closed at 21 DTE or at 50% of its credit, so the book always holds four rungs spanning 24-45 DTE.
strategies.max_profit: Sum of the four credits (or half of each under the 50% rule).
strategies.max_loss: Sum over rungs of (K_i - c_i) if every put is assigned at zero - four times a single rung's risk at a quarter of the size each, so equal to one full-size short put's risk; the ladder changes the path, not the total notional.
strategies.breakevens: Per rung K_i - c_i; the aggregate breakeven is a size-weighted blend of strikes set on four different weeks.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative, spread across four DTEs so the gamma peak of any one expiry is a quarter of a single-expiry book
greeks_at_inception.theta: positive and smoother through time (a rung is always in the fast-decay zone)

strategies.when_to_use: Smooth the path dependence and roll-date risk of monthly premium selling; keep capital continuously deployed; always have a rung near the 21-DTE exit so the book is never all-in at one gamma level. Also applies to laddered covered calls, laddered calendars and laddered LEAPS rolls.
strategies.risks: Same total tail risk as the single entry (a crash hits all rungs); four times the fills and management; strikes set on different weeks can cluster below spot after a rally (all rungs tested together); correlation of rungs is near 1 in a sell-off, so diversification is in timing only.
strategies.margin_note: Each rung margined as a naked (or cash-secured) put; the total margin equals one full-size position; portfolio margin recognises the common underlying.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists weekly expiries every Friday 08:00 UTC, so a four-rung weekly ladder maps exactly onto consecutive Fridays; credits in BTC; standard margin sums the rungs; 24/7 theta accrues on all rungs through weekends; DVOL-sized strikes.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: weekly options (Friday, plus Monday/Wednesday weeklies) make a weekly ladder possible on the active futures month; SPAN margin; 1256. GLD/SLV: weeklies available for the equity-option ladder. CME pages unreachable this session (503); weekly-option listing details from training knowledge.

legs.expiry_rule: 45 DTE; exit at 50% of credit or at 21 DTE
45 DTE; exit at 50% of credit or at 21 DTE

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Held to expiry: P&L(S) = C - max(Kp - S, 0) - max(S - Kc, 0). The strategy's defining feature is the exit rule, which truncates the path before the gamma-heavy last three weeks: the 45-DTE entry sits where theta per unit of gamma is highest and the 21-DTE exit removes the period where most of the P&L volatility arrives.
strategies.max_profit: C (full credit) if held to expiry with Kp < S < Kc; 0.5*C under the 50% rule; the realised credit at 21 DTE under the time rule.
strategies.max_loss: Downside: Kp - C; upside: unbounded (naked call) - defined-risk variants (iron condor) cap it at width - C.
strategies.breakevens: Kp - C and Kc + C at expiry; before expiry the exit rules make the realised breakeven path-dependent.

strategies.when_to_use: Systematic premium selling when IV rank is elevated and the term structure is in contango (see the regime-filter entry); tastylive's studies report that for 45-DTE 1SD SPY strangles, exiting at 21 DTE gave the highest return and lowest volatility, and 50% management beat holding to expiration; 25% targets for straddles, 10-50% for calendars/diagonals/iron flies (tastylive).
strategies.risks: Tail risk: a gap beyond a strike can lose many times the credit before any exit rule triggers; the studies are tastylive's own simulations (no sample period, no CIs); early assignment; the 50% target shrinks absolute profit while leaving absolute risk; capital drag from margin.

strategies.name: VIX futures / VIX options calendar (term-structure roll trade)

legs.expiry_rule: near: M1, Wednesday 30 days before the SPX monthly expiry

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At M1 settlement (SOQ of VIX, $1000 per point): P&L = (F1_0 - SOQ) + (F2_T - F2_0) = change in the M2 - M1 spread. In contango both futures roll down toward spot VIX as time passes, the front faster, so the spread narrows and the position earns the roll; in a vol spike M1 rises more than M2 (its beta to VIX is higher) and the position loses. VIX options variant: a long VIX call calendar, remembering each VIX option expiry is priced off its own VX future, not spot VIX.
strategies.max_profit: Bounded in practice by the initial M2 - M1 spread plus any further steepening; theoretically unbounded if M2 rallies while M1 settles low.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded in principle: a spike that lifts M1 far more than M2 (front beta to VIX ~1.5-2x the second month's). Historical worst days are many multiples of the mean daily roll gain.
strategies.breakevens: The spread (F2 - F1) at exit equals the spread at entry: P&L = 0 when the slope is unchanged.

greeks_at_inception.delta: negative to VIX (short the higher-beta front)
greeks_at_inception.vega: short front-month variance, long second-month variance

strategies.when_to_use: Contango with M2/M1 >= 1.05 and VIX below its 1-year median; exit or reverse when VIX/VIX3M >= 1 (regime filter). The reverse (long M1 / short M2) is a cheap crash hedge in steep contango only if the carry cost is tolerable. Johnson's SLOPE factor documents the premium being harvested.
strategies.risks: Vol spikes (Feb 2018, Mar 2020) produce losses far beyond the accumulated roll; margin calls on the short front; the spread's beta changes sign near expiry; futures are $1000 per point (XSP-sized retail cannot scale down; use VIX options or ETPs); Wednesday-morning SOQ settlement risk.
strategies.margin_note: CFE/clearing margin on a VX calendar spread is a fraction of the outright futures margin (spread credit), but spikes have produced intraday margin calls; VIX futures are 1256 contracts (regulated futures). ETP routes (short VXX/UVXY vs long VIXM) carry financing and borrow costs instead.

strategies.name: VIX term-structure regime filter (VIX3M/VIX gate for premium selling)

legs.expiry_rule: 45 DTE; entered only when VIX/VIX3M < 1 (contango); flat or long-vol when >= 1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: The gated position is a standard short strangle, P&L(S) = C - max(Kp - S, 0) - max(S - Kc, 0); the strategy is the gate. Regime: VIX/VIX3M < 1 is contango (normal; 1-month implied below 3-month), >= 1 is backwardation (stress). Johnson (JFQA 2017) finds the term structure's slope prices variance risk (predicts returns of variance swaps, VIX futures and SPX straddles) rather than forecasting VIX, which is the rationale for using the slope as a premium-selling gate. VIX3M (ex-VXV) is the 93-day analogue of VIX, daily since 2007-12-04, free from CBOE (VIX3M_History.csv) and FRED (VXVCLS).
strategies.max_profit: C per gated entry.
strategies.max_loss: Downside Kp - C; upside unbounded (the gate reduces frequency of stress entries, not the tail of any single entry).

greeks_at_inception.vega: negative - and the gate's purpose is to avoid holding this when the term structure says variance is being repriced

strategies.when_to_use: As the entry/exit switch for every short-theta strategy in this family (calendars, theta harvesting, ladders, VX calendars): sell premium in contango, stand aside or flip to long calendars / long VIX call spreads in backwardation. Mandel's registry already tests whether backwardation predicts a VIX decline (vix-term-structure-reversion); this entry tests whether the regime conditions strategy P&L.
strategies.risks: The ratio is a slow signal (it flips after the first leg of a sell-off); contango persists through gradual bear markets; thresholds invite overfitting (deflate); the 2008 and 2020 episodes dominate the backwardation sample; the gate does not shorten the tail of a single entry.
strategies.margin_note: Inherits the gated position's margin; in backwardation the alternative long structures are debit trades.

strategies.name: ZEBRA (zero extrinsic back ratio)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: P&L(S) = 2*max(S - K1, 0) - max(S - K2, 0) - D with K1 < K2 ~ spot. For S >= K2: S - (2*K1 - K2) - D (slope 1, stock-like); for K1 < S < K2: 2*(S - K1) - D (slope 2); for S <= K1: -D. Strikes are chosen so the short ATM premium offsets the two longs' extrinsic (tastylive: long extrinsic ~ half the ATM premium), leaving net extrinsic near zero.
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited: S - (2*K1 - K2) - D for S above K2.
strategies.max_loss: D (the debit), if S <= K1 at expiry; D ~ 2*(S0 - K1) + net extrinsic, i.e. roughly 20-30% of the stock price for 0.70-delta longs (tastylive).
strategies.breakevens: S* = 2*K1 - K2 + D ~ K2 + net extrinsic paid (tastylive: short strike plus extrinsic paid); put ZEBRA: short put strike minus extrinsic paid.

greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 (zero net extrinsic means almost no time decay to pay)
greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 (same cancellation); becomes positive as S rises away from K2

strategies.when_to_use: Stock replacement with full (100) delta at a fraction of the capital, a hard floor at the debit and no extrinsic bleed; unlike a single deep-ITM LEAPS it does not pay financing-like extrinsic, and unlike the PMCC it is not capped. Shorter expiries have lower debits and strikes nearer spot; longer expiries give more time and (for 365 DTE) long-term treatment (tastylive). On SPY, call skew makes call ZEBRAs costlier than put ZEBRAs (tastylive).
strategies.risks: Loses the whole debit on a move below K1 by expiry; between K1 and K2 the slope is 2 (over-exposed on the way down toward K1); the short ATM call can be assigned early before ex-dividend; rolling before expiry re-exposes the trader to extrinsic; slippage on three legs.
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full (the two longs cover the short); defined risk; IRA-eligible; no stock margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse options: the debit is in BTC, so a BTC call ZEBRA's floor is a fixed number of coins whose USD value falls with BTC (the floor is softer in USD terms); use USDC linear options for a USD-floor ZEBRA; European settlement removes assignment risk; BTC's call skew makes call ZEBRAs relatively expensive, like SPY. min_trade_amount steps allow fractional ratios (e.g. 1.8:1) to fine-tune zero extrinsic.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI: 2:1 structures on a single futures month settle into futures (American exercise; the short ATM call may be exercised against you into a short future late in life); SPAN margin on the net position is small; 1256 60/40. GLD/SLV: equity-option ZEBRA; SLV's call skew makes put ZEBRAs cheaper there too. CME pages unreachable this session (503).
