Long straddle (expensive, pays regardless of mode)
Iron condor if delay expected
Risk reversal (long call / short put) when independent approval probability > implied
Pair with Polymarket/Kalshi binary contract to hedge the mode and keep only the magnitude bet
strategies.claim: For FDA PDUFA decisions, the option-implied magnitude of the move (strangle-implied |move| conditional on a decision) is smaller than the realised |move| on decision days for small-cap biotechs, so a 25%/45% asymmetric strangle bought 5 days before and sold at the open after the decision has positive mean return on debit, excluding delayed decisions.

trial.statistic: Mean return on debit (decisions only) and including delays; hit rate; bootstrap CI; implied vs realised probability calibration of the bimodal model.
trial.procedure: Build PDUFA calendar (FDA/biotech calendars, free), chain captures for the strangle marks, daily OHLC for the move; decompose into decided vs delayed; walk-forward on the implied-probability filter.
trial.data: PDUFA/ruling calendar; chain captures; single-name OHLC; Polymarket/Kalshi odds where listed.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with CI excluding 0 including delays; calibration slope of implied vs realised probability between 0.7 and 1.3.
trial.controls: Random biotech non-event windows; market-adjusted moves (vs XBI); exclude large-cap pharma.

strategies.blocked_on: PDUFA calendar history + chain captures across >= 80 decisions (roughly 12 months).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Bimodal implied-distribution fitter (two-point mixture) from the chain; comparator with Polymarket/Kalshi odds.

strategies.name: Crypto macro-event straddle on Deribit (FOMC / CPI) - DVOL vs realised

legs.strike_rule: ATM (nearest listed USD strike to the Deribit index); flip to LONG when DVOL-implied event move < trailing realised FOMC-day move
legs.expiry_rule: BTC/ETH daily option expiring 08:00 UTC the morning after the 14:00 ET FOMC statement (≈ 18h), or the weekly containing it

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Inverse: payoff in BTC = max(S_T-K,0)/S_T for the call, max(K-S_T,0)/S_T for the put; USD P&L ≈ Cr_usd - |S_T-K| but the put side's USD value is damped by the falling S_T (concave). Settlement at the 30-minute TWAP of the Deribit index before 08:00 UTC.
strategies.max_profit: Short: Cr (in BTC, convert at S_T). Long: unbounded (call, in USD terms; in BTC terms bounded at 1 BTC per contract), K-D (put).
strategies.max_loss: Short: unbounded upside in USD; downside bounded at K-Cr in USD (and at 1 BTC per contract in coin). Long: D.
strategies.breakevens: K ± premium (USD-equivalent); adjust for inverse convexity.

greeks_at_inception.delta: ≈0 in BTC terms; inverse contracts carry extra short-BTC exposure for a USD-neutral book (hedge ≈ premium/S in perp)

strategies.when_to_use: Scheduled macro releases (FOMC, CPI, NFP) that move BTC/ETH: compute event-implied move from the daily straddle (or DVOL/sqrt(365)*sqrt(h/24)); compare to the trailing 12 same-event realised moves from the Deribit index; sell when implied/realised > 1.2, buy when < 0.8. 24/7 trading means the 14:00 ET statement is tradable live; options expire 08:00 UTC only.
strategies.risks: Deribit liquidation engine (no broker call); inverse payoff asymmetry; crypto-specific shocks (exchange failures, ETF flow prints) can coincide with the macro date; daily-option book is thin outside BTC/ETH ATM; fees per leg 0.03% of notional (capped at 12.5% of premium) are large for short-dated options; funding on any perp hedge.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit margin in coin: short option initial margin ≈ max(0.15 - OTM%, 0.1)*S + mark; portfolio margin available. US persons cannot legally access Deribit; US-regulated routes are CME BTC/ETH options (futures-style, 1256) or IBIT options (equity-style). No 1256 for IBIT.
strategies.crypto_notes: Core entry for the family. DVOL (Deribit 30-day BTC IV index) history is reachable via public/get_volatility_index_data (1D candles; ~1000 days), realised from BTC daily closes; expiries settlement_period day/week/month. ETF route: IBIT options on CBOE/NYSE (US), expiries Fri, equity-style margin, no 24/7.
strategies.metals_notes: Same event list as gold; run the two side by side to test whether BTC behaves as a macro asset (correlated event moves with GC) or not.
variants: Short daily straddle (described)
Long weekly straddle bought 24h before
Strangle at ±1 implied move
IBIT weekly straddle (US-regulated route, Friday expiry)
CME BTC option straddle (1256)
strategies.claim: The BTC close-to-close absolute return on FOMC decision days, as a fraction of the DVOL-implied one-day move (DVOL/sqrt(365)), is lower than on non-FOMC days, i.e. BTC event vol is overpriced on FOMC days and a short ATM straddle priced with DVOL-as-IV has positive mean return on those days.

trial.statistic: Mean of |r_T|/(DVOL_{T-1}/sqrt(365)) on FOMC days vs all days; mean P&L of a BS straddle (IV = DVOL, T = 1/365) sold at T-1 close; bootstrap CIs.
trial.null: Ratio on FOMC days >= ratio on other days; straddle P&L <= 0.
trial.procedure: Pull DVOL 1D candles (reachable now, ~1000 days), BTC daily closes, FOMC dates (≈ 22 events in window); compute statistics; because n is small, also pool CPI and NFP dates (≈ 70 events) as 'macro days' and report both.
trial.data: Deribit DVOL history (public API), BTC daily closes, FOMC/CPI/NFP calendars.
trial.pass: Pooled macro-day straddle P&L > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 and ratio difference < 0 with CI excluding 0; FOMC-only result reported as indicative until n >= 60.
trial.controls: Random non-macro days; weekend exclusion; VIX-regime control; check the inverse-payoff USD vs BTC accounting gives the same sign.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse the BTC VRP harness (DVOL vs realised) with an event-date mask; add inverse-option payoff mode to the payoff engine (payoff/S_T).

strategies.name: Crypto scheduled-catalyst strangle (ETF decisions, halving, protocol upgrades)

legs.expiry_rule: first weekly/monthly expiry AFTER the scheduled date, bought 2-4 weeks before

legs.strike_rule: OTM 10% (≈25-delta); for USD-neutral payoff buy ≈1.2x put quantity to offset inverse concavity

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-Kc,0)/S_T + 1.2*max(Kp-S_T,0)/S_T in BTC, minus D; USD ≈ max(S_T-Kc,0) + 1.2*max(Kp-S_T,0) - D_usd. Usually closed at the decision (sell the vol ramp) or the day after (hold-through).
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded upside (USD) / Kp-weighted downside.
strategies.max_loss: D if Kp <= S_T <= Kc.

greeks_at_inception.delta: ≈0 (slightly positive in BTC terms, offset by the extra put)
greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (the IV ramp into the catalyst is the primary driver)

strategies.when_to_use: Hard-dated binary catalysts: SEC ETF decision deadlines (spot BTC Jan 2024, spot ETH May 2024, altcoin ETF deadlines), Bitcoin halving (≈ every 4 years, block-height determined), Ethereum upgrades, large token unlocks, Mt Gox/FTX distribution dates. Buy when the event-expiry IV premium over DVOL is below its level at comparable past catalysts; sell before the decision (ramp) or hold through (move).
strategies.risks: Deadline slippage (SEC can delay) leaves you holding decaying premium; 'sell the news' means the realised move can be in the direction opposite to the sentiment and then reverse within the same day; very few comparable events (n in single digits), so this is a judgement trade with option-defined risk, not a statistically validated one yet.
strategies.margin_note: Debit only on Deribit; US-regulated route via IBIT/ETHA options or CME options.
strategies.crypto_notes: Core crypto entry. Inverse settlement: profits on puts are paid in a coin that has fallen; over-buy puts (described) or hedge with a short perp. Weekly expiries 08:00 UTC Fridays; monthlies last Friday. Fees capped at 12.5% of premium matter for far-OTM wings.
strategies.metals_notes: Analogue: hard-dated events for gold are policy (FOMC) and data, covered by the metals entry; no supply-schedule event like a halving.
variants: Sell-the-ramp (close before decision)
Hold-through (close day after)
Call-only ramp (bullish catalyst, e.g. ETF approval odds rising on Polymarket)
Short strangle after approval (post-event crush)
Calendar: long event expiry / short prior weekly
strategies.claim: For hard-dated crypto catalysts, the BTC/ETH event-expiry IV rises relative to DVOL over the 3 weeks into the date (ramp), so a 25-delta strangle bought 21 days before and sold 1 day before has positive mean return on debit; this cannot be validated before chain history spans >= 20 such events.

trial.statistic: Mean return on debit; mean dIV(event expiry) - dDVOL over the window; bootstrap CI (small n: report exact sign test as well).
trial.procedure: Record event-expiry ATM IV and DVOL daily from the Deribit public book (capture starts now); for each scheduled catalyst compute the window statistics; cross-check with Polymarket odds for the event as a proxy for information arrival.
trial.data: Deribit book captures (mark IV by expiry), DVOL, catalyst calendar (SEC deadlines, upgrade dates), Polymarket event odds.
trial.pass: Sign test p < 0.05 and mean return > 0 with CI excluding 0 when n >= 20.
trial.controls: Non-catalyst 21-day windows; DVOL-only control (does ambient vol explain the ramp?); separate ETF-type vs protocol-type events.

strategies.blocked_on: Deribit book capture by expiry across >= 20 hard-dated catalysts (years of history at current event frequency; partial evidence after 3-5 events).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Catalyst calendar table joined to Deribit expiry-level IV captures and Polymarket odds; report IV ramp per event.

strategies.name: Deribit expiry max-pain pin (sell the 08:00 UTC settlement straddle)

legs.strike_rule: max-pain strike (strike minimising total option payout given OI) if within ±2% of spot, else ATM
legs.expiry_rule: BTC/ETH monthly or quarterly expiry (last Friday, 08:00 UTC), entered 00:00 UTC same day (8h to expiry)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - |S_T - K| (USD-equivalent; in BTC the payouts are |S_T-K|/S_T). S_T = 30-minute TWAP of the Deribit BTC index ending 08:00 UTC.
strategies.max_profit: Cr at S_T = K.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded upside (USD); K - Cr downside.
strategies.when_to_use: Large monthly/quarterly Deribit expiries (billions notional) where OI is concentrated and the 'max pain' narrative is widely followed; sell the straddle 8 hours before settlement when spot is within 2% of max pain. The 30-minute TWAP settlement mechanically damps the final move relative to a single print.
strategies.risks: Pinning is weak in crypto because dealers are a smaller share of OI than in SPX; weekend and Asian-session liquidity; an 08:00 UTC expiry coincides with European open flows; one 3% move in 8 hours costs several credits; liquidation on margin.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit coin margin; US persons use CME BTC options (expire 4pm London on last Friday) or IBIT monthly opex as the regulated analogue.
strategies.crypto_notes: Core entry. settlement_period 'month' instruments expire 08:00 UTC last Friday; weekly on Fridays; daily every day. Public API exposes OI per instrument for max-pain calculation (public/get_book_summary_by_currency).
strategies.metals_notes: COMEX OG expiry (four business days before month-end) is the metals analogue; GC pinning to $50/$100 strikes is anecdotal and untested here.
variants: Short straddle at max pain (described)
Iron butterfly with ±3% wings
Short daily straddle on every Friday weekly
Long straddle on non-pin (spot > 3% from max pain) expiries
IBIT monthly opex short straddle
strategies.claim: On Deribit monthly expiry days the BTC 00:00-08:00 UTC absolute return is smaller than on other Fridays' 00:00-08:00 UTC window, and the Deribit index at 08:00 UTC is closer to the max-pain strike than the 00:00 UTC spot was.

trial.statistic: Mean |return| in the 8h window, expiry Fridays vs other Fridays (permutation test); mean |S_08 - K_maxpain| vs |S_00 - K_maxpain| (paired).
trial.null: No difference in 8h move; no convergence toward max pain.
trial.procedure: BTC hourly closes (Deribit public/get_tradingview_chart_data, free) for the 8h windows since 2019; OI per strike at 00:00 UTC on expiry days from daily book captures (from today) for the max-pain leg.
trial.data: Deribit hourly index history (public), monthly expiry calendar, book captures for OI.
trial.pass: Permutation p < 0.05 for smaller 8h move; paired convergence > 0 with CI excluding 0 (once >= 12 expiries captured).
trial.controls: Other Fridays; weekly vs monthly split; exclude expiries coinciding with FOMC/CPI; test ETH separately.

strategies.blocked_on: the 8h-move half is testable now with Deribit hourly index data (public endpoint); the max-pain half needs ~12 months of OI captures.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Deribit hourly index fetcher + expiry calendar; max-pain calculator from book summary OI.

strategies.name: Dividend run-up and ex-dividend option plays

legs.strike_rule: ITM 5% (≈70-delta) - stock replacement for the run-up leg
legs.expiry_rule: expiry AFTER the ex-dividend date (20-45 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S-K1,0), K2-K1) - D. Normally closed at the close BEFORE the ex-date, capturing the run-up but not the ex-div drop (calls do not receive the dividend; the drop is priced into call premium).
strategies.max_profit: (K2-K1) - D at expiry; pre-ex-date exit ≈ delta*(run-up) - theta.
strategies.max_loss: D.
strategies.when_to_use: Between dividend declaration (or the predictable 'dividend month' for regular payers) and the ex-date, for stocks with high dividend yield (>3% annualised) where the documented pre-ex-date drift exists. Exit at the close before ex-date. Separate variant: dividend-capture arbitrage with deep-ITM calls (exercise the day before ex-date when the call's extrinsic value < dividend).
strategies.risks: The run-up anomaly is small (tens of bps) and transaction-cost sensitive; option bid/ask may exceed the edge; being short a call through ex-date risks early assignment (you lose the dividend); dividend cut/suspension announcements.
strategies.margin_note: Debit. For the exercise-arbitrage variant you need stock buying power to take delivery (100 shares per contract) for one night.
strategies.crypto_notes: No dividends. The analogue is staking-yield / airdrop snapshot dates: spot run-up into the snapshot and drop after; ETH options on Deribit do not embed staking yield directly (no carry adjustment), so forward pricing already differs from equities.
strategies.metals_notes: No dividends on GLD/SLV/GC. Not applicable; the carry analogue (contango roll on GC) is not event-driven.
variants: 70-delta call vs call spread vs synthetic long (long call + short put, both ATM)
Dividend-capture exercise arbitrage: buy deep ITM call T-2, exercise T-1 if extrinsic < dividend (needs assignment-day logistics)
Short put through ex-date (collects early-exercise premium embedded in puts)
Ex-date short straddle (stock drops by dividend; option prices already adjust - placebo for testing)
strategies.claim: For US stocks with trailing yield > 3%, the underlying's mean return from 10 trading days before the ex-date to the close before the ex-date exceeds the same stock's mean return in non-dividend windows, and a 70-delta call held over that window captures a positive mean return on debit after half-spread costs.

trial.statistic: Mean excess return (event window minus matched non-event window) for the underlying; mean return on debit for the call; bootstrap CIs.
trial.procedure: Build ex-date calendar; for each (stock, ex-date) compute underlying 10-day pre-ex return and matched control; option overlay: BS-price a 70-delta call with chain-captured IV (or VIX-scaled proxy) and mark at T-1.
trial.data: Ex-dividend dates (free: Nasdaq dividend calendar / EDGAR), single-name daily closes, chain captures for IV.
trial.pass: Underlying excess return > 0 with CI excluding 0 and call return > 0 after costs.
trial.controls: Placebo windows (same stocks, random dates); market-adjusted returns (subtract SPY); yield tercile monotonicity.

strategies.blocked_on: ex-dividend date history and single-name closes (free, not wired); chain capture for IV marks.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Event-drift harness with 'declaration-to-ex' and 'ex-to-pay' windows; add early-exercise check (extrinsic vs dividend) to the engine.

strategies.name: Earnings iron condor / iron butterfly (defined-risk IV crush)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - max(K2-S,0) + max(K1-S,0) - max(S-K3,0) + max(S-K4,0). Iron butterfly: K2=K3=ATM.
strategies.max_profit: Cr if K2<=S<=K3.
strategies.max_loss: (K2-K1) - Cr on the downside, (K4-K3) - Cr on the upside (equal widths assumed).
strategies.when_to_use: Same filter as the naked strangle (IM/HM > 1.2) but when the account cannot carry naked risk or the name has a history of >2x gaps; wings at 2x implied move cap the tail. Iron butterfly when IM is extremely rich and you want max credit.
strategies.risks: Defined loss but the loss is frequently the max (a 2x gap blows through the wing); four legs of bid/ask in illiquid names can eat half the credit; pin risk at K2/K3 on Friday if held; early exercise of short ITM leg around ex-div.
strategies.margin_note: Margin = max wing width - credit (Reg-T), same under portfolio margin; IRA-eligible at most brokers.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit iron condors in BTC/ETH weeklies; strikes in USD, premiums in coin; four legs of maker/taker fees (0.03%/0.03% of underlying notional capped at 12.5% of premium) matter more than on US equity options. Portfolio margin recognises the spread.
strategies.metals_notes: GC options iron condor around FOMC/NFP using weekly GC options; SPAN margin recognises the spread; GLD iron condor is the equity-option route.
variants: Iron condor at 1x/2x IM
Iron butterfly (ATM body)
Broken-wing condor (wider call wing for negative-skew names)
Unbalanced: 2 put spreads : 1 call spread when IM/HM is rich only on the downside
Hold to expiry vs cover at post-print open
strategies.claim: An iron condor with shorts at 1x implied move and longs at 2x implied move, sold at the T-1 close and covered at the T+1 open, has positive mean return on max-loss and a return/CVaR ratio no worse than the naked strangle, because the wings cost less than the tail they remove.

trial.statistic: Mean return on max loss, CVaR(5%), mean/CVaR, compared paired with the naked strangle on the same prints.
trial.procedure: Same pipeline as the short strangle, adding the two long wings at 2x IM; paired comparison per print; walk-forward IM/HM filter.
trial.data: Daily chain captures + daily OHLC; earnings dates.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 (CI excludes 0) and paired difference mean/CVaR(condor - strangle) > 0 with bootstrap CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Placebo nights; spread-cost sensitivity (0.5x, 1x, 1.5x of quoted spread); sector stratification.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Payoff engine already handles 4-leg structures; add a 'paired structures on same event' comparator to the trial runner.

strategies.name: Earnings IV-crush short straddle/strangle

legs.strike_rule: OTM at 1.0-1.5x implied move (≈16-25 delta); straddle variant ATM
legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after earnings (1-3 DTE at entry)

legs.strike_rule: OTM at 1.0-1.5x implied move (≈16-25 delta); straddle variant ATM

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - max(S-Kc,0) - max(Kp-S,0). Closed at the post-print open: P&L ≈ Cr - new straddle/strangle value after crush.
strategies.max_profit: Cr (net credit), if Kp <= S <= Kc at expiry.
strategies.max_loss: Unlimited upside; Kp - Cr downside.
strategies.when_to_use: Sell at the close before the print when implied move exceeds the stock's trailing realised earnings move by a margin (IM/HM > 1.2), IV rank of the event expiry > 70, and the name has no history of >2x-implied gaps. Cover at the post-print open; do not hold to expiry.
strategies.risks: Fat-tail gaps (3-5x implied moves happen several times per season in a 200-name universe); the trade's distribution is many small wins and rare large losses, so Sharpe looks great until it doesn't; margin calls at the open; early assignment on the ITM leg if held through ex-div; broker may raise margin into earnings.
strategies.margin_note: Reg-T naked margin ≈ 20% of underlying ± OTM amount per side, charged on the larger side; portfolio margin stress-tests ±15%. Many retail brokers forbid naked short calls in IRAs; use the iron condor variant there.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit equivalent: sell BTC/ETH strangles into scheduled catalysts; margin is in coin with a maintenance ratio, liquidation engine acts 24/7; inverse payoff means a short put's loss in USD accelerates as BTC falls (loss in BTC = (K-S)/S per contract). Portfolio margin on Deribit nets vega.
strategies.metals_notes: Analogue is selling GC weekly strangles before NFP/CPI (see metals entry). Futures-style margin (SPAN), Section 1256 60/40.
variants: Short straddle (max credit, max gamma)
Short strangle at 1x IM
Short strangle at 1.5x IM (lower credit, more room)
Jade lizard (short put + short call spread) to kill upside risk when skew is steep
Sell at T-1 close, hold to Friday expiry (adds post-print theta, adds drift risk)
strategies.claim: Selling a 1x-implied-move strangle in the first post-earnings expiry at the T-1 close and covering at the T+1 open has positive mean return (earnings variance risk premium) across US large-cap earnings, but the return distribution has negative skew such that the 5% CVaR exceeds 10x the mean win.

trial.statistic: Mean P&L as % of margin, hit rate, 5% CVaR, and ratio mean/CVaR; bootstrap CI.
trial.null: Mean P&L <= 0, or mean P&L > 0 but mean/CVaR < 0.05 (edge not worth the tail).
trial.procedure: From the implied-move dataset: for each print compute strangle credit at T-1 close, value at T+1 open (reprice with T+1 captured IV and gap); subtract spread; aggregate by season; walk-forward IM/HM filter.
trial.data: Daily chain captures + daily OHLC; earnings dates.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with CI excluding 0 and mean/CVaR >= 0.1 on out-of-sample seasons.
trial.controls: Random-night placebo; split by IM/HM tercile to confirm the filter is monotone; drop the 5 largest losses and verify sign of mean unchanged (robustness, not proof).

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Short-vol event harness reporting CVaR and Kelly fraction alongside mean; margin model (Reg-T formula) in the payoff engine so P&L can be reported on margin.

strategies.name: Earnings reverse calendar / event forward-variance sale (sell event expiry, buy next)

legs.expiry_rule: NEAR: first expiry AFTER earnings (1-5 DTE)
FAR: next monthly expiry (30-45 DTE); scale qty so far vega = near vega (ratio ≈ sqrt(T_near/T_far), typically 0.3-0.5 per near unit)
same far expiry; same vega-neutral ratio

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At near expiry: Cr_near - |S-K| + (value of far straddle at S, post-crush IV) - D_far. Isolates the event variance: profit if the realised event move^2 is less than the forward variance implied between the two expiries.
strategies.max_profit: Approximately Cr_near - D_far + far straddle value at S=K (bounded, since far straddle value is finite).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded in principle (short near straddle) but the long far straddle gains ~delta-weighted on large moves; net loss on a move of size m ≈ m - far_straddle_gain(m) - net_credit, grows roughly as m*(1 - ratio).
strategies.breakevens: Numerical; roughly K ± (Cr_near - D_far + far_straddle(K))/(1 - far_ratio).

greeks_at_inception.vega: ≈0 by construction (vega-neutral), but short 'event vega' / long 'ambient vega'

strategies.when_to_use: When event-implied forward variance (sigma_near^2*T_near - sigma_far^2*T_far adjusted) is high relative to trailing realised event moves, and you want to sell the event without taking ambient vol risk (e.g. a VIX spike after the print would hurt a naked short straddle but is hedged here).
strategies.risks: Not truly hedged against a big gap (gamma is net short); the far leg crushes too (post-earnings the whole surface drops), so vega-neutral at inception is not vega-neutral at T+1; four legs of slippage.
strategies.margin_note: Short near / long far at same strike is a calendar (covered) for margin if quantities are 1:1; the ratioed version leaves (1-ratio) naked short straddles margined as naked.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit term structure around FOMC/ETF dates: sell the weekly containing the event, buy the next monthly; DVOL is 30-day so cannot isolate event vol - use the two expiries' mark IVs from the public book.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: sell weekly spanning FOMC/NFP, buy the serial monthly; SPAN margin nets the time spread.
variants: 1:1 reverse calendar (simplest, net short vega)
Vega-neutral ratio (described)
Double reverse calendar at ±1 IM strikes
Event variance swap replication via strips of strikes (institutional)
strategies.claim: Selling the straddle in the first post-earnings expiry and buying a vega-matched straddle in the following monthly, entered at T-1 close and closed at T+1 open, has positive mean return with lower variance than the naked short straddle on the same prints, because the post-print crush is concentrated in the event expiry.

trial.statistic: Mean P&L and P&L standard deviation, paired with naked short straddle; Sharpe difference with bootstrap CI.
trial.null: Mean P&L <= 0 or Sharpe(reverse calendar) <= Sharpe(naked straddle).
trial.procedure: Chain-capture marks at T-1 close and T+1 (reprice far leg with captured T+1 IV); compute per-print P&L for both structures; paired bootstrap.
trial.data: Daily chain captures incl. monthly expiries; earnings dates.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 (CI excludes 0) and Sharpe difference > 0 (CI excludes 0).
trial.controls: Placebo nights; sensitivity to vega ratio (0.3, 0.4, 0.5); exclude prints within 5 days of index opex.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Add forward-variance calculator (sigma_fwd^2 = (s2^2 T2 - s1^2 T1)/(T2-T1)) to the engine; event vol = s1^2 T1 - sigma_fwd^2 * T1.

strategies.name: Earnings risk reversal (skew mean-reversion into the print)

legs.strike_rule: OTM 25-delta (same expiry); reverse both sides when skew is unusually flat/inverted

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-Kc,0) - max(Kp-S_T,0) ± net premium (often near zero-cost when skew is steep). Long-stock-like outside the strikes, flat between.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (upside).
strategies.max_loss: Kp - net credit (downside, to zero).
strategies.breakevens: If net credit: Kp - Cr; if net debit: Kc + D.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ≈0 near spot, positive above Kc, negative below Kp
greeks_at_inception.theta: ≈0 to slightly positive when done for a credit
greeks_at_inception.vega: ≈0 net; long call vega short put vega - the position is long 'skew' (profits if put IV falls relative to call IV)

strategies.when_to_use: When the pre-earnings 25-delta put IV minus 25-delta call IV (skew) is in the top decile of the stock's own history: skew is both a hedging-demand artefact and, in some studies, a predictor of the earnings return direction. Two conflicting hypotheses: (A) steep skew mean-reverts (sell puts/buy calls, bet on crush of put IV); (B) steep skew predicts negative surprise (do the opposite). The trial decides which, if either, holds.
strategies.risks: Directional: a bad print puts you long stock at Kp with the stock 20% lower; early assignment on the short put is rare pre-expiry but occurs post-print if deep ITM; the 'skew predicts returns' literature is based on monthly skew measures and may not hold at the event horizon.
strategies.margin_note: Short put margin (Reg-T ≈ 20% of underlying minus OTM amount plus premium); call purchase is debit. Not 1256 for single stocks.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC/ETH 25-delta skew on Deribit swings widely around catalysts (calls bid into ETF decisions, puts bid into macro); same structure, inverse settlement means short puts carry concave USD risk - size by USD, not BTC.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/GC skew is usually call-skewed (upside crash protection in gold); the mirror structure (long put / short call) is the metals analogue into FOMC when call skew is extreme.
variants: Zero-cost risk reversal (strikes chosen so premium nets to zero)
Collar-like inverse when skew is flat
Put spread risk reversal (long call, short put spread) to cap downside
Hold through vs close at T+1 open
strategies.claim: For US stocks, a top-decile pre-earnings 25-delta put-call IV skew predicts the sign of the post-earnings return (negative), so a long put / short call risk reversal (hypothesis B) has positive mean return at the T+1 open, and the opposite structure (hypothesis A) does not.

trial.statistic: Mean P&L of the structure at T+1 open per unit of spot; Spearman between skew decile and earnings return; bootstrap CIs.
trial.null: Spearman rho >= 0 (skew has no negative relation to the earnings return) and both structures' mean P&L <= 0.
trial.procedure: From chain captures compute 25-delta skew at T-1 close in the event expiry; sort into deciles; measure T+1 open return; compute structure P&L via reprice at T+1 captured IV; walk-forward on decile cutoffs.
trial.data: Daily chain captures (IV by delta), earnings dates, daily OHLC.
trial.pass: rho < -0.1 with p < 0.05 and hypothesis-B structure mean > 0 with CI excluding 0 out-of-sample.
trial.controls: Placebo nights; control for the stock's prior-month return (skew correlates with momentum); sector dummies.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Skew-by-delta extractor from the chain capture (interpolate IV at 25-delta) stored per symbol-day; shared with the skew-family harness already built.

strategies.name: Hold-through-earnings long straddle/strangle (realised move > implied move)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after earnings, 1-7 DTE at entry

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Straddle: |S-K|-D. Strangle (Kp<Kc): max(Kc-S... ) = max(S-Kc,0)+max(Kp-S,0)-D. Closed the morning after the print, so P&L ≈ realised gap P&L minus IV crush on remaining extrinsic.
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited (upside), K-D or Kp-D (downside).
strategies.max_loss: D, when S between the strikes (strangle) or at K (straddle) at expiry; post-print exit loss is usually 40-70% of D when |move| < implied move because of IV crush.
strategies.breakevens: Straddle: K±D. Strangle: Kc+D, Kp-D. Implied move IM ≈ 0.85*straddle_price/S (or straddle/S for ATM-forward).

greeks_at_inception.theta: very negative (and the entire overnight decay + IV crush is paid at the print)

strategies.when_to_use: Only when the straddle-implied move is below the stock's historical realised earnings move (|gap| distribution of last 8-12 prints) by a margin: IM/HM < 0.8, or when a specific catalyst (guidance change, activist, restructuring) makes the distribution fatter than the market prices. Buy at the close before the print, sell at the open or first 30 minutes after.
strategies.risks: The documented base rate is that implied moves overstate realised moves most of the time (earnings VRP), so this is negative-expectancy unless filtered; weekend/holiday prints; after-hours print with pre-market gap unwinds; wide opening spreads; stock halts.
strategies.margin_note: Debit only. Single-stock options are not 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Analogue: hold a Deribit straddle through a binary catalyst (court ruling, ETF deadline). Inverse settlement: the put leg pays in BTC that is itself less valuable after a crash, so a USD-targeted strangle needs more put notional than call notional (buy ~1.3x puts at same delta).
strategies.metals_notes: Analogue is holding GC/GLD straddles through 8:30 ET releases (NFP/CPI); see metals-macro-event-straddle.
variants: ATM straddle vs 1-IM-wide strangle
Ratio strangle (2 puts : 1 call) for negative-skew names
Buy the week before and hold through (combines ramp + move)
Long straddle + short next-month straddle (event forward variance) to hedge the crush
strategies.claim: Buying an ATM straddle at the close before earnings and selling it at the next open loses money on average (realised move < implied move) for the full universe, but a filter IM/HM < 0.8 (implied move below trailing-8 median realised move) flips mean return positive.

trial.statistic: Mean per-trade return and hit-rate, bootstrap CI; difference between filtered and unfiltered subsets.
trial.null: Filtered mean return <= 0, i.e. the filter does not rescue the trade.
trial.procedure: Record straddle mid at T-1 close and at T+1 09:45 ET mark (reprice with captured IV if intraday is missing); compute IM = straddle/S and HM = median |gap| over prior 8 prints; split by IM/HM buckets; walk-forward threshold choice.
trial.data: Daily chain capture + daily OHLC for ~200 names; earnings dates from EDGAR.
trial.pass: Filtered bucket mean return > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0, and unfiltered mean < 0 (confirms the earnings VRP base rate).
trial.controls: Placebo: same filter on random non-earnings nights; shuffled IM/HM labels; check that gains are not concentrated in 3 outlier prints (drop top-3 and re-test).

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history; T+1 open marks (daily OHLC suffices for the gap, IV crush needs the T+1 chain capture).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Implied-move vs realised-move table per symbol-quarter stored as a first-class dataset; it feeds this and the three short-vol earnings entries.

strategies.name: Implied-move vs realised-move signal (conditional straddle, sign chosen by IM/HM)

legs.strike_rule: ATM; side flips to LONG when IM/HM < 0.8 (sell when IM/HM > 1.2, no trade in between)
legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after the event (earnings, FOMC, CPI)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Short: Cr - |S-K|. Long: |S-K| - D. Marked at the post-event open.
strategies.max_profit: Short: Cr. Long: unlimited / K-D.
strategies.max_loss: Short: unlimited / K-Cr. Long: D.
strategies.when_to_use: Any scheduled event with a priced straddle: compute IM = straddle_mid/S (or Cboe-style 0.85*straddle/S) and HM = median |realised event return| over the last 8-12 same-type events; trade only in the tails of the IM/HM ratio. This is the gating signal for the three earnings-vol entries and the macro-event entries.
strategies.risks: Regime shift (new CEO, new business line) makes historical moves irrelevant; small-sample median with 8 points is noisy; ratio tails may be populated by illiquid names where the straddle mid is fictional.
strategies.margin_note: As per the chosen side (naked margin when short; debit when long).
strategies.crypto_notes: For BTC/ETH use DVOL-implied event move: IM = DVOL/sqrt(365)*sqrt(hours/24) around FOMC/CPI; realised from Deribit index. ~1000 days of DVOL gives ~20 FOMC events now.
strategies.metals_notes: GLD/GC: IM from the GLD ATM straddle or GVZ; HM from GLD daily returns on past NFP/CPI/FOMC days.
variants: Thresholds 0.8/1.2 vs quintile-based
Use 0.85*straddle (Cboe/MM rule of thumb) vs full straddle
Strangle at 1x IM instead of straddle
Apply to SPX FOMC days with VIX-as-IV (testable now)
strategies.claim: The ratio of straddle-implied move to trailing median realised event move predicts the sign of the straddle's post-event return: top-quintile IM/HM events have negative long-straddle returns and bottom-quintile events have positive long-straddle returns, with monotone ordering across quintiles.

trial.statistic: Spearman rank correlation between IM/HM and subsequent long-straddle return across events; top-minus-bottom quintile mean return difference with bootstrap CI.
trial.null: Spearman rho >= 0 (no predictive ordering) and Q5-Q1 difference >= 0.
trial.procedure: For each event build (IM, HM, realised straddle return). For SPX/FOMC now: IM from VIX-as-IV BS straddle at T-1 close, realised from SPY close-to-close over the event day; for earnings later from chains. Walk-forward: estimate quintile cutoffs on first half, test on second.
trial.data: Now: SPY daily closes since 1993, VIX daily since 1990, FOMC decision dates (8/yr, hardcoded from Fed calendars). Later: chain captures + earnings dates.
trial.pass: rho < -0.2 with p < 0.05 and Q1-Q5 > 0 with CI excluding 0 out-of-sample.
trial.controls: Placebo on random non-event days; control for VIX level (regress out); check with realised move measured close-to-close vs close-to-open.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Build an 'event-move table' harness (event_type, date, IM, HM, realised) as the shared dataset for the whole family; VIX-as-IV SPX FOMC version first.

strategies.name: Index inclusion / rebalance options (S&P 500 adds, Russell reconstitution)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry AFTER the effective (inclusion) date

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S-K1,0), K2-K1) - D for the pre-effective leg; the spread is closed at the effective-date close and optionally reversed into a bear put spread for the post-inclusion mean reversion.
strategies.max_loss: D.

greeks_at_inception.vega: slightly positive (inclusion names see IV rise into the effective-date close)

strategies.when_to_use: On the evening of an S&P 500 inclusion announcement (typically 3-7 trading days before effective), buy the call spread; close at the effective-date close when index funds buy. Reverse variant: after the effective date, bear put spread or short call spread for the documented post-inclusion reversal. Russell variant: last Friday of June close, IWM / small-cap names.
strategies.risks: The inclusion premium has shrunk (more pre-positioning); announcement is after hours so the gap is already in the open; IV on the name jumps at the open, making calls expensive; Russell reconstitution effects are mostly in the closing auction (intraday), invisible to daily data.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread. For the reversal leg, bear put debit spread or short call credit spread (margin = width - credit).
strategies.crypto_notes: Analogue: inclusion in major crypto indices / ETF baskets (e.g. a token added to an index tracked by a large fund), Coinbase listing effect. Deribit only lists BTC/ETH (plus a few alts via linear USDC options), so it applies mainly through BTC/ETH ETF flow events.
strategies.metals_notes: Analogue: GSCI/BCOM commodity index annual reweights (January roll period) move GC/SI; trade GC call/put spreads across the reweight window. Section 1256.
variants: Call spread into effective date (described)
Post-effective bear put spread (reversal)
Russell reconstitution: short IWM straddle expiring the reconstitution Friday (sell closing-auction vol) vs long
Pair: long added-name call spread / short removed-name call spread
strategies.claim: For S&P 500 additions announced since 2020, the added stock's mean return from the first post-announcement open to the effective-date close is positive and exceeds SPY, and the following 20-day return is negative (reversal), so a call spread then a put spread sequence has positive combined expectancy.

trial.statistic: Mean excess return (vs SPY) in each window; bootstrap CI; option overlay return on debit.
trial.null: Pre-effective excess return <= 0 and post-effective excess return >= 0.
trial.procedure: Collect S&P index-change press releases (announcement, effective dates); compute underlying windows; option overlay via BS with captured IV when available.
trial.data: S&P DJI press release history (free, needs scraping), single-name closes, chain captures.
trial.pass: Both window signs as claimed with 95% CIs excluding 0.
trial.controls: Matched non-included stocks of similar size and momentum; placebo dates; exclude mega-cap IPO fast-entries (e.g. direct adds at IPO) as a separate bucket.

strategies.blocked_on: index change announcement history (scrape), single-name closes; chain capture for option marks.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Generic 'two-window event' harness (announce->effective, effective->+20d).

strategies.name: Metals macro-event straddle (FOMC / CPI / NFP) on GC or GLD

legs.strike_rule: ATM (GLD $1 strikes; GC $5/$10 strikes); flip to SHORT when GVZ/GLD-straddle-implied event move > 1.2x trailing realised event move
legs.expiry_rule: GLD: Fri weekly expiring after the release (0-2 DTE); GC: weekly option expiring that Friday (futures-style, exercises into the active GC future)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: |S_T - K| - D (long) or Cr - |S_T - K| (short); GLD American/physical delivery of shares; GC options exercise into futures (cash-like via futures margin).
strategies.max_profit: Long: unbounded / K-D. Short: Cr.
strategies.max_loss: Long: D. Short: unbounded / K-Cr.
strategies.breakevens: K ± premium. Gold's typical NFP/CPI day move is 0.8-1.5%; FOMC day similar with the move concentrated 14:00-15:30 ET.
strategies.when_to_use: 8:30 ET releases (CPI, NFP) hit gold pre-market: GC trades nearly 23h so the move is tradable live in GC options; GLD options open 9:30 after the gap, so for GLD the long straddle must be bought the prior close and the short straddle should be sold at 9:35 (post-gap crush). FOMC 14:00 ET is live for both. Gate with the implied-vs-realised event-move ratio using GVZ (Cboe gold vol index) or the GLD straddle.
strategies.risks: GC options are American and exercise into a futures position (margin jump); GLD early exercise risk on short legs is low (no dividend) but exists; gold's reaction to CPI/NFP is regime dependent (sign flips with the real-rate narrative) so historical realised moves are noisy; SLV/SI moves are ~2x gold's with worse liquidity.
strategies.margin_note: GC/OG: SPAN futures-style margin, Section 1256 (60/40), trades on CME Globex nearly 23h. GLD/SLV: equity-option margin, no 1256 (GLD is a grantor trust taxed as collectible on the shares, but options on GLD are not 1256; confirm with tax adviser).
strategies.crypto_notes: Run the same event list on BTC (crypto-macro-event-straddle) and test cross-asset: does the gold event move predict the BTC event move sign on the same day?
strategies.metals_notes: Core entry. GC weekly options (Mon/Wed/Fri expiries exist on CME for gold) allow 0-2 DTE event structures; OG monthly expires 4 business days before month-end of the month preceding the contract month. GVZ (Cboe gold vol index, free daily history at cboe.com) is the VIX analogue for the implied-move proxy.
variants: Long GLD straddle prior close through 8:30 release
Short GLD straddle at 9:35 after the gap (post-release crush)
GC weekly straddle sold at 14:05 ET after FOMC
SLV/SI version (higher beta)
Strangle at ±1 implied move
GLD/GC calendar across the release
strategies.claim: GLD's close-to-close absolute return on FOMC and CPI days, divided by the GVZ-implied one-day move (GVZ/sqrt(252)), is lower on average than on non-event days, so a short ATM GLD straddle priced with GVZ-as-IV at the prior close has positive mean return on those days.

trial.statistic: Mean |r_T|/(GVZ_{T-1}/sqrt(252)) event vs non-event; mean P&L of BS straddle (IV=GVZ, T=1/252) sold T-1 close; bootstrap CIs.
trial.null: Event-day ratio >= non-event ratio; straddle P&L <= 0.
trial.procedure: Load GLD daily closes (free) and Cboe GVZ history (free CSV, since 2008); FOMC/CPI/NFP dates; compute; stratify by GVZ tercile and by real-rate regime (10y TIPS yield change sign).
trial.data: GLD daily closes, Cboe GVZ daily history, FOMC/CPI/NFP calendars (all free, not yet wired).
trial.pass: Straddle P&L > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 and ratio difference < 0 with CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Non-event days; placebo dates; exclude 2008 and 2020-03; compare with the SPX result to see whether the gold event premium is larger or smaller.

strategies.blocked_on: GLD daily closes and Cboe GVZ history (both free, need a fetcher) plus CPI/NFP release calendars; FOMC-only version is runnable as soon as GLD closes and GVZ are loaded.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Generalise the VIX-as-IV straddle harness to (underlying, vol index) pairs: (SPY,VIX), (GLD,GVZ), (BTC,DVOL), (QQQ,VXN).

strategies.name: Monthly opex gamma pin (short ATM straddle / iron butterfly on heavy-OI strikes)

legs.strike_rule: the strike with the largest combined call+put OI within ±1% of spot (max-pain / pin strike)
legs.expiry_rule: third-Friday monthly expiry, entered Friday morning (0DTE) or Thursday close

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cr - |S_T - K| (straddle) with wings capping loss at (wing width) - Cr.
strategies.max_profit: Cr at S_T = K.
strategies.max_loss: Straddle: unbounded / K - Cr. Iron butterfly: wing width - Cr.
strategies.when_to_use: Monthly (third Friday) opex when estimated dealer gamma exposure is positive (customers net long calls/short puts ⇒ dealers long gamma, hedging damps moves) and a strike within ±1% carries outsized OI; sell the straddle on that strike Friday morning, hold to the close. Avoid when GEX is negative or a macro release falls on the same day.
strategies.risks: Pinning is a tendency, not a law: one trend day costs 3-5 credits; for SPX monthly (AM-settled, SOQ at the open) the 'pin' is at Friday's open, not the close - use SPXW PM or SPY for close pinning; dealer-positioning estimates from OI assume customers are long calls/short puts, which fails when funds are short calls (overwriting).
strategies.margin_note: Naked short straddle margin for the no-wing version (≈15-20% of underlying); iron butterfly margin = wing width - credit. SPX/XSP 1256; SPY/stocks not.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit monthly expiry (last Friday of month, 08:00 UTC) concentrates OI; 'max pain' pinning is widely discussed. Sell the 1-day BTC straddle expiring at 08:00 UTC on the pin strike at 00:00 UTC. 24/7 means no overnight gap, inverse payoff asymmetric.
strategies.metals_notes: COMEX gold options (OG) expire four business days before the end of the month preceding the contract month; GC often gravitates toward big round strikes into OG expiry. GLD monthly opex works like other equity options.
variants: Short straddle at pin strike (no wings)
Iron butterfly with ±1.5% wings
Short strangle at the two heaviest OI strikes bracketing spot
Long straddle inverse when GEX estimated negative (see 0dte-long-straddle-negative-gex)
Thursday-close entry (adds overnight theta, adds gap risk)
strategies.claim: On monthly third-Friday opex days, SPY's close lands closer to the nearest integer strike than on non-opex days (clustering), and a 0DTE ATM short straddle sold at the open on opex days has higher mean return than the same structure on non-opex Fridays.

trial.statistic: (a) Mean distance of close to nearest $1 strike, opex vs non-opex Fridays, with permutation test; (b) mean P&L of VIX-as-IV priced ATM 0DTE straddle (T=1/252 from open) opex vs non-opex Fridays.
trial.null: (a) No difference in clustering; (b) opex short-straddle P&L <= non-opex Friday P&L.
trial.procedure: Third-Friday dates since 1993; SPY daily OHLC; compute distance metrics and realised open-to-close move; price straddle at open with VIX (scaled to 1-day); compare distributions; later, with chain captures, condition on OI-weighted pin strike and on GEX sign.
trial.data: SPY daily OHLC since 1993, VIX; later chain OI captures.
trial.pass: (a) permutation p < 0.05 for smaller distance on opex; (b) mean difference > 0 with CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Non-opex Fridays and all other weekdays as controls; exclude opex days coinciding with FOMC/CPI; check pre-2010 vs post-2010 (0DTE era) stability.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add a GEX estimator (sum over strikes of OI*gamma*spot^2*0.01 with sign convention calls +, puts -) once chain captures accumulate; join to the opex clustering test.

strategies.name: Post-earnings announcement drift (PEAD) with vertical spreads

legs.strike_rule: ATM after the gap (positive surprise); for negative surprise mirror with puts

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S-K1,0), K2-K1) - D for the bull call spread; bear put spread mirror.
strategies.max_loss: D.
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D (bull call); K2 - D (bear put).

greeks_at_inception.theta: slightly negative (ATM long dominates) turning positive as spot moves through
greeks_at_inception.vega: ≈0 (spread) - deliberate, since post-crush IV is low but direction, not vol, is the bet

strategies.when_to_use: The day after a print where (a) earnings surprise (SUE) is in the top/bottom decile and (b) the stock gapped in the same direction and closed near the extreme of its day (no fade). Enter at T+1 close, hold 20-40 trading days or until the spread reaches 70% of max.
strategies.risks: PEAD has weakened in large caps since the 2000s (remains in small caps where options are illiquid); the gap already captures most of the news; spread caps upside; sector/market beta dominates single-name drift (hedge with SPY if needed).
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread, margin = debit. Bear put spread also debit. Alternative credit versions (bull put spread) margin = width - credit.
strategies.crypto_notes: No earnings; weak analogue is post-upgrade / post-ETF-flow drift. Deribit call spreads (debit) available in USD strikes; inverse payoff caps the USD value of a call spread gain slightly below (K2-K1)/S_T.
strategies.metals_notes: No analogue (no earnings); post-FOMC drift in gold is a separate macro entry.
variants: Bull call spread vs bull put credit spread (collect post-crush IV)
Risk reversal (long call, short put) when IV skew makes puts rich after a gap down
Stock replacement: long 70-delta call instead of spread
Hedge beta with SPY put spread
strategies.claim: A 30-45 DTE ATM/+5% call debit spread bought at the T+1 close after a top-decile positive earnings surprise with a same-direction gap earns a positive mean return on debit over 30 trading days, exceeding the return of the same spread bought on random days for the same stocks.

trial.statistic: Mean return on debit and difference vs matched random-day spreads; bootstrap CI; also underlying-only 30-day drift as sanity check.
trial.procedure: Underlying leg testable sooner: sort post-earnings gaps by size/direction, measure 30-day drift (needs single-name closes + earnings dates). Option leg: mark spread at T+1 close and 30 days later from chain captures (or BS-reprice with captured IV).
trial.data: Earnings dates and SUE (EDGAR + consensus; consensus not free - use gap size as proxy); single-name daily closes; chain captures for option marks.
trial.pass: Mean excess return > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 over at least 2 non-overlapping seasons.
trial.controls: Match on market beta (SPY return over holding period); size terciles; placebo entries on random days; check the sign in both directions (bear spreads after negative surprises).

strategies.blocked_on: earnings-date history + single-name daily closes (free but not wired); chain capture for option-level marks (30+ days).
strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse the underlying 'event drift' harness for the stock leg; BS-reprice the spread with captured IV for the option overlay.

strategies.name: Pre-earnings long calendar (sell pre-event expiry, buy event expiry)

legs.expiry_rule: NEAR: last expiry BEFORE the earnings date (3-10 DTE)
FAR: first expiry AFTER the earnings date

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At near expiry: value of far-dated call at S minus max(S-K,0) minus D. Max value when S=K at near expiry with far IV elevated.
strategies.max_profit: Approximately C_far(K, S=K, IV_event) - D at near expiry; not closed-form, grows with far-month IV.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit) if S moves far from K so both legs lose extrinsic (far leg can't be worth less than near leg at same strike, so loss capped at D).
strategies.breakevens: S levels at near expiry where C_far(S) = max(S-K,0) + D; solve numerically.

greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long far vega, and far IV is the one that ramps into earnings)

strategies.when_to_use: When the near expiry (pre-print) IV is not much below the event expiry IV (flat term structure), 2-3 weeks before earnings; the trade profits as the event expiry IV ramps and the pre-event week decays. Close at or just before near expiry, do NOT hold the long leg through the print (that becomes a long straddle bet).
strategies.risks: A big pre-print move kills both legs' extrinsic; early assignment on the short near leg if deep ITM near ex-div; the event IV may already be fully ramped (check event-expiry IV vs its 8-quarter pre-print median); if the earnings date shifts earlier than the near expiry the short leg is suddenly across the event.
strategies.margin_note: Long calendar is a debit spread; margin = debit (far expiry is later than near, so it is a 'covered' short). Portfolio margin treats it as a time spread.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit has daily, weekly and monthly expiries (settlement_period day/week/month), so a calendar straddling a known catalyst is straightforward; all expiries 08:00 UTC. Inverse settlement means both legs pay in coin; calendar P&L is small relative to coin price moves, so hedge the coin exposure if USD-denominated.
strategies.metals_notes: GC weekly options allow a calendar around FOMC (sell the pre-FOMC weekly, buy the post-FOMC weekly). GLD route identical to equities.
variants: Call vs put calendar
Double calendar (OTM call cal + OTM put cal) for width
Diagonal: far leg one strike OTM in the direction of drift
Reverse (short) calendar: see earnings-reverse-calendar for the crush trade
strategies.claim: An ATM calendar that is short the last pre-earnings weekly and long the first post-earnings expiry, opened 10-15 trading days before the print and closed at the near expiry, has positive mean return on debit because event-expiry IV rises into the print while pre-event expiry IV decays.

trial.statistic: Mean return on debit, hit rate, bootstrap CI.
trial.procedure: From chain captures, mark both legs at entry and at the near expiry close; compute return; filter by term-structure slope at entry (IV_far - IV_near) and test monotonicity across slope terciles.
trial.data: Daily chain captures with weekly expiries for ~200 names; earnings dates.
trial.pass: Mean > 0 with CI excluding 0; flattest-slope tercile outperforms steepest.
trial.controls: Same calendar in windows with no earnings between the two expiries (placebo); exclude names with ex-div between legs.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through 2+ earnings seasons; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Term-structure slope per symbol per day (IV_near vs IV_event) as a stored feature; mark-to-market via BS reprice.

strategies.name: Pre-earnings long straddle (buy the IV ramp, exit before the print)

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry AFTER the earnings date (7-21 DTE at entry)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S-K,0)+max(K-S,0)-D = |S-K|-D, where D = call+put debit. Strategy is normally closed before expiry (at the close before the announcement), so the realised P&L is the mark-to-market change: approx vega*(IV_exit-IV_entry) + 0.5*gamma*dS^2 - theta*days.
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited upside (S->inf), K-D on downside (S->0) if held; if exited pre-print, bounded by vega*dIV + gamma P&L.
strategies.max_loss: D (net debit), at S=K at expiry. Pre-print exit loss ≈ theta decay minus IV ramp.
strategies.breakevens: K+D and K-D at expiry; pre-print breakeven is dIV >= theta_decay/vega.

greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long front-month vega, the point of the trade)

strategies.when_to_use: 5-10 trading days before a scheduled earnings date when the event expiry's IV is still below its own history of pre-earnings peaks (IV_now < median pre-print IV of last 8 quarters) and the stock has a record of rising implied move into the print. Exit at the close before the announcement; never hold through (that is a different strategy, see earnings-hold-through-straddle).
strategies.risks: Theta can exceed the IV ramp when the ramp is already priced; a pre-announcement (guidance warning, M&A) can gap the stock while you are long gamma (good) or crush IV early (bad); earnings date changes; wide bid/ask in single names costs 2-5% of the straddle per round trip; assignment risk is nil (long only).
strategies.margin_note: Debit paid in full; Reg-T no margin. Section 1256 does not apply to single-stock options (60/40 only for broad index like SPX/XSP).
strategies.crypto_notes: No earnings, but the same vol-ramp structure applies to scheduled catalysts (ETF decision dates, network upgrades, token unlocks). On Deribit buy BTC/ETH straddle in the weekly expiring after the date; inverse contracts: P&L in BTC, so a BTC drop shrinks the USD value of gains on the put leg (convexity drag). 24/7 trading means no overnight gap, expiry 08:00 UTC.
strategies.metals_notes: No earnings analogue. Nearest equivalent is buying GLD/GC straddles 3-5 days before FOMC/CPI when GVZ is below its pre-event median (see metals-macro-event-straddle). GC options are futures-style margined and Section 1256.
variants: Buy 10 days out, exit day before (pure ramp)
Buy 3 days out (less theta, less ramp)
Strangle version: 25-delta call + 25-delta put (cheaper, less vega per dollar)
Short-the-ramp inverse: sell straddle 10 days out, close day before (bets the ramp is already priced)
Calendarised: long event expiry, short same strike expiry BEFORE earnings (see pre-earnings-calendar)
strategies.claim: For US large-cap stocks, an ATM straddle in the first expiry after earnings, bought 7 trading days before the announcement and sold at the close before it, has a mean return > 0 and a Sharpe > 0 net of half the bid/ask spread, because event-expiry IV rises more than theta decays over that window.

trial.statistic: Mean per-trade return on debit (and Sharpe), with 95% studentized block-bootstrap CI; secondary: mean dIV(7d->0d) vs mean theta decay as % of straddle.
trial.null: Mean net return <= 0 (IV ramp fully priced; theta = ramp).
trial.procedure: For every earnings date in the capture window and every symbol with chain capture: at close T-7 record ATM straddle mid in the first post-earnings expiry; at close T-1 (pre-print) record the same straddle mid; return = (mid_T1 - mid_T7 - spread_cost)/mid_T7. Walk-forward: use first 2 seasons to choose filter (IV percentile), test on the following seasons. Deflated Sharpe over number of filters tried.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain captures (bid/ask/IV) for ~200 liquid names; earnings dates from EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 filings (free) or company IR calendars.
trial.pass: Bootstrap 95% CI for mean net return excludes 0 and point estimate > 2% of debit; deflated Sharpe p < 0.05.
trial.controls: Same structure on non-earnings 7-day windows for the same stocks (placebo); a VIX-regime control (exclude days with VIX change > 10%); sign test per season to check stability.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture through at least 2 earnings seasons (~180 days) for single names; earnings-date history.
strategies.harness_suggestion: Add an 'event window' harness: takes (symbol, event_date, offsets) and returns straddle mid/IV path from the chain store; reuse payoff engine for mark-to-market via BS reprice at captured IV.

strategies.name: Pre-FOMC announcement drift call spread

legs.strike_rule: ATM at T-1 close (SPX/SPXW or SPY)
legs.expiry_rule: expiry on or just after FOMC day (1-3 DTE)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: min(max(S-K1,0), K2-K1) - D; normally closed at 13:55 ET on FOMC day, before the statement.
strategies.max_loss: D.
strategies.when_to_use: Buy at the close of the day before the FOMC decision (or 24h before), sell at 13:55 ET on decision day. Based on the Lucca-Moench pre-FOMC drift (large positive SPX excess return in the 24h before scheduled announcements, 1994-2011). Use the spread so the position is cheap and insensitive to the IV ramp into the statement.
strategies.risks: The drift has weakened/vanished post-2011 in several follow-ups; the spread's short leg caps the gain if the pre-FOMC rally is large; theta on a 1-2 DTE spread is high; holding through the statement by accident converts the trade into an event bet.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread. SPX/XSP 1256-eligible; SPY not.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC shows a weak and unstable pre-FOMC pattern; Deribit daily options (settlement_period 'day', 08:00 UTC) do not line up with 14:00 ET, so use the weekly and close before the statement.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's pre-FOMC drift is not documented as robust; test GLD separately before trading.
variants: Call debit spread (described)
Long SPY/ES outright 24h (underlying version)
Bull put credit spread (collects elevated pre-event IV)
Risk reversal (long call / short put) for more delta
strategies.claim: SPY's close(T-1) to 13:55 ET(T) return on scheduled FOMC decision days has a positive mean that exceeds the mean return over the same 20.5-hour window on non-FOMC days, and the effect persists out-of-sample after 2011.

trial.statistic: Mean return difference (FOMC window minus non-FOMC window), t-stat with HAC/bootstrap; sub-period split pre/post 2011.
trial.procedure: Using daily closes as the first pass (close T-1 to close T includes the post-statement move, so also test close T-1 to open T as a cleaner proxy); when intraday is available use 13:55 ET. Option overlay: BS price the spread with VIX-as-IV at T-1 and reprice at exit.
trial.data: SPY daily OHLC since 1993 (open T is reachable), VIX, FOMC dates.
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 in the post-2011 subsample.
trial.controls: Random-date placebo; exclude unscheduled/emergency meetings; control for overall equity drift (subtract unconditional mean).

strategies.harness_suggestion: Event-window return harness with (T-1 close -> T open) and (T-1 close -> T close) variants; flag that intraday 13:55 is the true target.

strategies.name: SPX macro-event straddle (FOMC / CPI / NFP): event vol vs realised

legs.strike_rule: ATM (SPX/SPXW or XSP), side flips to SHORT when event IM/HM ratio > 1.2
legs.expiry_rule: SPXW expiring the event day (0-1 DTE; PM settled 4pm ET) or the day after

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long: |S_T - K| - D at the 4pm ET SPXW settlement. Short: Cr - |S_T - K|.
strategies.max_profit: Long: unbounded / K-D. Short: Cr.
strategies.max_loss: Long: D. Short: unbounded / K-Cr (cash-settled, no assignment).
strategies.breakevens: K ± premium. Event implied move IM = straddle/S; for FOMC day typically 0.8-1.3%.

greeks_at_inception.vega: positive (long) / negative (short); IV collapses within minutes of the 2pm FOMC statement or 8:30 CPI print

strategies.when_to_use: Long when the event-day straddle (bought at the prior close, or 13:55 ET for FOMC) is cheap relative to trailing realised event moves and the macro surprise distribution is wide (e.g. dispersion of economist forecasts high); short when the event straddle is rich. Variant: sell the 0DTE straddle at 14:05 ET after the statement to harvest the post-announcement crush while the press conference is live.
strategies.risks: 0DTE gamma: a 1.5% move on the short side costs 3-5x the credit; CPI at 8:30 means the move is a pre-market gap (SPXW opens 9:30, so the short side has no exit before the gap - use the prior-day expiry only when you intend to carry); FOMC dot-plot/presser can reverse the initial move twice.
strategies.margin_note: SPX options are cash-settled, European, Section 1256 (60/40). Naked short SPX straddle margin ≈ 15% of index value under Reg-T; portfolio margin stress ±8-10%. XSP (1/10th) for sizing.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC/ETH react to FOMC/CPI; see crypto-macro-event-straddle.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold reacts strongly to FOMC/CPI/NFP; see metals-macro-event-straddle.
variants: Long event-day straddle bought prior close
Long straddle bought 13:55 ET on FOMC day (minimal theta)
Short 0DTE straddle sold 14:05 ET after statement (post-announcement crush)
Short straddle in the day-after expiry sold at the event-day close (sells residual event vol)
Strangle at ±1 IM instead of straddle
Pre-FOMC drift directional (separate entry)
strategies.claim: The SPY close-to-close absolute return on FOMC decision days is, on average, smaller than the move implied by the prior-day VIX (VIX/sqrt(252)) scaled by the historical FOMC-day/average-day realised ratio, i.e. a short ATM straddle priced with VIX-as-IV at the prior close and settled at the FOMC close has positive mean return since 1994, with the premium concentrated in high-VIX regimes.

trial.statistic: Mean P&L of a BS-priced ATM straddle (IV = VIX at T-1 close, T = 1/252) short-sold at T-1 close, settled on |SPY_T/SPY_T-1 - 1|; bootstrap CI; stratified by VIX tercile.
trial.null: Mean P&L <= 0 (FOMC-day realised move >= VIX-implied daily move).
trial.procedure: FOMC decision dates 1994-2026 (hardcoded, 8/yr ≈ 260 events); for each, price straddle with VIX-as-IV; compute realised; compare with same statistic on all non-FOMC days (unconditional VRP) to isolate the event-specific premium. Walk-forward: estimate on 1994-2010, test 2011-2026.
trial.data: SPY daily closes since 1993, VIX daily since 1990, FOMC decision dates.
trial.pass: Mean P&L > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 and FOMC-day premium differs from non-FOMC VRP (difference CI excludes 0 in either direction - report sign).
trial.controls: Non-FOMC days as control; placebo dates (FOMC date ± 7 days); exclude 2008-09 and 2020-03 as a robustness pass; note VIX is 30-day IV, so scale by trailing ratio of 1-day to 30-day realised vol.

strategies.harness_suggestion: VIX-as-IV straddle pricer over an event-date list; run the identical code for CPI and NFP dates once BLS release calendars are loaded (also free).

strategies.name: Triple witching / quarterly rebalance close (long gamma into the close)

legs.expiry_rule: SPXW PM-settled expiring that third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec (or SPY same-day)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: |S_T - K| - D at the 4pm settlement, where the closing auction carries index rebalance and futures/options expiry flows.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded / K - D.
strategies.max_loss: D (very small, 1 hour of ATM premium ≈ 0.15-0.3% of spot).
strategies.when_to_use: Quarterly triple witching Fridays (third Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec: index futures, index options and stock options all expire and S&P quarterly rebalance trades at the close), plus Russell reconstitution (late June) and MSCI semi-annual (end May/Nov) closes. Buy the straddle at 15:00, hold to 4pm. The bet is that the closing-auction imbalance produces a larger last-hour move than the 1-hour premium implies. Inverse variant: short the straddle if the realised last-hour move is historically smaller than implied (pinning dominates).
strategies.risks: Daily data cannot see the last hour; SPX monthly (AM-settled) contracts settled at the open, so the PM move is only tradable via SPXW/SPY; last-hour liquidity is good but the premium is tiny so fees and spread matter; the sign of the effect (pin vs imbalance move) is an empirical question - do not trade before the test.
strategies.margin_note: Debit; SPX/XSP 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit quarterly expiry (last Friday of Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, 08:00 UTC) is crypto's 'witching'; buy the daily straddle at 07:00 UTC into the 08:00 settlement (settlement price is a 30-minute TWAP of the index, which damps the final move).
strategies.metals_notes: GC quarterly option expiry and first-notice-day flows for the active contract are the metals analogue; GC trades nearly 23h so the 'close' is the 13:30 ET settlement window.
variants: Long 15:00 straddle (described)
Short 15:00 straddle (pin bet)
Long straddle from Thursday close through Friday (captures SOQ gap for AM-settled plus close)
Russell reconstitution IWM straddle
MSCI rebalance EFA/EEM straddle
strategies.claim: On triple-witching Fridays, SPY's intraday range and absolute close-to-close return exceed those of other Fridays, so a same-day ATM straddle priced with VIX-as-IV at the open has higher mean return than on non-witching Fridays.

trial.statistic: Mean |return| and mean (high-low)/open on witching vs other Fridays; mean P&L of VIX-priced 0DTE straddle; permutation and bootstrap CIs.
trial.null: No difference in realised move, or straddle P&L difference <= 0.
trial.procedure: Quarterly third Fridays since 1993; SPY OHLC; VIX; compute metrics and straddle P&L; later refine with 15:00 ET intraday capture.
trial.data: SPY daily OHLC, VIX, calendar.
trial.pass: Difference > 0 with p < 0.05 (permutation) for at least one of the two realised measures and straddle P&L difference CI excluding 0.
trial.controls: Other Fridays and monthly non-quarterly opex Fridays as separate controls; exclude witching days coinciding with FOMC.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Event-day realised-move comparison harness (event dates vs matched weekday controls) with VIX-as-IV straddle pricer.

strategies.name: VIX settlement (Wednesday SOQ) trades

legs.strike_rule: VIX call spread: short K1 = front VIX future + 2 points, long K2 = K1 + 5 (expiry = Wednesday settlement)
legs.expiry_rule: VIX monthly/weekly expiring the next Wednesday, entered Friday-Monday before (3-5 DTE)

legs.strike_rule: SOQ variant: SPX far-OTM puts (5-10 delta) in the SPX expiry used by the VIX SOQ, sold at Wednesday's open into the settlement print
legs.expiry_rule: SPX expiry 30 days after the VIX expiry (the SOQ constituent series); covered within the day

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: VIX call spread: Cr - min(max(VIX_SOQ - K1, 0), K2 - K1). SOQ-put variant: intraday P&L = premium sold at the open - repurchase price after the opening auction.
strategies.max_profit: Cr (call spread); opening premium minus repurchase (puts).
strategies.max_loss: (K2-K1) - Cr (call spread); unbounded until covered (naked SPX puts, same-day).
strategies.breakevens: K1 + Cr for the call spread.

greeks_at_inception.delta: short VIX delta (bearish vol) for the call spread; short SPX put delta (long market) for the SOQ puts
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative (short vol-of-vol / short SPX tail vol)

strategies.when_to_use: VIX options settle to a Special Opening Quotation computed from the opening prices of the SPX options series that define the 30-day VIX on Wednesday morning (Cboe). Two documented regularities to test: (1) VIX futures/options converge to the SOQ with the front future usually in contango and drifting down into settlement; (2) the SOQ auction has shown deviations from the prior close and from the post-open VIX (Griffin-Shams), often driven by far-OTM SPX put orders. Trade (1) with a short VIX call spread into Wednesday; trade (2) by selling far-OTM SPX puts into the opening auction on settlement Wednesdays and covering after.
strategies.risks: VIX spikes are discontinuous; the call spread's max loss is 3-5x the credit; the SOQ-puts variant is a naked short tail for ~30 minutes on a day when the auction is known to be noisy, exactly the wrong exposure in a crash; Cboe has changed SOQ procedures over time, so historical deviations may not recur.
strategies.margin_note: VIX options are cash-settled, European, 1256-eligible (broad-based index); margin for the call spread = width - credit. Naked SPX far-OTM puts need large margin and portfolio-margin stress.
strategies.crypto_notes: No VIX settlement analogue; DVOL is an index but has no tradable settlement event. Deribit's own expiry at 08:00 UTC with 30-min TWAP delivery is the closest 'settlement window' effect.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ (gold vol index) has no listed options with a settlement event; not applicable.
variants: Short VIX call spread into Wednesday (contango roll-down)
Short VIX straddle expiring Wednesday when VIX3M/VIX ratio > 1.1 (steep contango)
SOQ far-OTM SPX put sale at the Wednesday open
Long VIX call spread when VIX3M/VIX < 1 (backwardation, event risk)
VIX weekly versions
strategies.claim: On VIX settlement Wednesdays, the VIX index open deviates from the prior close by more than on other Wednesdays (SOQ-related), and the VIX futures-to-SOQ convergence is negative on average when VIX3M > VIX (contango), so a short VIX call spread expiring that Wednesday entered 3 days earlier has positive mean return conditional on contango.

trial.statistic: (a) Mean |VIX_open - VIX_prevclose| on settlement Wednesdays vs other Wednesdays (permutation test); (b) mean of (VIX_T-3 close proxy for front future minus VIX_SOQ≈VIX open on T) conditional on VIX3M>VIX, with bootstrap CI.
trial.null: (a) no difference; (b) mean convergence >= 0 under contango.
trial.procedure: VIX expiration dates = 30 days before the third Friday of the following month (Wednesday rule), computed since 2006 (VIX options launch); VIX and VIX3M daily OHLC; compute both statistics; option-level P&L needs VIX futures history (free from Cboe) and VIX option chains (capture from today).
trial.data: CBOE VIX, VIX3M daily OHLC since 1990/2002; VIX settlement calendar (computable); optionally Cboe VIX futures settlement history.
trial.pass: (a) p < 0.05 and (b) mean < 0 with CI excluding 0 under contango.
trial.controls: Non-settlement Wednesdays; backwardation subsample; exclude 2008, 2018-02, 2020-03 as robustness; placebo offsets ±1 day.

strategies.harness_suggestion: VIX settlement calendar generator + VIX/VIX3M OHLC event harness; add VIX futures history fetch (Cboe CFE CSVs) for the futures-based version.

strategies.max_loss: S0 - C

strategies.name: Cash-secured put / put-write (Cboe PUT, WPUT, PUTD)

legs.strike_rule: ATM (PUT: first strike at or below the index) or OTM 2% (PUTY) / delta -0.30; cash = K held in T-bills
legs.expiry_rule: 1 month rolled 3rd Friday (PUT); weekly (WPUT); dynamic sizing (PUTD)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: P - max(K - S_T, 0) + T-bill interest on K
strategies.max_profit: P (+ interest)
strategies.when_to_use: Neutral-to-mildly-bullish; willing to own the asset at K-P; harvests the variance premium with a fixed-income collateral base. By put-call parity it equals a covered call at the same strike (Israelov: PUT vs BXM differences come from roll-day mechanics, not economics).
strategies.risks: Substantial downside to zero; assignment leaves a long position in a falling market; margin calls if not fully cash-secured; weekly puts concentrate gamma; IV spike marks the short put against you before expiry.
strategies.margin_note: Cash account: cash or escrow equal to aggregate strike. Margin account (Cboe manual): 100% premium + 20% of underlying (15% broad-based index) minus OTM amount, min 10% of strike + premium.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit inverse puts are collateralised in BTC, so a short BTC put is 'cash-secured' in a currency that falls with the strike being breached (wrong-way collateral); USDC linear puts (instrument_type 'linear', settlement USDC) give a true cash-secured put.
strategies.metals_notes: Short OG/SO puts need SPAN margin, not full cash; GLD/SLV puts follow the 20% equity rule; a short GC put assigned becomes a long GC future (not metal).

strategies.name: Collar (protective collar, Cboe CLL 95-110)

legs.strike_rule: OTM 5% (K_p = 95% of index, CLL) or delta -0.20 to -0.30
legs.expiry_rule: CLL: quarterly (3 months); generic: same expiry as call

legs.strike_rule: OTM 10% (K_c = 110%, CLL) or delta 0.20-0.30; K_p < S0 < K_c
legs.expiry_rule: CLL: monthly, rolled 3rd Friday; generic: same as put

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(K_p, min(S_T, K_c)) - S0 - (P - C)
strategies.max_profit: K_c - S0 - net debit (or + net credit)
strategies.max_loss: S0 - K_p + net debit (or - net credit)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = S0 + net debit (= S0 - net credit)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: near zero / slightly negative near call, positive near put
greeks_at_inception.theta: near zero (OIC: offsets); slightly negative when put is costlier
greeks_at_inception.vega: near zero; long skew exposure (long put vega > short call vega when strikes equidistant)

strategies.when_to_use: Holder wants a hard floor (concentrated stock, pre-earnings, tax-deferred holding) and will give up upside above K_c to pay for it; cheapest when skew is flat.
strategies.risks: Floor only to K_p; upside capped; CLL-style monthly calls vs quarterly puts create cross-rolls when the call strike falls under the put; early assignment on the call before dividends; collar on employer stock may have legal/tax constructive-sale issues.
strategies.margin_note: Cboe manual 'Collar': put and call same expiry, put strike < call strike; margin account: pay for put, 50% on stock, maintenance on stock is lower of 10% of put strike + OTM amount or 25% of call strike; cash account allowed.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit collars are quoted in BTC; the long put's BTC payoff is convex in USD (inverse), so the floor in USD is lower than K_p implies; use USDC linear options (instrument_type 'linear') for a USD floor.
strategies.metals_notes: GC collars via OG puts/calls settle into futures; GLD collars are equity-style; gold skew is often call-skewed (unlike equities) so 95-110 collars on gold are rarely zero-cost.

strategies.name: Protective put / married put (Cboe PPUT 5% OTM)

legs.strike_rule: OTM 5% (PPUT: first strike below 95% of index) or ATM / delta -0.30; tail variant OTM 10% quarterly (PPUT3M)

strategies.max_profit: unbounded (S_T - S0 - P)
strategies.max_loss: S0 - K + P
strategies.when_to_use: Bullish holder fears a sharp temporary decline and needs a defined floor (margin, mandate, taxes prevent selling). Economically it is a bet that realised vol will exceed implied over the hedge horizon (Israelov: 'buying a put is a bet that realized volatility will exceed implied').
strategies.risks: Persistent negative carry from the variance and skew premium (puts are 'still not cheap'); roll timing; floor resets each month so a slow grind lower is not protected; IRS may treat a deep ITM put on appreciated stock as a constructive sale.
strategies.margin_note: Cboe manual 'Long Put and Long Underlying': pay for put in full; stock maintenance is the lower of 10% of put strike + OTM amount or 25% of stock value (American-style put).
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the inverse put pays in BTC whose USD value falls as BTC falls, so a USD floor needs ~K/S_T more contracts (or USDC linear puts); DVOL vs realised shows BTC puts also carry a variance premium on average.
strategies.metals_notes: GC puts settle into short futures; GLD puts are equity-style; gold put IV is usually below call IV (positive skew) so downside protection on gold is comparatively cheap.
