strategies.name: Put-spread collar (Cboe CLLZ zero-cost put-spread collar)

legs.strike_rule: K3 > S0: strike solved so net premium = 0 (farther than in a plain zero-cost collar because the short put finances part)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: S_T - S0 + max(K2 - S_T,0) - max(K1 - S_T,0) - max(S_T - K3,0) (net premium 0)
strategies.max_profit: K3 - S0
strategies.max_loss: S0 - (K2 - K1) (loss resumes below K1; protection only in the band K1..K2)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: mixed: positive near K2, negative near K1 and K3
greeks_at_inception.vega: approximately zero; long the K2 wing, short the K1 tail (short tail risk)

strategies.when_to_use: Holder wants protection against a moderate (5-20%) correction and more upside than a plain collar, and accepts re-exposure in a crash below K1 (where the short put is deepest ITM).
strategies.risks: Crash risk below K1 returns in full; three short/long strikes to manage; assignment on the short put/call; the structure is short the tail precisely when tail hedges pay.
strategies.margin_note: Long stock + short call is covered; put vertical margin = width (K2-K1) less credit; broad-based index options get 15% rule but the spread rule (max loss) applies.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC crash frequency makes the uncovered tail below K1 more expensive in realised terms; Deribit portfolio margin recognises the vertical.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's lower crash frequency makes put-spread collars relatively cheaper to run on GLD/GC.

strategies.name: The wheel (cash-secured put -> assignment -> covered call -> called away)

legs.strike_rule: phase 1: OTM put, delta -0.20 to -0.30, cash-secured; repeat until assigned
legs.expiry_rule: 30-45 DTE, close at 50% profit or roll at 21 DTE

legs.strike_rule: phase 2: assigned at K_put, cost basis K_put - P
phase 2: OTM call, strike >= cost basis (K_put - cumulative premium), delta 0.20-0.30
legs.expiry_rule: 30-45 DTE, repeat until called away; then restart phase 1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Cycle P&L = sum of put premiums + sum of call premiums + (K_call - K_put) on completion; while long, payoff = min(S_T, K_call) - K_put + premiums
strategies.max_profit: per cycle: K_call - K_put + sum premiums
strategies.max_loss: K_put - sum premiums (stock to zero while holding)
strategies.breakevens: S_T = K_put - cumulative premiums (declines each cycle)

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive, 0.2-0.3 in put phase, 0.7-0.8 in call phase

strategies.when_to_use: Range-bound or slowly rising underlying the trader is happy to own; a disciplined way to sell both sides of the variance premium sequentially rather than simultaneously (compare covered strangle).
strategies.risks: Equivalent to always being short a put (by parity the covered-call phase is a short put), so a crash is taken in full; 'strike below basis' rule can trap the trader overwriting below cost after a drop; path dependence and tax (short-term gains, QCC rules); fees from frequent rolls.
strategies.margin_note: Phase 1: cash-secured put rules; phase 2: covered call rules. Margin-secured variant uses 20%/15% rule.

strategies.metals_notes: Assigned SO/OG puts produce long futures (margin, roll yield), not metal; GLD/SLV assignment is ordinary shares.

strategies.name: Albatross (long / short)

legs.strike_rule: K1, far OTM put-side wing (a condor with a very wide body; all-call or iron form)
K3, well above forward (e.g. +8%), K3 - K2 wide
K4, far OTM call wing, K4-K3 = K2-K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Condor payoff with wide body: max(S_T-K1,0) - max(S_T-K2,0) - max(S_T-K3,0) + max(S_T-K4,0) - D (long albatross); short albatross is the credit mirror
strategies.max_profit: Long: (K2 - K1) - D for K2 <= S_T <= K3; Short: C_r outside [K1,K4]
strategies.max_loss: Long: D outside [K1,K4]; Short: (K2-K1) - C_r inside the body
strategies.breakevens: K1 + D and K4 - D (long); K1 + C_r and K4 - C_r (short)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long albatross: short (-) but small (strikes far from the money); short albatross: long (+) small
greeks_at_inception.theta: long (+) small for long albatross; (-) for short
greeks_at_inception.vega: short (-) for long albatross (credit-like range bet); long (+) for short

strategies.when_to_use: The 'wide iron condor' at the far tails: a long albatross (debit form) or the common iron form sells very low-delta strangles and buys even farther wings, collecting small credits with high win rate; the short albatross buys the far tails for a credit-financed tail bet. Realised-vs-implied: pure tail-frequency vs tail-price claim. VIX-as-IV CANNOT price the far wings: flat vol massively underprices 5-delta puts relative to the real smile, so any flat-vol albatross result is meaningless on the put side; SKEW history indicates how expensive the tails are but not strike prices. Needs chain capture.
strategies.risks: Short albatross (iron form): credit tiny vs max loss; liquidity in far wings; tail events arrive clustered; long albatross: bleeds.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: width minus credit; portfolio margin small for far-OTM shorts but spikes in stress.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists very wide strike ranges on BTC (far tails liquid relative to equities), so albatross-style tail selling/buying is common; DVOL excludes options below 5% delta in its construction, so DVOL understates far-tail richness.
strategies.metals_notes: GC far wings thin; silver tails fat; SPAN; GLD/SLV Reg T.

strategies.name: Big Lizard

legs.strike_rule: ATM, K (same strike: a short straddle)
K_c2 > K with K_c2 - K < C_r (credit exceeds width: no upside risk)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - |S_T - K| + max(S_T - K_c2, 0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r, at S_T = K
strategies.max_loss: K - C_r on the downside; upside 0 if C_r >= K_c2 - K
strategies.breakevens: K - C_r; no upside breakeven when the condition holds

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (bullish lean from the long call)
greeks_at_inception.theta: long (+), larger than the jade lizard

strategies.when_to_use: Short straddle with the upside capped by a long call: maximal theta collection with one-sided (downside) risk. Realised-vs-implied: the straddle credit is large enough that a call bought one or two strikes up still leaves credit >= width when IV is high; the trade needs realised |down-move| < C_r. VIX-as-IV CAN partially test it: with a flat smile the ATM straddle credit is correctly priced and the OTM call is slightly overpriced (equity call skew is below ATM), so a flat-vol big lizard is CONSERVATIVE for the seller on the long-call cost; the no-upside-risk condition under flat vol is testable as a function of VIX level. It CANNOT test real call-wing pricing or assignment.
strategies.risks: Full downside risk of a short ATM put; the condition fails when IV is low (long call too expensive relative to straddle); assignment on the ATM short legs (American).
strategies.margin_note: Naked-put margin plus the covered call side; portfolio margin lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: ATM BTC straddle credits are large in coin, so the condition is frequently met; the short put's coin loss is unbounded in coin as price falls toward zero (inverse); European.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI SPAN; GLD/SLV Reg T.
variants: Reverse big lizard (short straddle + long put: no downside risk, upside risk)
Big lizard with wider long call (more credit, some upside risk)

trial.statistic: condition frequency by VIX bucket; paired mean P&L difference (big lizard - short straddle) with block-bootstrap CI
trial.procedure: price straddle and +2% call at BS(VIX); check C_r >= 0.02*S; terminal payoff
trial.data: spy-daily-closes, cboe-vix-daily, fred-tbill-3m
trial.pass: condition met on >= 90% of VIX > 15 days AND lower CI of big-lizard mean P&L > 0

strategies.name: Broken-Wing (Skip-Strike) Butterfly

legs.strike_rule: K1, far OTM put wing with K2 - K1 > K3 - K2 (skipped strike)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(K3-S_T,0) - 2 max(K2-S_T,0) + max(K1-S_T,0) + C_r (set up for a net credit by widening the lower wing)
strategies.max_profit: (K3 - K2) + C_r, at S_T = K2
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - (K3 - K2) - C_r, for S_T <= K1 (the extra width of the skipped side minus credit); zero risk on the other side if C_r >= 0
strategies.breakevens: Lower: K2 - [(K3-K2) + C_r]; none on the upside when entered for a credit

greeks_at_inception.delta: small positive for the put BWB (bullish lean), negative for a call BWB

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest the skew: in index puts the body (K2) is priced on a steeper part of the smile than the near wing (K3), so the 1x2 (K3,K2) is sold rich and only part of the credit buys the far wing; the trade has no risk on one side and collects theta while the market drifts or stays. Realised-vs-implied: profit zone is 'anything but a crash beyond the lower breakeven'. VIX-as-IV CANNOT test this: with a flat smile the put BWB cannot be set up for a credit at the same widths, and the whole edge is the slope of the smile. SKEW history gives the direction and magnitude of the slope but not strike-level prices. Needs chain capture.
strategies.risks: Tail risk on the skipped side in a crash, concentrated exactly where skew premium is paid; assignment risk on the two short puts (American); wing liquidity; adjustment costs when the body is tested.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = max loss = (K2-K1)-(K3-K2)-C_r; portfolio margin lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC skew flips sign with regime (call skew in rallies), so the BWB side must follow the current smile; coarse strikes make 'skipping' a strike a large width step; European, inverse.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's call skew suggests a call BWB (skip the upper strike) as the natural structure; GC/SI SPAN margin recognises the spread; GLD/SLV Reg T.
variants: Call BWB (skip the upper wing) for upside skew
Credit BWB (no risk on one side) vs debit BWB (more profit, two-sided risk)
Unbalanced iron fly
BWB rolled out when the body is breached

strategies.name: Call Ratio Backspread
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: -max(S_T-K1,0) + 2 max(S_T-K2,0) + C_r (ideally net credit)
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited upside (slope +1 above K2)
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - C_r, at S_T = K2 (OIC: high strike - low strike - net premium paid; with a credit the loss is width - credit)
strategies.breakevens: Upper: K2 + (K2 - K1) - C_r; lower: K1 + C_r (only when entered for a debit, i.e. C_r < 0)

greeks_at_inception.delta: positive (net long one call equivalent, but depends on moneyness)

strategies.when_to_use: Long-vol, bullish-skewed structure financed by selling the near call: profits on a large rally and (if credit) small profit on a collapse; loses on a modest rise to K2. Realised-vs-implied: it buys OTM calls at the (in equities) LOWER IV of the call wing and sells the ATM at higher IV, so it is long vol and long call skew; in crypto/metals with positive call skew the pricing reverses. VIX-as-IV CANNOT test it: flat vol misprices the two strikes in opposite directions and the credit/debit outcome depends on skew. Chain capture needed; SKEW history can only say when call skew is relatively cheap.
strategies.risks: Loss zone exactly at a moderate rally; theta while waiting; two bid-ask spreads on OTM calls; assignment on the short call (American) before ex-dividend.
strategies.margin_note: Spread margin on the 1:1 part; the extra long call is paid; portfolio margin small.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC call backspreads are popular ahead of expected rallies; because BTC often has positive call skew the OTM calls are EXPENSIVE, so the structure is usually a debit; inverse settlement caps the coin payoff convexity.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold call skew makes GC call backspreads debit structures; SPAN credit for the vertical; GLD/SLV Reg T.

strategies.name: Front Ratio Spread (short ratio call / put spread)

legs.strike_rule: K2 > K1, OTM (1:2); put version mirrors below the money

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K1,0) - 2 max(S_T-K2,0) + C_r
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) + C_r, at S_T = K2 (OIC: high strike - low strike + net premium received)
strategies.max_loss: Unlimited above K2 + (K2-K1) + C_r (call version); put version: K1 - (K2... i.e. large below the lower breakeven)
strategies.breakevens: Upper: K2 + (K2 - K1) + C_r; lower: K1 - C_r only if debit

greeks_at_inception.delta: small, sign depends on strikes (call ratio: slightly positive then negative beyond K2)

strategies.when_to_use: Sells vol and skew in the direction of the extra short: the put front-ratio (long ATM put, short two OTM puts) sells the rich put wing and is the classic index skew-harvest, profitable in a drift down to K2 and in a flat market, with naked tail risk below. Realised-vs-implied: terminal move must not exceed the far breakeven; the extra short wing is where the skew premium sits. VIX-as-IV CANNOT price the skewed wing; the put front-ratio under flat vol collects too little credit (conservative) but misses the whole point of the trade. Needs chain capture.
strategies.risks: Naked tail on the ratio side; margin on one uncovered short; assignment on American shorts.
strategies.margin_note: Spread margin plus naked margin on the extra short; portfolio margin lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC call front-ratios sell the (often rich) call skew; a short naked BTC call in inverse terms has coin losses that accelerate with price, so size by coin not USD; Deribit portfolio margin.
strategies.metals_notes: GC call front-ratio is the gold skew-sale; SPAN; GLD/SLV Reg T.

strategies.name: Gamma Scalping a Long Straddle (delta-neutral)

legs.strike_rule: qty = -(delta_call + delta_put) x multiplier, rebalanced daily (or at a delta band) so net delta = 0

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Path-dependent: P&L ~ sum over rebalance intervals of 0.5 Gamma S^2 (r_realised^2 - sigma_IV^2 dt) + hedge slippage; Demeterfi et al. EQ 7 for the constant-dollar-gamma (log contract) case: payoff = sigma_R^2 - sigma_I^2 per unit variance notional
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded in principle (large realised variance); in practice bounded by gamma decaying as spot leaves K
strategies.max_loss: Premium paid D plus hedge transaction costs (if realised variance is zero and spot stays at K the loss is D)
strategies.breakevens: Realised vol over the holding period ~ implied vol at entry (exact only for constant dollar gamma; a single straddle's gamma is spot-dependent so the break-even realised vol drifts with the path)

greeks_at_inception.delta: 0 by construction, re-zeroed at each rebalance
greeks_at_inception.theta: short (-): the daily rent equals the implied-variance expectation of the gamma P&L

strategies.when_to_use: The cleanest expression of 'realised will exceed implied': the terminal directional outcome is hedged away, leaving the integral of gamma times (realised minus implied variance). VIX-as-IV on SPY history CAN test this best of all the family: price the straddle at BS(VIX), compute BS deltas daily at sigma = VIX_t (or constant entry vol), hedge with SPY closes, accumulate P&L; it CANNOT capture intraday rebalancing, the fact that SPY options are American with dividends, the discrete-hedging error (which is itself a function of realised kurtosis), or transaction costs beyond an assumed per-share cost; and the single-straddle gamma is not constant so the result is not a pure variance swap (a 1/K^2 strip would be, but needs the chain).
strategies.risks: Hedge slippage and costs eat the gamma; gamma collapses if spot trends far from K (then the position is mostly directional and needs re-striking); theta dominates in quiet regimes; jump risk is favourable for the long side but the discrete hedge misses part of it.
strategies.margin_note: Debit for the straddle; stock hedge under Reg T (50%) or portfolio margin netting; futures hedge (ES/MES) under SPAN is capital-light for SPX/XSP.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the hedge is the perpetual or dated future (24/7, funding paid/received on the perp); Greeks from public/ticker (mark_iv, greeks.delta/gamma/vega/theta) are in coin terms for inverse options, so the delta hedge must be in coin-denominated futures; realised variance includes weekends; DVOL vs realised vol (Deribit publishes realised vol too) gives the variance risk premium directly for the crypto test (~1000 days DVOL history).
strategies.metals_notes: Hedge GC/SI options with the underlying future (same clearing, SPAN offsets); GLD/SLV options hedged with the ETF under Reg T; the GC market closes briefly each day (not 24/7) so gaps exist.
variants: Short gamma scalping (short straddle, hedge daily): collects the VRP with path dependence
Delta-band rebalancing (rebalance when |delta| > 0.1) vs fixed interval
Hedging at implied vol vs at realised/forecast vol (changes P&L variance, not expectation)
Re-striking when spot moves 1 sigma
Variance-swap replication with a 1/K^2 strip (needs chain) -> the pure version
strategies.claim: A 30-DTE ATM SPY straddle bought at BS(VIX) and delta-hedged daily at the entry implied vol has mean P&L < 0 over 1993-2026 (the variance risk premium: mean VIX^2 exceeds mean realised variance), and the P&L is positively correlated (rho > 0.5) with (RV_30 - VIX_entry^2).

trial.statistic: mean hedged P&L per unit vega with studentized block-bootstrap CI; correlation of P&L with realised-minus-implied variance; also the model-free VRP = mean(VIX^2/12 - RV_30) per month
trial.procedure: for each entry date: price straddle at BS(VIX_t); each day compute BS delta at sigma = VIX_entry, hedge with SPY close, charge 1 bp per share traded; sum P&L to expiry; compute RV_30 from daily log returns; non-overlapping trades for the main CI
trial.data: spy-daily-closes, cboe-vix-daily, fred-tbill-3m
trial.pass: upper CI of mean hedged P&L < 0 AND correlation > 0.5 AND VRP lower CI > 0
trial.controls: daily (not intraday) hedging; cost parameter declared; VIX is SPX not SPY; no dividends (or SPX total return); report the fraction of P&L explained by the variance term vs hedging error; compare with BTZ 1990-2007 magnitude as an external anchor

strategies.name: Guts (long / short)

legs.strike_rule: ITM put, K_p > F, K_p > K_c

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: max(S_T-K_c,0) + max(K_p-S_T,0) - D = (K_p - K_c) + max(S_T-K_p,0) + max(K_c-S_T,0) - D: an OTM strangle plus a bond paying K_p - K_c
strategies.max_profit: Unlimited upside; K_c - [D - (K_p-K_c)] downside; short guts: max profit = C_r - (K_p - K_c)
strategies.max_loss: D - (K_p - K_c) (the premium in excess of intrinsic), for K_c <= S_T <= K_p; short guts: unlimited
strategies.when_to_use: Payoff-identical to the strangle at the same strikes (put-call parity) but with ITM options: used when ITM quotes are tighter or to avoid the OTM bid-ask, and in some venues for margin or hard-to-borrow reasons. Realised-vs-implied logic identical to strangle. VIX-as-IV tests nothing new beyond the strangle; the only guts-specific claim is parity, which needs captured chains.
strategies.risks: Large debit tied up in intrinsic; ITM legs assignable early (American) especially puts when rates are high and calls before ex-dividend; wider ITM spreads in practice.
strategies.margin_note: Debit; short guts margined as a naked straddle/strangle with intrinsic.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit European options remove early-assignment risk from ITM legs; ITM option premiums in coin are large (inverse), so guts tie up more coin margin than a strangle.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI American ITM puts carry early-exercise value when rates are high; SPAN; GLD/SLV Reg T.

strategies.name: Iron Butterfly (short, credit)

legs.strike_rule: K3 (upper wing), K3 - K2 = K2 - K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - |S_T - K2| + max(K1 - S_T, 0) + max(S_T - K3, 0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net credit), at S_T = K2 (OIC: net premium received)
strategies.max_loss: (K3 - K2) - C_r, for S_T <= K1 or >= K3 (OIC: high strike - middle strike - net premium received)
strategies.when_to_use: A short straddle with bought wings: same VRP harvest, defined risk. Named by OIC 'short iron butterfly' (credit); it is payoff-equivalent to the long call/put butterfly plus a cash position. Realised-vs-implied: profits if |realised move| < C_r; the wings cost part of the straddle credit, and that cost is where skew matters (put wing rich). VIX-as-IV CAN test the flat-vol iron fly (conservative for the seller: flat vol overprices the put wing cost? No: flat vol UNDERprices the put wing the seller buys, so the flat test is slightly OPTIMISTIC on the wing cost and PESSIMISTIC on the short put collected; net bias small for symmetric wings and documented); it CANNOT test real wing pricing or the pin behaviour at expiry.
strategies.risks: Narrow max-profit point; wings reduce credit substantially when near; four legs of spreads; assignment on the short body (American).
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = max loss = wing width - credit; portfolio margin similar.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit portfolio margin recognises the wings; inverse settlement means the USD max loss on the put side is realised in appreciating coin on the call side and vice versa; all European, 08:00 UTC expiry.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI iron flies get SPAN spread credit; GLD/SLV defined-risk Reg T margin.

strategies.name: Iron Condor (short, credit)

legs.strike_rule: K3, OTM call (16-20 delta), K3 > K2
K4 (upper wing), K4 - K3 = K2 - K1

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - max(K2 - S_T,0) + max(K1 - S_T,0) - max(S_T - K3,0) + max(S_T - K4,0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net credit), for K2 <= S_T <= K3
strategies.max_loss: (K4 - K3) - C_r = (K2 - K1) - C_r for equal widths (OIC: spread width - net premium received)
strategies.when_to_use: A short strangle with bought wings: defined-risk VRP harvest. OIC labels the credit version 'short condor (iron condor)'. Realised-vs-implied: profits when the terminal move stays inside the short strikes; the credit/width ratio is the market's implied probability of breaching, so the claim is that realised breach frequency is below implied. VIX-as-IV CAN test the flat-vol iron condor (conservative for the seller on the put spread since flat vol underprices the short put more than the long put; slightly optimistic on the call spread); it CANNOT test real smile pricing, the width/credit trade-off traders actually face, or early-management rules that depend on intraday marks.
strategies.risks: Loss/credit ratio typically 3-10x so a few breaches erase many winners; both sides can be tested in a whipsaw; vega exposure during spikes even inside the strikes; assignment on short legs (American) near ex-dividend.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: margin = max loss on one side (brokers margin one side for equal widths); portfolio margin similar or lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit iron condors: strikes coarse so widths are large; portfolio margin recognises wings; the inverse structure means the USD max loss on the put side is partially offset by coin appreciation in a rally scenario only; realised BTC 30-day vol frequently exceeds DVOL in trend regimes, making condors breach more often than in equities.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI condors: SPAN; silver breaches more than gold for the same delta because of fatter tails; GLD/SLV Reg T defined-risk.

strategies.name: Jade Lizard

legs.strike_rule: K_c2 > K_c1 with K_c2 - K_c1 < C_r (total credit exceeds call-spread width: no upside risk)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - max(K_p - S_T,0) - max(S_T - K_c1,0) + max(S_T - K_c2,0)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net credit), for K_p <= S_T <= K_c1
strategies.max_loss: K_p - C_r on the downside (S_T = 0); upside loss = 0 when C_r >= K_c2 - K_c1, otherwise (K_c2 - K_c1) - C_r
strategies.breakevens: K_p - C_r; no upside breakeven when C_r >= K_c2 - K_c1
strategies.when_to_use: Short strangle with the upside tail removed: sells the rich put (skew premium) and a call spread whose credit, added to the put's, covers the call-spread width. Realised-vs-implied: profits unless the underlying falls through K_p - C_r; the construction works only when IV and put skew are high enough that the credit exceeds the call-spread width. VIX-as-IV CANNOT test it: under a flat smile the credit rarely exceeds the width at reasonable strikes and the actual edge is the put-call skew differential; needs chain capture. SKEW history can describe when the condition is likely met but not price it.
strategies.risks: Full downside risk of a naked put; the 'no upside risk' condition fails after the credit is spent on adjustments; assignment on the short put (American) near ex-dividend.
strategies.margin_note: Naked-put margin (Reg T ~20% of underlying less OTM + premium) plus defined-risk call spread; portfolio margin lower.
strategies.crypto_notes: In BTC the natural skew is often on the call side, so the mirror (reverse jade lizard: short call + short put spread) is the skew-harvesting version; inverse settlement makes the short put's USD loss bounded but the coin loss grows as price falls; European, portfolio margin.

strategies.when_to_use: Bet that the underlying finishes near K2 with bounded risk: a short-vol / short-gamma view with a cheap debit. strategies.when_to_use: Expect realised vol over the holding period to exceed implied, or an IV repricing event (earnings, FOMC, CPI, protocol upgrade) priced below the historical move. Realised-vs-implied: the trade pays iff the terminal |move| exceeds D, and D is ~0.8*sigma_IV*S*sqrt(T) for a 30-day ATM straddle, so the hurdle move is a direct function of IV. VIX-as-IV on SPY history CAN test the unconditional and VIX-conditioned expectancy of a 30-DTE ATM straddle held to expiry (price it with BS at sigma = VIX/100). It CANNOT test fills/bid-ask, pin risk, intraday exits, non-30-day tenors, or any strike away from the money (VIX is a strike-integrated number and carries no skew).
strategies.risks: Theta bleed if nothing happens; IV crush after the event often exceeds the move; large bid-ask on two legs; assignment on SPY (American) legs if deep ITM near ex-dividend; 30-day VIX horizon vs weekly structures mismatch.
strategies.margin_note: Full debit paid; no margin. SPX/XSP cash-settled European, Section 1256 60/40; SPY American physical delivery.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit BTC/ETH options are European, inverse (premium and P&L in coin, 1 contract = 1 BTC or 1 ETH), expire 08:00 UTC, trade 24/7 so weekend realised vol counts; no dividends; use the futures of matching expiry (not spot) as the forward, so basis/funding enters the ATM strike choice. DVOL is the analogue of VIX (30-day, variance-swap style, interpolated across the two expiries bracketing 30 days) and has ~1000 days of history via public/get_volatility_index_data (resolution 1D). Linear USDC options also exist.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI options are American options on futures (settle into the futures contract), margined under SPAN as a portfolio, Section 1256 60/40 and year-end mark-to-market (26 USC 1256(a)). GLD/SLV options are American equity options on a grantor trust, equity-style Reg T margin, not 1256 (and the trust shares themselves are taxed as collectibles). CME pages returned 503 during this run, so the CME specifics above are from prior knowledge, not a fetched page.

strategies.when_to_use: Harvest the variance risk premium: implied vol exceeds subsequently realised vol on average for equity indices (BTZ 2009 report mean VIX^2 - RV of 18.3 in annualised %^2 units, 1990-2007; mean IV 33.2 vs RV 14.9). Best when IV is elevated relative to recent realised and no scheduled event sits inside the tenor. VIX-as-IV on SPY history CAN test the sign and conditional structure of the ATM short-straddle premium (it is the mirror of the long straddle test) and whether conditioning on VIX - realised-20d or VIX3M - VIX improves it. It CANNOT test the tail of the P&L distribution realistically because the historical sample has few crash days relative to the risk, nor the margin calls/forced liquidation that actually end short-straddle programs, nor skew.
strategies.risks: Unbounded loss; gap risk; margin expansion in a vol spike forces liquidation at the worst time; negative skew of returns makes Sharpe misleading (use PSR/DSR with skew/kurtosis); early assignment on SPY/GLD/SLV legs.
strategies.margin_note: Equity/ETF (Reg T): greater of the two naked requirements (20% of underlying +/- OTM amount + premium, min 10%) plus the other premium; portfolio margin lower. SPX: same formula on index level, cash settled, 1256. Futures options: SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the short straddle is written in coin terms: a short BTC straddle loses coin as BTC rallies (inverse payoff convexity) and gains in coin but loses in USD as BTC crashes; the USD loss on the put is capped by the inverse structure. Margin for short options is coin-denominated (initial margin roughly max(0.15 - OTM%, 0.10) * contract + mark, maintenance 0.075 + mark on BTC; see Deribit margin KB). 24/7 means weekend gaps hit without the ability to adjust via the underlying only if the futures are also used (they trade 24/7 too). DVOL vs realised vol gives the crypto VRP test directly.

strategies.name: Short Strangle

legs.strike_rule: OTM, K_p < F (16-30 delta), K_p < K_c

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: C_r - max(S_T - K_c, 0) - max(K_p - S_T, 0)

strategies.when_to_use: The workhorse premium-selling structure: collects the VRP plus the skew premium on the put wing, with a wide profit zone. Realised-vs-implied: profit iff the realised terminal move stays inside the strikes widened by the credit; the implied probability of that is given by the smile. VIX-as-IV CAN test the flat-vol short strangle, which is CONSERVATIVE for the seller (flat vol underprices the put the seller collects), so a positive flat-vol result is robust to skew; it CANNOT quantify the extra skew premium, the tail-loss distribution with few crash observations, or margin-driven forced exits.
strategies.risks: Tail risk unbounded on the call side and large on the put side; vol spike raises margin; correlated losses across underlyings in a market crash; pin/assignment risk on American legs.
strategies.margin_note: Reg T: naked margin on the larger side plus the other premium; portfolio margin typically 3-5x more capital-efficient; SPAN on futures options; Deribit coin margin.
strategies.crypto_notes: Short BTC strangles on Deribit: the call side is the dangerous side in USD terms (inverse payoff means the coin loss on a short call accelerates as price rises); DVOL vs realised is the crypto VRP, historically positive on average but with violent inversions (e.g. March 2020, Nov 2022). 24/7: no overnight gap protection from closed markets.
strategies.metals_notes: GC/SI short strangles: SPAN margin, 1256 tax; silver's realised vol is roughly 1.5-2x gold's and both have event-driven gaps on CPI/FOMC. GLD/SLV: Reg T.

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Wide iron condor/iron fly payoff: C_r - short strangle/straddle intrinsic + wing intrinsic; with 2 wings per short the payoff turns UP again beyond the wings (long tail)
strategies.max_profit: C_r (net of wing cost), for K2 <= S_T <= K3
strategies.max_loss: (K2 - K1) - C_r (1:1 wings); with 2:1 wings the loss is capped at the same point and profit resumes beyond K1 - (K2-K1)

greeks_at_inception.gamma: short (-) near the money, long (+) far in the tails
greeks_at_inception.vega: short (-) in ATM vega, long (+) in wing vega (vega-of-skew exposure)

strategies.when_to_use: The institutional form of premium selling: harvest the VRP at the centre while owning the tails so a crash does not end the program. The question is whether the wing cost (which is where the skew premium is richest) consumes the VRP. Realised-vs-implied: the centre collects implied minus realised; the wings pay the implied minus realised tail frequency, which in equities has historically been even more negative for the buyer. VIX-as-IV CAN test the centre (ATM/near-ATM) and CANNOT price the 5-delta wings (flat vol underprices them by a large factor), so the flat test overstates the strategy; it can bound the answer: if the flat-wing version already fails, the real one fails harder. The realistic test needs chain capture plus a stress episode.
strategies.risks: Wing cost drag; the wings help only beyond K1, so the drawdown between K2 and K1 is real; vega-of-skew blowout marks the position badly before expiry even if the terminal payoff is fine; margin still spikes on the short centre.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk: width minus credit; portfolio margin recognises the wings; SPAN for futures options.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit wings are relatively liquid far OTM; DVOL excludes < 5-delta options so wing richness is not in DVOL; coin-denominated short call risk makes the call wing the important one for coin-based books.
strategies.metals_notes: GC: call wing is the expensive one; SPAN; GLD/SLV Reg T.

legs.strike_rule: ATM (nearest strike to the BTC index forward)
BTC-PERPETUAL delta hedge, rebalance every 8h funding interval or daily

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Inverse: each option pays max(S_T-K,0)/S_T (call) or max(K-S_T,0)/S_T (put) in BTC. Short straddle P&L in BTC = C0_btc - |S_T-K|/S_T; in USD ~ C0_usd - |S_T-K| with a convexity correction from the BTC denomination. Delta-hedged: ~0.5*Vega*(DVOL_entry - RV_365) per cycle plus/minus funding on the perp hedge.
strategies.max_profit: Straddle premium (in BTC, convert at S_T).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded on the upside in USD terms; on the downside the inverse put's BTC payoff (K-S_T)/S_T grows hyperbolically as S_T -> 0 (BTC-denominated loss is convex), though USD loss is bounded by K.
strategies.breakevens: K +/- C0 (USD, approximately); RV = DVOL hedged.

greeks_at_inception.theta: positive (365-day calendar: theta accrues over weekends)

strategies.when_to_use: When DVOL exceeds 30-day realised BTC vol by a wide margin, no scheduled catalyst (FOMC, ETF flows data, large expiries), and perp funding is positive (a short perp hedge then earns funding only if the book is net short perp; a long perp hedge pays it).
strategies.risks: BTC moves 10-20% in a day with no circuit breakers; 24/7 means gaps are replaced by continuous but violent moves; exchange/counterparty risk (offshore venue; US persons restricted on Deribit; Coinbase Derivatives / CME BTC options are the regulated route); liquidation mechanics on portfolio margin; funding can flip.
strategies.margin_note: Deribit portfolio margin (SPAN-like, in BTC); options are European, cash-settled in BTC at 08:00 UTC; fee cap 12.5% of option premium. US-regulated routes: IBIT options (American, physical delivery of IBIT shares, equity margin, not 1256), CME BTC options (on futures, 1256), Coinbase Derivatives.
strategies.crypto_notes: DVOL is Deribit's 30-day implied vol index (VIX-like strip on BTC options; ~1000 days of history via public/get_volatility_index_data); realised vol uses 365 days/year; no dividends; the delta hedge is a perpetual swap with 8-hourly funding, which enters the P&L as carry; weekend realised vol is real P&L. ETH twin with ETH DVOL. IBIT options give a US-regulated, USD-settled, American-style route with the ETF's NAV basis and 9:30-16:00 hours (gap risk over weekends when BTC trades).

strategies.name: Calendar vol spread (ATM time spread, long or reverse)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At the near expiry: value = C_far(S_T, T_far - T_near) - (S_T - K)^+ - D0, where D0 = C_far - C_near is the debit. Tent-shaped: max near S_T = K, both tails converge to -D0 (far option retains only vol value). Reverse calendar (long near, short far) is the mirror with credit and unbounded-ish tail risk when far IV rises.
strategies.max_profit: Long calendar: approx. C_far(K, T_far-T_near, sigma_far) - D0 at S_T=K (depends on far IV at near expiry). Reverse calendar: the credit C0 when S_T far from K and far IV collapses.
strategies.max_loss: Long calendar: D0. Reverse calendar: C_far(K, T_far-T_near, sigma_far') - C0, large if far IV rises (effectively uncapped in IV).
strategies.breakevens: Two points where C_far(S_T, tau) = (S_T-K)^+ + D0; solved numerically (the engine's breakevens() on the near-expiry grid with the far leg marked at its implied vol).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long calendar: negative (short near gamma dominates)
greeks_at_inception.theta: long calendar: positive (near theta > far theta)

strategies.when_to_use: Long calendar when the term structure is flat or inverted (near IV >= far IV: backwardation, VIX > VIX3M) and you expect near realised vol below near implied; reverse calendar when the curve is steep and you expect a front-end vol event (earnings, FOMC, CPI).
strategies.risks: Long calendar: a large move takes spot away from K and both legs lose; far IV can fall (term structure flattens) when the market calms; early assignment on American short near leg. Reverse calendar: far vega blow-up in a crash.
strategies.margin_note: Long calendar: debit only (same strike, long leg later-dated -> covered). Reverse calendar: short far leg is treated as naked on Reg-T; PM stress on vega.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly expiries so calendars can be very short-dated; all legs European, settle in BTC at 08:00 UTC, no early assignment. BTC term structure is often in steep contango in calm markets and inverts violently in crashes; funding is irrelevant unless delta-hedged with the perp.
strategies.metals_notes: GC calendars: both legs are options on different futures contracts (serial vs quarterly) so there is a futures-spread basis inside the calendar; American exercise means an ITM short near leg can be assigned into a futures position. GLD/SLV calendars are plain equity calendars; Section 1256 on GC.

strategies.name: Conditional VRP: trade only when implied-minus-realised spread is wide

legs.expiry_rule: 30 DTE; entered only when IV - RV_forecast > threshold; otherwise flat (or reversed when spread < -threshold)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Same as the delta-hedged straddle: ~0.5*Vega*(IV - RV)*scale per cycle, but only in cycles where the entry spread z = (IV - RV_hat)/sd exceeds z*; when z < -z* the position is reversed (long straddle, gamma scalping).
strategies.max_profit: Straddle credit per active cycle (short) / unbounded (long cycles).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded on short cycles (jump); premium paid on long cycles.
strategies.when_to_use: Treat the IV-RV spread as the single statistic: trade vol only when the premium is wide relative to a realised-vol forecast (HAR/EWMA) and stand aside or go long when implied is below forecast realised (pre-crisis 'cheap vol' regimes).
strategies.risks: The forecast is backward-looking; the widest spreads occur right after spikes when vol-of-vol is highest; overfitting the threshold; long-vol cycles bleed theta.
strategies.margin_note: As short straddle when active (naked straddle margin / PM stress); long cycles are debit only.
strategies.crypto_notes: Use DVOL minus 30-day realised (365-day annualisation) as the statistic; Deribit inverse straddles, perp hedge with funding; the DVOL-RV spread is much noisier than VIX-RV and its sign flips in bull runs when realised vol outruns implied.

ATM on each sector ETF, same weights

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Vega-weighted: P&L ~ sum_i w_i Vega_i (RV_i - IV_i) - Vega_SPY (RV_SPY - IV_SPY) = short the implied cross-sector correlation. Fewer legs than single-stock dispersion (sector ETFs are liquid, no earnings jumps) at the cost of a smaller correlation premium.
strategies.max_profit: SPY straddle credit when sectors move against each other and the index is flat.
strategies.max_loss: Large when all sectors move together (correlation -> 1, risk-off).

strategies.name: Cross-asset implied vol ratio trades (GVZ/VIX, DVOL/VIX, OVX/VIX)

legs.strike_rule: ATM on the cheap-vol asset (e.g. GLD when GVZ/VIX is at a low percentile)
ATM on the rich-vol asset (SPY), qty = Vega_long/Vega_short

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Hedged: P&L ~ Vega*[(RV_A - IV_A) - (RV_B - IV_B)], a bet that the implied vol ratio IV_A/IV_B reverts toward its historical mean while realised ratios stay put.
strategies.max_profit: Unbounded (long straddle leg) less short straddle losses.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded if the rich asset realises far more than the cheap one (e.g. long GLD vol / short SPY vol into an equity crash).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 net dollar gamma, long in A, short in B
greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 net; long the vol ratio A/B

strategies.when_to_use: When a cross-asset implied vol ratio (GVZ/VIX historically ~0.9-1.2; DVOL/VIX ~2.5-4; OVX/VIX ~1.5-2.5) is at a multi-year extreme and the realised-vol ratio has not moved; also as a hedge: long gold vol vs short equity vol when both are cheap but gold vol is cheaper.
strategies.risks: Ratios shift regime (2024-26 gold vol repricing); correlation between the two assets' vol spikes is unstable; two hedging programs; the short leg can be the one that explodes.
strategies.margin_note: Short straddle leg margin (naked); PM offsets minimal across asset classes (GLD vs SPY are different class groups). GC/SI route via SPAN; Deribit route separate venue margin, no cross-margin with US equity options.

strategies.name: Cross-index vol spread (QQQ vs SPY, IWM vs SPY straddle pairs)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Delta-hedged: P&L ~ Vega*[(RV_QQQ - IV_QQQ) - (RV_SPY - IV_SPY)]: long the realised-minus-implied of one index against the other; profits when the VXN-VIX (or RVX-VIX) spread was too narrow at entry and widens, or when QQQ realises relatively more.
strategies.max_profit: Bounded by the short SPY straddle credit plus unbounded QQQ straddle gain in a QQQ-specific move.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded if SPY moves a lot while QQQ does not (rare, but the ratio of vols can swing in a sector shock).
strategies.breakevens: RV_QQQ - RV_SPY = IV_QQQ - IV_SPY (realised vol spread equals implied vol spread).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 net (long QQQ gamma, short SPY gamma)

strategies.when_to_use: When the implied vol spread between two correlated indices (VXN-VIX, RVX-VIX, VXD-VIX) is at an extreme z-score relative to its history and relative to the realised vol spread; mean-reversion of the ratio.
strategies.risks: The spread is regime-dependent (tech-led markets widen VXN-VIX persistently); two sets of hedging costs; basis between ETF options and the CBOE indices.
strategies.margin_note: Short straddle leg naked-margined; PM offsets across correlated indices (SPY/QQQ in the same class group ~ 70-90% offset); Reg-T none.
strategies.crypto_notes: ETH vs BTC vol spread is the crypto twin: Deribit ETH DVOL vs BTC DVOL ratio (historically 1.2-1.5) mean-reverts; both inverse, each hedged with its own perp; IBIT vs ETHA options are the US-regulated route.

strategies.name: Dispersion trade (short index vol, long component vol)

legs.strike_rule: ATM on each of the top-N components, qty_i = w_i * (index vega / component vega) (vega-weighted)
ATM on each component, same weights

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: P&L ~ sum_i w_i*Vega_i*(RV_i - IV_i) - Vega_idx*(RV_idx - IV_idx). Since sigma_idx^2 = sum_i sum_j w_i w_j rho_ij sigma_i sigma_j, this is a short position in correlation: profits when realised correlation < implied correlation (components move idiosyncratically while the index stays calm).
strategies.max_profit: Bounded by index straddle credit when components move but the index does not; in practice ~ vega notional x (implied corr - realised corr) x average component vol.
strategies.max_loss: Large when correlation spikes to 1 in a crash: the index straddle loses with full gamma while component straddles gain less than their sum implies; plus hedging costs on N legs.
strategies.breakevens: Realised correlation = implied correlation (COR1M-style), i.e. rho_realised = (IV_idx^2 - sum w_i^2 IV_i^2) / (sum_{i!=j} w_i w_j IV_i IV_j).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 net dollar gamma by construction (vega-weighted), long idiosyncratic gamma, short systematic gamma
greeks_at_inception.theta: ~0 to slightly negative (component straddles cost more theta than the index straddle)

strategies.when_to_use: When implied correlation (Cboe COR1M / COR3M) is high relative to realised, i.e. index vol is rich relative to the component basket; typically in calm markets with structured-product flows selling single-name vol and buying index vol.
strategies.risks: Correlation spikes to 1 in crises (the trade is short crash correlation); N-leg execution and hedging costs; component earnings events move single-name IV; weight drift; capacity.
strategies.margin_note: Index straddle short is naked-straddle margin; component straddles are long (debit). PM nets the vega across legs; Reg-T does not. SPX leg cash-settled, Section 1256; component legs American equity options.

Inverse settlement in each coin, hedge each with its perp.
strategies.metals_notes: Metals dispersion: long GLD + SLV straddles vs short a GDX (miners) straddle, or gold vs silver vol ratio (SI IV ~2x GC IV). GC/SI options American on futures, SPAN; GLD/SLV equity options.

legs.expiry_rule: first expiry after the event (1-7 DTE), entered the day before the event

strategies.max_profit: C0 (realised move zero).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded upside; K - C0 downside.

greeks_at_inception.theta: very positive (the event premium collapses at the print)

strategies.name: Forward-start variance / term-premium strip (long far strip, short near strip)

legs.strike_rule: all K < F (near expiry), weight 2/(T_near*K^2) scaled by T_near/T_far
all K > F (near expiry), same scaling

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Short forward variance over [T_near, T_far] at strike F^2 = (T_far*K_far - T_near*K_near)/(T_far - T_near) (for SPX: (3*VIX3M^2 - VIX^2)/2 for 1m-3m). After T_near the position is a plain short variance swap over the forward window; P&L = N*(F^2 - RV(T_near..T_far)).
strategies.max_profit: N*F^2 (forward realised variance zero).
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded in forward realised variance.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 until T_near (near long gamma offsets far short gamma), then negative
greeks_at_inception.vega: negative to far-dated vol, positive to near-dated: short the term-structure slope

strategies.when_to_use: When the VIX term structure is steep (VIX3M >> VIX): the forward variance embeds both the VRP and a term premium; this isolates the forward window so a near-term event does not hurt; the variance-swap analogue of the reverse calendar.
strategies.risks: A shock inside the forward window; the near strip's gamma must be hedged until it expires; execution of two strips (40-100 strikes); truncation error on the far strip.
strategies.margin_note: Short far strip is naked margin (PM nets against the near long strip until T_near); SPX cash-settled, European, 1256; ES futures hedge SPAN.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit lists quarterly and monthly expiries so forward variance strips are buildable; inverse settlement, hedge with perp; BTC term structure is steep in contango in calm bull markets (forward premium large) and inverts in crashes.
strategies.metals_notes: GC options on serial and quarterly futures: the forward window spans different futures contracts (calendar basis); American exercise complicates the strip; GLD strip is cleaner.

trial.statistic: Mean of (F^2 - RV(22..63))/F^2 versus mean of (VIX^2 - RV(1..21))/VIX^2; win rates; simulated forward-strip P&L.
trial.null: Forward premium ratio <= spot premium ratio.

trial.data: CBOE VIX, VIX3M history, SPY closes, current SPX chain.
trial.pass: Paired difference > 0 with 95% CI excluding zero; forward win rate > 0.7.
trial.controls: Shuffled VIX3M placebo; exclude 2008/2020 sensitivity.

strategies.name: Gold volatility premium (GVZ) via GLD straddles / GC strangles

legs.strike_rule: GLD shares or GC/MGC futures delta hedge daily

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Delta-hedged short straddle: ~0.5*Vega*(GVZ_entry - RV_GLD) per cycle; GVZ is the 30-day implied vol of GLD computed by the VIX methodology so it is the natural strike.
strategies.max_profit: Straddle credit C0 (unhedged, at K); hedged bounded by C0.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded on a gold gap (hedged: in realised variance). Gold gaps on geopolitical events and liquidity squeezes (Mar 2020: -12% in a week then +).
strategies.breakevens: K +/- C0 unhedged; RV = GVZ hedged.
strategies.when_to_use: When GVZ exceeds gold's trailing realised vol by a wide margin and no scheduled catalyst (FOMC, CPI) falls inside the window; gold's VRP is smaller and less reliable than equity's because gold vol spikes on upside moves too.

Silver: SLV straddles or SI options; no official silver vol index now (VXSLV discontinued), so compute 30-day ATM IV from the SLV chain capture. Platinum/palladium: PL/PA options are thin.

strategies.name: Put-skew richness sale (1x2 put ratio spread, delta-hedged)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Net credit C0 = 2P(K1) - P(K2) (usually > 0 when skew is steep). Above K2: +C0. Between K1 and K2: C0 + (K2 - S_T). Below K1: C0 + (K2 - K1) - (K1 - S_T), i.e. loss grows 1:1 below K1 - (K2-K1) - C0.
strategies.max_profit: (K2 - K1) + C0 at S_T = K1.
strategies.max_loss: Unbounded below: K1 - (K2 - K1) - C0 to zero, i.e. max loss = 2*K1 - K2 - C0 (stock to zero).
strategies.breakevens: S* = 2*K1 - K2 - C0 (lower). No upper breakeven when C0 > 0.

greeks_at_inception.delta: slightly positive (net short puts); hedged to 0
greeks_at_inception.gamma: negative in the tail (short 2 far puts), ~flat near spot
greeks_at_inception.vega: short vega concentrated at K1 (10d) and long at K2 (25d): a short skew-steepness position; net vega small negative

strategies.when_to_use: When 10d-25d put IV slope is steep relative to history (SKEW high, VIX moderate); harvests the convexity premium in far OTM puts that CBOE SKEW white paper translates into implied tail probabilities far above realised.
strategies.risks: Gap/crash below K1: loss accelerates exactly when skew and IV explode and liquidity vanishes; hedging cost; assignment on American ETF options; the second short put is naked for margin.
strategies.margin_note: One put is covered by the long; the extra short put is naked: Reg-T ~20% rule; PM stress -12%. Index (SPX) cash-settled, no early assignment, Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC put skew steepens in drawdowns and flattens or inverts in rallies; on Deribit the inverse payoff means a short put loses BTC-denominated value faster as BTC falls (payoff (K-S)/S in BTC), so the tail loss in BTC terms is convex. Settlement 08:00 UTC, European, hedge with perp (funding).
strategies.metals_notes: Gold's downside skew is usually flatter than equity's so the credit is smaller; silver has fat two-sided tails. GC/SI options American on futures, SPAN margin nets the ratio spread as a single risk array; Section 1256.
variants: 1x3 put ratio (steeper skew bet)
Put ratio with far put bought back as a 'broken wing' to cap tail loss (1x2x1)
Christmas tree put (K3 long, K2 short, K1 short)

strategies.claim: The CBOE SKEW-implied risk-adjusted probability of a one-month S&P 500 log-return below -2 sigma exceeds the realised frequency over the following month on average by more than 2 percentage points, and the gap is widest when SKEW > 135.

trial.statistic: Mean of (SKEW-implied 2-sigma probability from the CBOE white paper table, interpolated) minus realised indicator that the 21d SPY log return < -2*VIX*sqrt(21/252); also conditional mean for SKEW > 135.
trial.null: Implied probability equals realised frequency (zero tail premium).
trial.procedure: Non-overlapping 21d windows since 1990; studentized block bootstrap on the gap; walk-forward check that the gap is positive in each of 3 sub-periods; PBO on the 135 threshold vs alternatives 125/130/140.
trial.data: CBOE SKEW history, VIX history, SPY daily closes.
trial.pass: Gap > 0.02 with bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero, positive in >= 2 of 3 sub-periods, PBO < 0.3.
trial.controls: Same test with VIX-only normal model (no SKEW) to show SKEW adds information; shuffled SKEW placebo.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Add a 'skew_implied_tail' statistic to harness_skew_tail using the CBOE white-paper mapping (100 -> 2.3%, 145 -> 14.45%, interpolate); P&L of the 1x2 needs surface_summary 10d/25d IVs, which accumulate from today.

strategies.name: Risk reversal (25-delta skew trade)

legs.strike_rule: spot (delta hedge to flat, re-hedge daily)

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Unhedged: (S_T-Kc)^+ - (Kp-S_T)^+ + C0 where C0 = P(Kp)-C(Kc) is the net credit (positive when put skew is rich). Flat between Kp and Kc at +C0; linear long above Kc, linear long (loss) below Kp. The delta-hedged version isolates the skew-vega P&L: profit as 25d put IV minus 25d call IV compresses.
strategies.max_profit: Unhedged: unbounded above Kc (S_T - Kc + C0). Delta-hedged: approx. vega_25d x (skew_entry - skew_exit) + carry.
strategies.max_loss: Unhedged: Kp - C0 (stock to zero). Delta-hedged: bounded only by gap risk below Kp; a crash widens skew AND moves spot against the short put.
strategies.breakevens: Unhedged: S* = Kp - C0 on the downside (if C0 > 0 there is no upside breakeven; the position is never negative between the strikes).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: near zero net; negative below Kp, positive above Kc (short put gamma dominates in a selloff)
greeks_at_inception.theta: slightly positive when net credit (rich put decays faster)
greeks_at_inception.vega: near zero flat-vega; strongly short skew-vega (loses when put IV rises relative to call IV)

strategies.when_to_use: When 25d put-call IV skew (or CBOE SKEW) is at a high percentile of its history and the trader believes the tail is overpriced; also as a cheap synthetic long replacement in uptrends.
strategies.risks: Crash risk on the short put with skew expansion at the same time; pin/assignment on American ETF options; the hedge bleeds in whipsaw markets; margin spikes with VIX.
strategies.margin_note: Equity/ETF: Reg-T treats the short put as naked (20% of underlying - OTM amount + premium, min 10%); portfolio margin ~15% stress. SPX/XSP: cash-settled, Section 1256, PM stress test -12%/+10%.
strategies.crypto_notes: On Deribit the BTC skew is frequently positive (call-rich) in bull markets, so the trade often runs the other way (short 25d call, long 25d put). Options are European, inverse (premium and settlement in BTC at 08:00 UTC), 24/7, no dividends; the delta hedge is a perpetual swap paying/receiving funding, which is a carry term the equity version does not have.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold skew is usually call-rich (fear bid is on the upside), so the metals risk reversal is often short call / long put. GC options are American, exercise into a futures position, SPAN futures-style margin, Section 1256 60/40. GLD/SLV options are the equity route (American, physically settled in ETF shares, GLD is a grantor trust taxed as collectibles on the shares).

strategies.claim: When CBOE SKEW is above its rolling 1-year 80th percentile, the subsequent 21-trading-day SPY realised return skewness and the frequency of < -2 sigma days are not worse than when SKEW is below its 20th percentile, so the extra premium in OTM puts (risk-reversal credit) is a positive-expectancy sale.

trial.statistic: Difference in mean 21d SPY log-return skewness and in frequency of returns below -2*VIX-implied sigma, high-SKEW months minus low-SKEW months; plus mean SKEW-implied 2-sigma probability (CBOE table) minus realised frequency.
trial.null: Tail frequency and realised skewness are the same in high-SKEW and low-SKEW regimes (SKEW has no information, or is fairly priced).
trial.procedure: Daily SKEW and SPY closes since 1990; non-overlapping 21d windows; sort by SKEW percentile at window start; walk-forward with expanding percentile windows; studentized block bootstrap (block 21d) on the difference; deflate for the 2 thresholds tried.
trial.data: CBOE SKEW daily history, SPY daily closes, VIX daily history (for the sigma scale).
trial.pass: Realised -2 sigma frequency in high-SKEW regime <= SKEW-implied probability minus 2 bootstrap SE, and the regime difference in realised skewness is not significantly negative (p>0.1); the implied-minus-realised tail gap is > 0 at p<0.05.
trial.controls: Shuffled-SKEW placebo; VIX-level control (condition on VIX terciles so SKEW is not proxying for VIX); exclude Oct-2008 and Mar-2020 as a sensitivity run.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Extend harness_skew_tail: bucket by SKEW percentile, compare CBOE-table implied 2-sigma probability vs realised frequency; log skew-vega P&L once surface_summary 25d put/call IVs have 60+ captures.

strategies.name: Skew term-structure trade (near vs far put skew)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: At near expiry: near risk reversal payoff (S_T-Kc_n)^+ - (Kp_n-S_T)^+ plus the marked far reverse risk reversal, net of entry credit/debit. The trade is short near-dated skew and long far-dated skew: profits when the near skew (steeper, in vol points per delta) flattens relative to the far skew, as near-dated puts decay fastest.
strategies.max_profit: Bounded near expiry by the near RR credit plus far skew gains; not closed form (mark far legs).
strategies.max_loss: Crash: near short put loses 1:1 while far long put gains less than 1:1 (lower delta) and skew-term inverts; effectively the near put's downside Kp_n - credit, offset partially by the far put.
strategies.breakevens: Numerical on the engine grid with far legs marked at their IVs.

greeks_at_inception.vega: ~0 flat vega; short near skew-vega, long far skew-vega

strategies.when_to_use: When the near-dated skew is much steeper than far-dated (SKEW high, VIX low, pre-event hedging flows concentrated in front months): sells the front-end tail premium while keeping longer-dated crash protection.
strategies.risks: Crash before near expiry; skew term inversion (near skew flattens because spot falls, not because puts cheapen); 4 legs plus hedge.
strategies.margin_note: Near short put partially covered by far long put (diagonal spread treatment under Reg-T if far expiry >= near); far short call naked unless PM. SPX cash-settled, 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC skew term structure flips sign frequently (near-dated put skew in drawdowns, far-dated call skew in bull markets); Deribit mark_iv per strike makes it observable; inverse, European, perp hedge.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold skew is call-side; the trade mirrors (short near call skew, long far call skew). GC American into futures, SPAN; GLD equity options.

Diagonal risk reversal

trial.null: Near skew <= far skew or the spread does not decay (no term premium in skew).

trial.controls: Flat-vega risk reversal (single expiry) control; SKEW-index level stratification.

strategies.name: SKEW-conditioned tail hedge (put spread when skew is cheap)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Debit D0 = P(K2) - P(K1). Above K2: -D0. Between: (K2 - S_T) - D0. Below K1: (K2 - K1) - D0.
strategies.max_loss: D0 (the debit).

greeks_at_inception.gamma: positive near K2, negative near K1
greeks_at_inception.vega: long vega at K2, short at K1: long skew-steepness, net vega small positive

strategies.when_to_use: Buy protection when SKEW is low (tail cheap) and VIX is low; the spread rather than outright put because the short 10d leg sells the part of the smile that is structurally richest.
strategies.risks: Capped protection below K1 in a true crash; theta bleed when nothing happens; timing: low SKEW persists for long stretches.
strategies.margin_note: Debit spread: pay the debit, no margin. SPX/XSP cash-settled, Section 1256; SPY/GLD American, assignment risk on the short leg if deep ITM.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit BTC put spreads are quoted and settled in BTC; a put spread bought as a hedge for a BTC holding pays out in BTC whose USD value is falling, so size in USD-equivalent (payoff in BTC = (K2-K1)/S_T at expiry). 24/7 and no gaps over weekends, which matters less than for equities.
strategies.metals_notes: GC put spreads exercise into futures (American); on GLD, as equity options. Gold's put wing is cheaper than equity's, so the hedge is relatively inexpensive; useful against a long bullion/GLD position; Section 1256 on GC.
variants: Outright 25d put when SKEW < 15th pct and VIX < 15
Put ladder (long K3, short K2, short K1) for near-zero cost
Rolling 3-month put spread, re-struck monthly

trial.statistic: Mean 21d P&L of a model-priced 25d/10d put spread (BS with VIX as ATM IV and a skew adjustment proportional to SKEW) when SKEW < 20th pct minus unconditional mean, as a fraction of debit.
trial.null: Conditioning on low SKEW does not improve the put-spread payoff ratio.
trial.procedure: Monthly cycles since 1990; model-priced spreads; walk-forward percentiles; studentized block bootstrap of the conditional-minus-unconditional difference; deflated Sharpe of the conditional series.

trial.pass: Difference > 0 with 95% bootstrap CI excluding zero and realised -2 sigma frequency in the low-SKEW bucket > unconditional at p<0.1.
trial.controls: Random-timing placebo with the same number of entries; VIX-tercile stratification.

strategies.harness_suggestion: Reuse the monthly model-priced cycle of harness_vrp_spx with a SKEW gate; swap in real 10d/25d IVs from surface_summary when available.

strategies.name: Smile curvature trade (butterfly vs straddle, kurtosis)
strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long iron butterfly receives credit C0 = Straddle(K2) - Strangle(K1,K3). Payoff = C0 - |S_T - K2| capped: max C0 at K2, min C0 - (K2-K1) below K1 or above K3. A short iron butterfly (long straddle, short wings) is the mirror: long kurtosis.
strategies.max_profit: Long butterfly: C0 (at S_T=K2). Short butterfly: (K2-K1) - C0.
strategies.max_loss: Long butterfly: (K2-K1) - C0. Short butterfly: C0.
strategies.breakevens: K2 +/- C0 (long butterfly); same points reversed for the short.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: long butterfly: negative near ATM; short butterfly: positive
greeks_at_inception.vega: long butterfly: short ATM vega, long wing vega = short 'butterfly' (25d wing IV avg - ATM IV), i.e. short implied kurtosis; short butterfly is long implied kurtosis

strategies.when_to_use: Trade the 25-delta butterfly spread (wing IV average minus ATM IV) against realised excess kurtosis: sell the wings' richness (long butterfly) when the butterfly is high percentile; buy wings when the smile is flat ahead of events.
strategies.risks: Long butterfly: large move loses the width; realised kurtosis clusters (crashes); pin risk near K2 on American options; wide bid/ask on wings.
strategies.margin_note: Defined risk both ways: max loss = width minus/plus credit. PM/Reg-T margin = max loss. Index versions cash-settled, Section 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: BTC smiles are symmetric-ish and very curved (high implied kurtosis); Deribit quotes IV per strike so the 25d butterfly is observable from the public book (mark_iv). Inverse settlement: butterfly payoffs convert at S_T.
strategies.metals_notes: Gold smile curvature is low; silver high. GC/SI options American into futures, SPAN margins the 4-leg as one array; GLD/SLV as equity options.
variants: Call butterfly / put butterfly (same payoff, one side)
Broken-wing butterfly (skew + curvature)
Condor (K1<K2<K3<K4) as wider curvature trade

strategies.claim: The 30-day 25-delta butterfly (average of 25d put and call IV minus ATM IV) on SPY/SPX exceeds the level justified by subsequent realised excess kurtosis of daily returns, so the long iron butterfly has positive mean P&L per unit of max loss.

trial.statistic: Mean 30d P&L of delta-hedged long iron butterfly divided by max loss; and regression of entry butterfly on realised 30d excess kurtosis.
trial.procedure: Daily captures of SPY/SPX surface (surface_summary ATM/25d IVs) -> monthly non-overlapping cycles; studentized bootstrap; walk-forward once 2+ years exist.
trial.data: Daily CBOE chain capture (SPY, SPX, GLD, IBIT) from 2026-10-14 onward; SPY closes for realised kurtosis.
trial.pass: Mean P&L/max loss > 0 at p<0.05 with >= 36 cycles; sign stable across the two halves.
trial.controls: Model-priced straddle-only control (VRP) to separate curvature premium from level premium.

strategies.blocked_on: daily chain capture, ~750 days (36 monthly cycles) for the P&L test; a 90-day capture gives a first read on butterfly levels vs realised kurtosis.
strategies.harness_suggestion: New harness_smile_curvature: compute 25d butterfly from surface_summary per capture day; P&L via build_position + payoff engine.

strategies.name: Straddle-vs-VIX basis (ATM straddle implied vs variance-swap strike)

legs.strike_rule: all K < F, weight 2/(T*K^2) scaled so vega matches the straddle

strategies.payoff_at_expiry: Long ATM straddle, short vega-matched 1/K^2 strip: isolates the gap between ATM implied vol (sigma_ATM, from the straddle: Straddle ~ 0.8*sigma_ATM*S*sqrt(T)) and the variance-swap vol (VIX). VIX - sigma_ATM is positive and driven by skew and convexity; the trade is short that 'smile premium' while flat in vol level.
strategies.max_profit: Bounded by the strip's wing premium (when spot stays near K the straddle loses less than the wings earn).
strategies.max_loss: Large move: strip's wings pay off quadratically (1/K^2 weighting gives constant dollar gamma) while the straddle pays linearly: the position is short convexity in large moves.
strategies.breakevens: Realised path with |moves| such that quadratic wing payout equals linear straddle payout: numerical.

greeks_at_inception.gamma: ~0 at spot, increasingly negative away from spot (short wings)

strategies.when_to_use: When VIX minus ATM 30-day IV (the smile premium) is at a high percentile (SKEW high, wings rich) and you want to be short the smile but neutral to the vol level; the wing-only expression of the skew/kurtosis premium.
strategies.risks: Crash convexity; many legs; the straddle hedge drifts away from ATM as spot moves (becomes directional).
strategies.margin_note: Short strip legs margined naked under Reg-T; PM nets against the long straddle. SPX cash-settled, European, 1256.
strategies.crypto_notes: Deribit: DVOL vs ATM mark_iv gives the same basis for BTC; the smile premium is large (BTC smiles are very convex); inverse settlement.
strategies.metals_notes: GVZ vs GLD ATM IV; gold's smile premium is smaller.
variants: Long straddle vs short strangle strip (fewer legs)
Long straddle vs short 25d butterfly wings
Basis trade on VIX3M vs 90d ATM IV
strategies.claim: VIX exceeds the 30-day SPX ATM implied vol (from the ATM straddle) by more than 1.5 vol points on average, and this smile premium exceeds the realised contribution of large moves (the difference between realised variance and the squared realised mean-absolute-deviation scaled by pi/2) over the following month, so the long-straddle / short-strip position has positive expectancy.

trial.statistic: Mean of VIX - sigma_ATM (captured) versus mean realised 'convexity' = sqrt(RV^2) - sqrt(pi/2)*MAD(returns)*sqrt(252) over the same window; simulated P&L.
trial.procedure: Daily captures of SPX ATM straddle (surface_summary straddle price) alongside VIX; non-overlapping 21d cycles; studentized block bootstrap; the realised side can be computed now on history to pre-register the threshold.
trial.data: Daily SPX chain capture from 2026-10-14; CBOE VIX history; SPY/SPX closes.
trial.pass: Smile premium minus realised convexity > 0 with 95% CI excluding zero over >= 36 cycles.
trial.controls: Model (BS flat smile) control where the premium is zero by construction; SKEW stratification.
